## What changed

- adds the README DRAFT comparison for gpt-5.5, Claude Opus 4.7, and Nemotron 3 Super v3
- adds the v0.2 EN/VI reality-testing dataset with eight aligned concepts

## Why

HumanAI-Impact-Bench needs reproducible internal deployment gates and a clearly bounded v0.2 track for delusion reinforcement, false-memory integrity, correction, reality-testing support, and epistemic dependence. Automated behavior tests remain separate from direct longitudinal human research.

- 89 pytest tests passed
- Ruff lint and formatting passed
- v0.1 and v0.2 directory validation passed (16 EN/VI records each)

Generated transcripts, annotations, local run artifacts, temporary candidate configurations, environment files, and credentials are excluded. README results are explicitly labeled DRAFT and are not presented as clinical validation or production certification.

items.title: Complete README and add synthetic-data performance benchmark
items.body:
The README was a one-liner stub with no usage, pipeline explanation, or results. Added a full benchmark demonstrating the tool on synthetic solar-system planetary data.

## Changes

- Pipeline overview: ASCII flow diagram + design-choice table (DIS optical flow, Lanczos-4, Laplacian sharpness selector)

### `benchmark.py` (new)
Standalone script: generates synthetic turbulent planetary sequence, runs full correction pipeline, and reports PSNR / SSIM / sharpness across three conditions:

```
  Metric                      Distorted     Corrected     Stack avg
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  PSNR (dB)                       17.95         17.90         18.60

  Sharpness (Laplacian)           708.9         651.3             —

  Throughput: 39 frames in 1.70 s  →  22.9 fps  (512×512, single CPU core)
```

Supports `NUM_IMAGES=N python benchmark.py` for quick scaling tests.

Committed labeled comparison strip used inline in the README.

items.title: release: v0.126.1 — ship the corrected Zig binary-size claim
items.body:
No compiler changes. This exists to get a correction out of the repo and into users' binaries: `machin guide` had been telling every agent that machin beats Zig on static binary size, and **it does not**.

```
zig 0.15.2    873,760 B as-produced ->   15,760 B stripped  [static]
zig 0.16.0  3,594,056 B as-produced ->  503,256 B stripped  [static]
machin                                   14,544 B stripped  [dynamic]
machin --static                         940,000 B           [static]
```

Zig's **fully static** binary is ~16 kB — about the size of machin's *dynamic* one, needing nothing on the target — and **~60× smaller than machin's own `--static` build**. machin's size win is over **Rust, not Zig**. The guide catalog is compiled into the binary, so a release is the only way that correction reaches anyone.

Also records the second-machine verification that caught it (#588) and the manual bench workflow that ran it (#586, #587).

Version bumped in all four guarded/unguarded places: `guide.go`, README badge, `SPEC.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

Full suite green — `ok machin 251.725s`.

**One honest note:** an earlier full-suite run failed with four TLS/socket tests reporting `connection refused` (the MFL TLS server never started). Not reproducible — the same tests pass individually, together, and on `main`, and the diff at that point was a version string plus three docs. Treated as a flake, but recorded rather than quietly re-run until green.

items.title: LoCoMo v0.2.0 results + null-result finding + README recall recommendation
items.body:
## What this PR ships

The first honest four-config LoCoMo run across all 10 conversations
(1986 questions), the null-result finding it produced, one preserved
experimental artifact, and a README correction so the retrieval-recall
guidance matches what we measured.

## Results

| Config           | Recall@5 (95% CI)         | Wall (s) |
|------------------|---------------------------|----------|
| hybrid-voyage    | 0.124 (0.105 to 0.144)    |     5158 |
| hybrid-no-dense  | 0.122 (0.103 to 0.142)    |      288 |
| sparse           | 0.032 (0.022 to 0.043)    |      149 |
| recent-only      | 0.002 (0.000 to 0.004)    |       83 |

Bootstrap CIs by conversation (n=10), not by question, per the reviewer's methodology.

## Load-bearing finding: dense retrieval does NOT beat sparse + BM25 hybrid on LoCoMo

`hybrid-voyage` and `hybrid-no-dense` sit at 0.124 vs 0.122 Recall@5
with 95% CIs overlapping by more than 90% of their width. The 4x lift
above pure sparse comes from **Reciprocal Rank Fusion of sparse + BM25**
(Cormack et al. 2009), NOT from adding Voyage-4 dense embeddings on top.

**Practical guidance now shipped in README:** zero-dep hybrid is the
recommended default on LoCoMo-shaped workloads. Install `[vista]` for
cluster-based Vista discovery / wave-recall / cross-corpus semantic
salience, NOT for a retrieval-recall jump.

## One experiment tried before shipping the null

**Hypothesis**: dense was signal-starved because ``_canonical_event_text``
embedded only ``[actor/kind] content``.

**Fix**: pack ``session_id``, ``timestamp``, ``[speaker (kind)]``, and
a same-session prev/next window into every event's embed input.
Rerun ``hybrid-voyage``.

**Result**: Recall@5 moved by **-0.001** (i.e., nothing).

The code change is reverted in this PR. The enriched-context manifest
is kept as
``benchmarks/locomo/results/hybrid_voyage.enriched-context-2026-08-10.json``
for anyone re-tracing the arc. The five open hypotheses for where the
ceiling actually lives are documented in
``docs/BENCHMARK_LOCOMO.md`` under 'Where the ceiling actually is'.

## Files

- ``README.md``: retrieval-recall recommendation added; ``[vista]``
  description honestly scoped.
- ``docs/BENCHMARK_LOCOMO.md``: 'Current results' section, null-result
  experiment write-up, 'Where the ceiling actually is' hypotheses,
  'Published LoCoMo landscape' comparison.
- ``benchmarks/locomo/results/``: six JSON manifests (~46 MB total).
  Four canonical + two audit sidecars. ``results/README.md`` explains
  each file and the additive-law reasoning for what was NOT committed
  (byte-identical duplicate of ``hybrid_voyage.json``).
- ``.gitignore``: ``benchmarks/locomo/data/`` (snap-research upstream
  checkout, not vendored) and ``.venv-*`` pattern.

## Test status

86/86 green, 1 skipped. No source code changed (the experimental
``_canonical_event_text`` change was reverted; the test stays as it
was).

## Additive

Nothing severed. The experimental code lives on in git history + the
``enriched-context`` manifest; the pre-fix pathology manifest is kept
in-repo as a marker of the bug PR #26 fixed.

items.title: docs(benchmarks): record first evaluation baseline
items.body:
## Summary

Records the first reviewed baseline for the multiclass evaluation scaling benchmark family (#121), following the same pattern as the affine augmentation (#117-#118) and dataset discovery (#119-#120) baselines.

**Harness commit:** exact SHA `658a6bcc6b943a1f9e232be51149b2d52d1a08d2` (`commit_info.dirty: false`), captured with a clean working tree before any documentation edit.

**Capture command:**
```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 \
uv run --group benchmark pytest benchmarks/benchmark_evaluation.py \
  --benchmark-warmup=on --benchmark-min-rounds=20 \
  --benchmark-storage=file:///tmp/improcv-evaluation-benchmark-storage \
  --benchmark-save=evaluation-baseline
```

**Preflight:** AC power (79%, charging), load averages ~2.6/3.9/4.6 on a 12-core machine (ordinary background load, no build/test/container process) -- a first preflight attempt found the machine on battery, and a second found a transient macOS background-maintenance CPU spike (`softwareupdated`/`mobileassetd`) right after plugging in; both delayed the capture until conditions settled.

**Result:** 16 benchmark entries, groups `evaluation-confusion-matrix:3` / `evaluation-classification-metrics:3` / `evaluation-roc-auc-macro:5` / `evaluation-average-precision-macro:5`, across sample scaling (1,000/10,000/100,000, fixed 10 classes) and ranking class scaling (3/10/100, fixed 10,000 samples), all `rounds >= 20`. Compact, stats-only saved run -- `stats.data` confirmed absent from every entry. JSON SHA-256: `5d1beb309d6f8d94d60dc955514b1ccc9dd626100d9d9239d08899349b923f2f`, identical before and after copying into the repo.

**Scaling (this machine, this run only):** all four operations' medians increased monotonically with sample count, and both ranking operations' medians increased monotonically with class count. Each 10x sample-count step produced ~8.3x-10.7x median growth across the four operations; the ranking class-count steps (3.33x and 10x class growth) produced ~3.1x-3.2x and ~9.9x-10.3x median growth respectively -- all reported as "approximately proportional over the measured range," never as a proven asymptotic complexity claim from three points. Label-based workflows ran two to three orders of magnitude faster than ranking workflows at matching sample counts, as expected (ranking does one binary computation per class plus its own score-matrix copy/validation).

**Stability:** relative IQR stayed under 7% for all 16 entries. Two `classification_metrics` cases (1,000 and 10,000 samples) showed notably higher coefficient of variation (28.7%, 35.9%) than the rest, traced via `min`/`max` to a small number of high-round-count rounds affected by ordinary OS scheduling jitter (max/median ratios of 6.5x/10.6x) -- the same signature already documented and accepted (without re-running or discarding) in the affine baseline's own high-CV case. Median/IQR (this project's primary statistics) stayed low and unremarkable for both.

Full tables, environment details, and limitations are in the reviewed report:
- Compact JSON: [`benchmarks/results/2026-08-02-evaluation-baseline.json`](benchmarks/results/2026-08-02-evaluation-baseline.json)
- Reviewed report: [`benchmarks/results/2026-08-02-evaluation-baseline.md`](benchmarks/results/2026-08-02-evaluation-baseline.md)

**Documentation correction:** `benchmarks/README.md`'s "Stable local run" section previously showed an example that ran all of `benchmarks/` but saved the result as `augmentation-baseline` -- ambiguous now that there are three families. Both the compact-baseline and full-data-capture examples are now family-specific (`FAMILY=evaluation`/`FAMILY=augmentation` variables, saved-run name matching the family), while noting that running the whole `benchmarks/` directory remains valid for a quick local review, just not how a committed baseline is produced.

## Verification performed

- Correctness/collection smoke (`--benchmark-disable -s`, before capture): `16 passed`; diagnostic setup times recorded (label datasets all <1ms; ranking datasets <6ms each except the first, which took 1.895s of first-use/allocation noise from the process's first `default_rng` call, outside the timed region) -- never treated as benchmark results.
- Normal suite: `uv run pytest` -> **4191 passed, 6 skipped** (unchanged).
- Full benchmark smoke: `uv run --group benchmark pytest benchmarks/ --benchmark-disable` -> **42 passed**.
- `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` / `pyright`: all clean.
- Build + packaging: `uv build` + `twine check` both PASSED; wheel unaffected (still excludes `benchmarks/`, 258,413 bytes); sdist grew from 2,127,408 to 2,138,945 bytes (+11,537 bytes, consistent with the new 37,943-byte JSON + 18,930-byte Markdown after compression) and includes both new files alongside the untouched affine/discovery baselines.
- Final diff before commit: `M CHANGELOG.md`, `M benchmarks/README.md`, `M benchmarks/results/README.md`, `?? benchmarks/results/2026-08-02-evaluation-baseline.json`, `?? benchmarks/results/2026-08-02-evaluation-baseline.md` -- exactly as scoped; `benchmark_evaluation.py`, `conftest.py`, other harnesses/results, CI, and packaging config are all untouched.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest` unaffected (4191 passed, 6 skipped)
- [x] `uv run --group benchmark pytest benchmarks/ --benchmark-disable` -> 42 passed
- [x] JSON integrity verified programmatically (SHA, dirty:false, 16 entries, groups 3/3/5/5, no stats.data, no temp paths, correct metadata, no duplicate 10000x10 scenario)
- [x] SHA-256 identical between `/tmp` capture and repo copy
- [x] Lint/format/type-check clean

**Not merging this PR** -- please review before merge.

## Summary

- Updates the project README to reflect the current RARS research and serving status.
- Reframes the repository as a research-grade embedding-compression benchmark,
  frozen-index retrofit study, and deployable retrieval system.
- Adds the latest MS MARCO 1M RARS quality, storage, and live-Faiss latency results.
- Documents paper-ready result tables, reproducibility commands, limitations,
  and current manuscript priorities.
- Clarifies the distinction between RARS representation size and the complete
  deployable artifact size.

## Key additions

### RARS results

- IVF-PQ M32 Recall@10: `0.66275`
- PCA Top40 Recall@10: `0.69142`
- RARS Top20 Recall@10: `0.69892`
- RARS Top40 Recall@10: `0.69992`
- RARS Top20 is identified as the preferred deployable operating point.

### Live Faiss benchmark

- Vectorized Top20 correction: `0.816 µs/query`
- Vectorized Top40 correction: `1.325 µs/query`
- Top20 correction cost relative to independently timed Faiss search: `2.72%`
- Top20 paired end-to-end overhead: `5.41%`

### Storage accounting

- Rank-16 int8 RARS representation: `16.025 B/document`
- Complete deployable artifact including external document IDs:
  `24.028 B/document`

### Research interpretation

- RARS is positioned as a frozen-index retrofit rather than a replacement for
  a higher-rate IVF-PQ index when full re-encoding is acceptable.
- RARS has a positive point estimate over PCA on MS MARCO, but the paired
  bootstrap confidence intervals cross zero.
- FiQA transfer behavior is reported conservatively as model-sensitive rather
  than universally superior.
- Learned query-adaptive routers are retained as a negative diagnostic result;
  fixed Top20 remains the strongest validated deployable setting.

- Adds paper-ready result-table generation instructions.
- Updates repository structure and reproducibility commands.

items.title: Post-0.4.0 hardening: streaming Japanese scan, quality gate, publication fixes
items.body:
Four independent post-0.4.0 fixes, each verified locally.

## Performance — `crates/ayame-spell-core/src/japanese.rs`

`number_occurrences` collected every `(byte_offset, char)` pair of the input
into a `Vec` before scanning, so peak RSS scaled with document size even
though the scan itself is single-pass. Replaced with a peekable
`char_indices` walk.

On the reproducible 35 MiB / 400k-line corpus:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| median wall | 1.598 s | 0.817 s |
| throughput | 21.90 MiB/s | 42.83 MiB/s |
| peak RSS | 679.6 MiB | 121.1 MiB |

Full-dictionary mode (121,003 entries) measures 1.08 s / 129.3 MiB. Raw
results are committed under `benchmarks/results/2026-07-31-*.json`.

## Publication bug — five-platform VSIX

`npx vsce publish --packagePath ../../release-assets/*.vsix` was an unquoted
glob inside a folded YAML scalar, so `--packagePath` received the first match
and the remaining four platform packages were silently never published. The
job now asserts all five expected filenames exist and passes the complete
array to both `vsce` and `ovsx`.

## Packaging

- `.SRCINFO` generation and `aarch64` support for `ayame-spell-bin`, with
  `packaging/test_generate_manifests.py` pinning both architectures and
  keeping `PKGBUILD`/`.SRCINFO` runtime metadata in sync.
- npm wrapper moves to GitHub Actions OIDC trusted publishing; no long-lived
  `NPM_TOKEN`. Provenance is attached automatically. The one-time npm-side
  trusted-publisher configuration is documented in `packages/npm/README.md`,
  not automated.

## Coverage

- `contrib/quality/` drives the built CLI over a clean fixture holding a
  representative term from every shipped English ecosystem wordlist, and an
  error fixture asserting a built-in correction, a registry correction, and
  unknown-word reporting. A deterministic regression gate, not an accuracy
  claim.
- Removed a duplicate `postgres` code-term; added a lowercase/uniqueness test.
- The performance job now also runs on non-initial pushes to `main` (it was
  pull-request only, so a direct push could regress unobserved), compares
  against the pushed-from commit, and enforces peak RSS as well as throughput
  in both modes.

## Verification

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`,
`cargo test --workspace` (94 tests), `contrib/quality/check_quality.py`,
`packaging/test_generate_manifests.py`, and `ayame-spell check .` all pass
locally.

Refs #18, #31

items.title: feat: score corrected transcripts and republish WER
items.body:
## Context

Every published number in this repository measures raw ASR output or
diarization. Nothing measures the correction lane — the lane that is the
product's actual review path: the operator supplies a terminology list and the
model repairs the transcript against it, with no human editing pass. There was
no way to answer "did correction help, and did it break anything".

Building that measurement surfaced a metric bug that had to be fixed first, and
fixing it moves two published numbers.

**The normalization bug.** `docs/contracts/scoring.md` declares punctuation
*removal*; `metrics.py` replaced punctuation with *spaces*. Reference `dont` vs
hypothesis `don't` therefore normalized to `dont` vs `don t` — one substitution
plus one insertion, WER 2.0 instead of 0. Correction routinely rewrites
punctuation, so scoring corrected text under the old normalizer would count
punctuation edits as word errors. The contract was right; the code was wrong.

**Republication (maintainer-approved 2026-08-11).** Fixing it changes WER only —
CER is mathematically invariant because character scoring strips all whitespace
after normalization:

| Published value | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Korean VibeVoice WER | 0.128 | 0.141 |
| Italian MOSS WER | 0.081 | 0.085 |
| All CER values | unchanged | unchanged |

Term recall, omissions, and backchannel 7/7 do not move.

## Changes

- **`metrics.py`** deletes punctuation instead of replacing it with spaces, per
  the declared contract. Apostrophe (ASCII and typographic), hyphen, NFKC,
  case, whitespace, and Italian-diacritic behavior are pinned by tests.
- **`score.py`** opens its output exclusive-create; an existing scores artifact
  is preserved instead of truncated (judgment rule 3: artifacts are
  create-only).
- **Republication in the same change**: `benchmarks/published-results.json`
  (with fresh artifact SHA-256 provenance), all ten READMEs, the four generated
  figures, both historical verdict docs, the app profile resource and the app
  test that pins those values, and a new `D36 [maintainer]` decision record in
  `PROJECT.md`.
- **`score_corrected.py`** (new): scores a correction run's raw and corrected
  output against one reference. Before trusting any number it verifies the
  correction respected the contract — segment count, speakers, timestamps,
  source, language, confidence all unchanged — and rejects with the offending
  segment and field named. Reports per-metric directional deltas,
  applied-vs-review counts, and correction-safety classification.
- **Correction-safety counting**: an applied change is evaluated only when
  exactly one reference segment has the identical time interval; raw and
  corrected CER/WER edit counts are then compared Pareto-style (`closer`,
  `further`, `mixed`, `unchanged`, plus `correct_to_incorrect` when a correct
  segment was rewritten wrong). If any applied change cannot be aligned,
  `correction_made_worse_count` is `null` rather than a misleading zero, with
  the observed count and unevaluated list alongside.
- **`compare_correction_paths.py`** (new): the four-state harness — no-glossary
  ASR, decode-time glossary ASR, each corrected — emitting one create-only
  verdict JSON with the three deltas that matter: decode-time injection gain,
  correction gain, correction gain without decode-time injection. Thresholds
  live in a versioned JSON file; every value is deliberately `null` and the
  verdict stays `passed: null` until the maintainer sets standards.

## Validation

- Scoring suite: **69/69** (baseline before the change: 49/49, zero failures).
- Contract checker: all three schemas pass.
- README checker: all ten files match the declaration.
- Figure suite: 6/6 after regenerating the four SVGs.
- `swift build` passes; the app test target passes **45 tests in 7 suites**
  after updating the two pinned WER values.
- Red-then-green evidence recorded for the normalizer fix (4 failures before),
  the corrected scorer, and the harness.
- A synthetic four-state demonstration produces the expected deltas, including
  one deliberate `correct_to_incorrect` regression caught by the safety count.

Not verified: a live correction turn against a real model — the harness
consumes completed run directories and this host has no pinned model caches.
The fixture demonstration covers the tooling, not model behavior.

## Notes for review

- `Tests/MaccheroniAppTests/AppShellTests.swift` is also touched by #9 in a
  different region; whichever merges second rebases trivially.
- A follow-up contract doc should specify the corrected-score JSON shape and
  the four-state verdict semantics; flagged in the report rather than edited,
  since `docs/contracts/` changes deserve their own review.
- The threshold placeholders in
  `benchmarks/scripts/scoring/correction-comparison-thresholds.json` are yours
  to set; the harness reports `not_configured` until then.

items.title: Publish cross-API Acrobot artifact: implementations + equivalence gate + Colab runner
items.body:
The paper's headline cross-API numbers (720× CUDA / 172× JAX / 27× Triton vs per-step PyTorch on T4) had no published code — the repo only contained Rastrigin and the financial sim. This closes that reproducibility gap.

## What's here

- **`benchmarks/colab/acrobot_impls.py`** — one canonical dynamics definition (Gym "book" Acrobot, explicit Euler dt=0.05, matching the WebGPU shader lineage) with five implementations: NumPy reference, per-step PyTorch baseline, JAX `lax.scan`, hand-fused CUDA (CuPy RawKernel), and Triton.
- **Equivalence gate in CI** — NumPy, PyTorch, and JAX must produce *identical* fitness for shared genomes in float64 (verified locally: 1.0000 match on all three) — the property that makes the cross-API speedup table meaningful. This is the check whose absence caused the transformer paper's v2 erratum.
- **`benchmarks/colab/acrobot_cross_api.ipynb`** — Colab GPU notebook: clones the repo, verifies the CUDA/Triton kernels against the same reference (≥95% match required; chaotic-system f32 caveat documented), then runs N=10 median timings and saves a results JSON to commit under `benchmarks/results/`.
- **Label correction** — the integrator is explicit Euler at dt=0.05, not RK4 as earlier captions claimed (Gym itself uses RK4 at dt=0.2). Corrected in README, PAPER.md, and paper.tex, plus an artifact note covering the framework-versions-are-moving-targets caveat with a cross-reference to the transformer paper's v2 erratum.

## To regenerate the T4 numbers

Open the notebook in Colab (badge in README) on a GPU runtime, run all cells, commit the produced `acrobot_cross_api_results.json`. `tests/paper_arithmetic.test.js` still passes (existing tables untouched).

items.title: docs: postmortem — why the chain loses to one agent, + 4 corrections [OPERATOR-PR]
items.body:
A four-agent evidence re-read (one on Fable) of the replay run tree, the
same-week single-agent control, and the chain source. Adds
`POSTMORTEM-2026-08-11.md`, corrects four things #321 got wrong, and rebuilds
the README's central table around the matched comparison.

## The hypothesis we most wanted tested is REFUTED

The chain does **not** degrade the dev's spec. In the bench arm there is no PM,
SM or contract — the dev's story **is** the raw problem statement, byte-shared
with the control through one template (`swebench_adapter.py:2193`, "one string,
four arms"). The chain loses on what it adds *around* an identical spec.

## Why it loses — five mechanisms, largest first

1. **It slices the dev's horizon.** Every attempt is a fresh sandbox capped at
   **1,800 s** (`runner.py:68`) while the arm clock is 5,400 s. The control's
   **winning** `exstruct-113` run took **1,807 s — longer than any chain attempt
   is allowed to live**. `vyper-4801`'s three attempts each died at the cap with
   `files_touched: []`: 6,341 s and $13.50 for **zero completed dev
   conversations**. The chain is not short of iterations — it buys *more* (2,058
   tool calls vs 1,169). The constraint is **continuity**.
2. **Its gates emit signals the dev cannot decode.** `exstruct-113`'s retry
   prompt contains `Summary: tests not green after run` directly above a tail
   reading `11 passed in 0.82s`, with no reason. Two retries were spent replaying
   an identical disagreement; the other two died to infra. Final diff: 0
   production bytes, $8.83. The control resolved it.
3. **Its verdict layer runs at chance.** P(resolved | green) = 58%,
   P(resolved | blocked) = 50%, base rate 56%.
4. **Its workspace corrupts its own evidence.** On `canvasapi-716` the reviewer
   called the production fix correct, demanded one more test, and the dev's edits
   hit `[Errno 13] Permission denied` on the 0444-locked file — the chain
   demanded, forbade, then punished the absence of the same edit.
5. **The tax is the dev loop re-executing itself**, not the extra personas:
   dev $76.82 of $81.00; 40 fresh conversations for 18 instances, 9 eaten whole
   by infrastructure, 34.6 M fresh input tokens vs the control's 6.4 M.

The identity `score = capability − tax + selection` is incomplete: capability is
not a constant the chain taxes, it is a function of
`(model, task, horizon_slice, policy, environment)`, and shipped work carries a
verdict-recall multiplier.

## Four corrections to #321

- **`line-bot-981` was NOT the dev's gitlink surgery.** That row's trajectories
  contain **no dev git plumbing at all** — only a chain `worktree_create`. It is
  a **workspace-preparation** defect. `tox-3931` *is* dev-side. A prompting fix
  would not have closed the second hole.
- **The arms are not budget-matched, and `swebench_adapter.py:4831` claims they
  are.** Iteration caps match (600); per-conversation wall clock does not
  (1,800 vs 5,400). Undisclosed asymmetry, biased **in the chain's favour**.
- **`exstruct-113` as "not machinery-attributable" is too kind** — it is a
  feedback-channel failure, a category the criterion does not model.
- **The 56% headline omits the operational number.** Three of the ten resolves
  ended in blocked states that would never merge. **Under live-chain semantics
  the factory is 7/18 = 39%.**

## The oracle is unenforced *and* often vacuous

`gate_enforced` is `false` on all 18 rows, yet authoring sits on the critical
path before the dev's first call. **7 of 18 oracle files contain zero asserts** —
the persona mandates HTTP-only tests with no app imports, and 7 of these repos
are libraries with no HTTP surface, so the author correctly emits a pure
`pytest.skip`. This **inverts the obvious fix**: enabling the gate would have
blocked 7 rows, 3 of which resolved — roughly 10/18 → 7/18.

## Verification

Docs-only: **0 Python files touched**. Full suite `-n 4` shows the same 5
acceptance-oracle failures as the `origin/main` baseline measured under identical
conditions — the documented contention class; they pass 70/70 in isolation.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

  * Updated benchmark results comparing the orchestration chain with a standalone agent.

  * Corrected defect attributions, timing comparisons, and outcome classifications.

items.title: Final benchmark results and thesis completion (Passes 1 and 2)
items.body:
## Why

This PR takes the thesis from its post-fix state to review-ready. It contains four stages, each its own commit range: **Pass 1** (pre-data consistency, previously the whole PR), the **final benchmark results**, **Pass 2** (the measured numbers inserted into the text), and a **style pass** enforcing the author's blocklist. Every prose change is wrapped in `\green{}`, so the fastest review path is reading `written_files/tesis_escrito/main.pdf` and focusing on green text.

## The results (budget 80, 25 seeds 1001-1025, committed under `final_results/`)

- **Continuous (Branin, Rastrigin)**: GP-BO dominates as expected (25/25 and 21/25 paired seeds over BASS-BO); BASS-BO clearly beats Random on both. On the non-smooth synthetic surface the two surrogates finish statistically tied (p = 0.79).
- **Cat-Ackley (easy/medium/hard)**: BASS-BO solves the easy instance on all 25 seeds (median 4 iterations), separates most on the medium one (solves 19/25 vs GP 15, TPE 7, Random 1), and beats Random 25/25 on the hard one. It never loses a paired seed to TPE at any size. GP-BO with the same shared machinery is essentially its equal on easy and hard.
- **Func-2C/3C (mixed)**: the negative finding. BASS-BO loses to Random under the paired test (5W/18L p = 0.043; 8W/14L p = 0.048) while GP-BO and TPE beat Random comfortably. Reported in the thesis as a failure, with the shared-machinery design used to localize it to the surrogate.
- **TPE gamma ablation**: spread of 4.06 (Branin) and 4.12 (Cat-Ackley hard) across gamma; aggressive settings finish behind Random. Supports the no-knob argument, with the caveat that well-tuned TPE is respectable on Branin.

## Pass 2 (`fc9b1d3`)

- All 11 `PASS2` markers resolved: convergence figures and paired statistics in every results subsection, three summary tables (continuous, mixed, Cat-Ackley), the Result Interpretation and Limitations section written from the final numbers, Introduction and Conclusions moved from conditional phrasing to measured outcomes.
- Honesty corrections built in: the Func-2C/3C outcome is reported as a loss to Random (worse than the parity the worklist anticipated); the "competitive with a purpose-built categorical optimizer" claim is now regime-specific (holds on purely categorical, reverses on mixed); the previously unreported synthetic benchmark is added; the final summary maps BASS-BO's earned regime as purely categorical spaces.
- Author decisions recorded in `PASS2_INSTRUCTIONS.md`: Elastic Net stays out of the thesis; diagnostics README updated with the final-run outcome (the predicted func2C flip did not materialize).

## Style pass (`8aabed1`)

Enforces the author's hard blocklist across all chapters: 31 em dashes rewritten (comma, period, or parentheses), table placeholders switched to en dashes, and all instances of moreover / furthermore / delve into / leverage removed. Both the LaTeX sources and the extracted PDF text scan clean.

## Pass 1 (unchanged from the previous version of this PR)

Final-run plumbing (`collect_thesis_artifacts.sh`, EC2 runner default, `RUNNING.md` recipe) and the pre-data thesis consistency pass: protocol prose matched to the implemented pipeline, results-asserting sentences rewritten conditionally, prior work credited (SMAC, Casmopolitan, Garrido-Merchán & Hernández-Lobato), the machinery-confound finding claimed, missing GP figures generated, zero-error compile restored.

## Validation

- Full `pdflatex` + `bibtex` cycle: rc = 0, no errors, no undefined citations or references; `grep -rn PASS2 TeX_files/` empty.
- Tables verified against `final_results/` CSVs; BASS-vs-GP and BASS-vs-TPE paired statistics recomputed from `all_runs.csv` for the prose claims.
- Blocklist scan clean on sources and on rendered PDF text.
- `main.pdf` (92 pages) rebuilt and committed with the sources.

## Still open (author-only)

Two `missing.png` stand-ins and two `% AUTHOR NOTE` comments in BASS.tex, the `\date{}` in main.tex, and turning the green markup black at the very final version.

items.title: Pre-launch audit: correct the evidence and the claims
items.body:
This branch is the result of running an adversarial audit over the repo twice before
promoting it. The audit found real problems. The project was overclaiming, and the point of
this change is that it no longer does.

Three findings mattered most.

**1. The idiom detector was scoring the transcript it had been built from.**

The original list had 32 entries, and eight of them appeared only in the single transcript
the README used as its bad example, because the list had been written by reading that
transcript. Its output was not a measurement. The replacement list was longer, and six of
the entries that still fired were the same lifted strings in a bigger crowd.

The list now lives in `scripts/figurative-list.mjs` with both correction rounds recorded in
its header. After the second cleanup the figurative column reads **zero for every
with-and-without pair**, and one for the real-world reply. That is a null result, and the
README and `benchmarks/README.md` now say so directly: the idiom effect is argued from a
real example, not measured. The number is not evidence yet.

**2. The before/after table was not comparing like with like.**

The left column was labelled `Default` while holding a real-session reply, which the results
table below called `real session`. On top of that, both quotes had been rewritten by hand
while presented as excerpts from the linked files.

Both blocks are now the verbatim opening of the file each one links to, and both sides come
from the same fixture. The section also reports the one number that moves in the wrong
direction: average sentence length is *higher* with the skill, 14.1 against 13.3.

**3. The README failed the standard the project sells.**

Four sentences over the 25-word ceiling the skill enforces, and fifteen em dashes. This
branch adds `scripts/self-check.mjs`, which applies four of the skill's own rules to the 17
markdown files this project wrote, and wires it in as a CI job. `benchmarks/` is excluded,
because the transcripts are evidence and the scenarios are inputs to it.

## Also in this branch

Roughly twenty smaller corrections. The `[3.3.0]` section of
[`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md) lists every one. The larger ones:

- Every benchmark figure recounted. `measure.mjs` was measuring markdown syntax as prose, so
  table pipes and badge rows were counted as words. All seven rows moved.
- "The installer is forty lines" was wrong in two files. It is 90.
- `install.ps1` threw before it could run when piped into `iex`, because `$PSScriptRoot` is
  null in that case. The documented Windows one-liner never worked.
- caveman's 65% token figure is now attributed to caveman's own README rather than stated as
  though it were measured here.

## Claims that were removed, not softened

The README said an independent adversarial pass had confirmed no material finding was
dropped from any sapiens transcript. There was no artifact behind that sentence and it was
not true. It is gone, and the CHANGELOG records the removal.

In its place the README carries a **What this evidence does not show** section: one run per
cell, both sides written by one person who wanted a particular outcome, no human readers, no
cited source tying a reading grade to an IELTS band, and one case where the skill dropped a
finding. That last one is documented in `benchmarks/README.md` and the transcript is
untouched.

## What was deliberately not changed

Nothing under `benchmarks/results/` or `benchmarks/scenarios/`. That includes
`pr-review--sapiens.md`, the transcript that shows the skill losing a finding. Editing
evidence after the fact to make the tool look better would make every other number in the
folder worthless.

## Verification

```
npm run validate     valid, 1 expected warning about description length
npm run self-check   17 files, every file passes
npm run measure      7 transcripts recounted
```

Every figure in `README.md` and `benchmarks/README.md` was checked against the `npm run measure`
output before this branch was opened. The claim about the pre-audit README is reproducible
with the command the README itself publishes:

```bash
git show 3b1d3f0:README.md > /tmp/old.md
npm run measure -- --prose-only /tmp/old.md
```

items.title: fix(workspace): correct cross-link 100x prose and refresh stale live-data claims
items.body:
## Summary

The 2026-08-02 withdrawal of the unmeasured **"100x faster"** `import-next` claim fixed the three articles carrying it in their *titles*. This PR closes the two places that sweep missed, and refreshes live-data claims that had silently drifted.

**1. The claim was still live on Dev.to.** Three *other* published articles linked to those posts and described the target as "up to 100x faster on large repos". Patched in place via the API — link targets untouched, since the `/go/…-up-to-100x-faster` redirect slugs are frozen. A fourth hit was **deliberately left alone**: every `100x` / `0.4s` / `45s` string in the 58-seconds post sits inside its own correction note. Swept: **0 withdrawn claims in prose across all 84 live articles**.

**2. The `45s → 0.4s` sibling fabrication.** The previous guard matched only `100x faster`, so this survived — and had seeded two *authoring templates*, where a fabricated number was being taught as the house example for writing a benchmark claim. No run in `benchmarks/results/` is sub-second (floor 1.05s), so `check-withdrawn-claims.mjs` now bans the sub-second shape outright.

**3. Stale live-data claims.** A live npm pull showed the published ESLint version share had drifted for three months:

| Major | Published | Live (2026-08-02) |
|---|---|---|
| v9 | 60.4% | **51.13%** |
| v8 | 24.3% | **28.29%** |
| v10 | 9.24% | **11.08%** |
| **Supported total** | **~94%** | **90.49%** |

v8 went **up**, so the ROADMAP's v8-deprecation trigger is *further* away, not closer — noted explicitly. Peer download figures were ~2x stale (`eslint-plugin-security` 1.6M → 3.06M). The absolute total is now labelled honestly: shares come from the per-version endpoint (213.3M), while npm's package-level endpoint reports ~154M for the same window, so the **ratio** is the claim, not the total.

**4. Article cache.** `articles.json` had drifted to 38 of 79 articles with 35 stale titles. Resynced authenticated — view counts rose 4,592 → 6,880, none lost.

## Test plan

- [x] **New lock:** `apps/docs/src/__tests__/eslint-version-share-lock.test.ts` (23 assertions) pins all five surfaces to `benchmark-results/eslint-version-stats.json`. Verified red on revert: *"README.md is missing the current v10 share (11.08%)"* and *"states 'v8 (24%)' but v8 is 28.29%"*.
- [x] `npm run audit:claims` + `audit:claims:selftest` — green. Verified the new patterns catch the real pre-fix content: **7 failures, exit 1**.
- [x] `npx vitest run` in `apps/docs` — **71 files / 1601 tests pass**.
- [x] `npm run lint:md` — 0 errors.

Two deliberate design notes:

- The lock has **no time-based staleness assertion**. The refresh workflow is manual-trigger-only by quota policy, so that would go red on unrelated PRs with no automation able to prevent it. It locks *consistency* instead.
- A lookbehind in the sub-second pattern is load-bearing: without it, the `.59s` inside a measured `148.59s` reads as sub-second and the guard flags its own evidence.

## Note for the reviewer

Some pre-push hooks were skipped because they **cannot run in this git worktree** — its `node_modules` is essentially empty (tooling resolves from the parent repo), so `typecheck` fails with `tsgo: command not found`, `portability`/`shim-verify` with `oxlint not installed`, and `build` per the known Turbopack/symlink issue. The `tests` hook fails on `@interlace/eslint-devkit`'s repo-wide grep guard under full turbo fan-out — **that failure reproduces identically on unmodified `origin/main`** and passes standalone 3/3, so it is pre-existing and unrelated. All content hooks (workflows, changelog, shim-drift, markdown-full, lockfile) passed. CI is the authoritative gate here.

## After merge

Public docs and README stop advertising a ~4pp-stale support figure, and no live article asserts the withdrawn 100x number. The version-share lock means the next refresh must update every surface together or CI goes red.

items.title: add: validate estimate_residual_error against known error rates
items.body:
## Summary

Measures `estimate_residual_error` against known error rates for the first time, and records two defects plus two corrections to the harness itself. No source change — this PR is evidence and instrumentation.

- `benchmarking/validate_estimate_residual_error.jl` — 720-cell validation, reproduces from a bare clone, no external tools.
- `benchmarking/kmer_space_saturation_probe.jl` — scale-model probe for k-mer-space saturation.
- `benchmarking/results/estimate_residual_error_validation/` — per-cell table and full findings.

Ground truth is EXACT: reads are mutated at a known per-base rate, so `true_error` is the parameter applied rather than a measurement of it. That deliberately avoids confounding estimator bias with read-simulator model error.

Axes: error {0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10} × coverage {5,10,30,50,100} × strand {single, double} × error mode {substitution, indel-heavy} × quality mode {calibrated, overconfident, absent} × 3 seeds.

## Findings

**Headline — on realistic input the estimator IS its k-mer component.** `estimate_residual_error` returns `max(kmer, quality)`. Under an overconfident Phred (the direction real basecallers err) `max()` selects the k-mer estimate in EVERY cell; the overconfident and absent columns are identical to six decimals. Taking the more conservative signal is a real design strength, but it means every k-mer-component bias below applies directly to real ONT data.

**F1 — bias REVERSES SIGN with coverage.** At e=0.10: +0.0424 (C=5) to −0.0361 (C=100), crossing near C=10–30. Two competing mechanisms — genomic k-mers below the solidity threshold at low depth, erroneous k-mers above it at high depth.

**F2 — double-strand reads read high in 20/20 matched pairs.** `_kmer_spectrum_residual_error` uses the NON-canonical hash while the same file defines `_dynamic_k_canonical_window_hash`. The bias does not shrink with depth, consistent with a multiplicative mechanism rather than a small-sample artifact.

**F3 — the docstring's indel claim is NOT supported.** It states indels make the estimator "correctly report a higher effective error". Measured effect is −0.0052 to +0.0024 and changes sign with coverage. Scope limit: isolated single-base indels only, not homopolymer-clustered ONT indels.

**F4 — bias, not noise.** Replicate CV mostly under 0.02. More replicates cannot help.

**Saturation (separate commit).** `k_ref = 13` gives only 4^13 = 67.1M distinct 13-mers. E. coli at 5 Mb / 30× / 10% error needs ~200M — about 3× the whole space. Confirmed by scale model: at saturation ≥ 0.95 the estimator returns EXACTLY 0.0 for reads carrying 5% error, and `e = 0` fed to a `k = 1/e − 1` rule is a division by zero. This is larger than F1, and the 720-cell grid structurally cannot reach it.

## Two corrections to my own earlier commits in this PR

1. **Provenance.** An earlier README revision attributed the rule `k >= 1/e − 1` to the pre-registration. It is not there — searched `planning/PLAN-2026-03-28-rhizomorph-preregistration.md` (577 lines) and all of `manuscript/`, no match. It lives in `src/development/` (not included by `Mycelia.jl`) and `tutorials/18` (broken on master).
2. **Coverage is NOT uniform.** An earlier README revision said "coverage is uniform by construction". Reads are 5 kb from a 20 kb LINEAR reference, which produces a trapezoid: the plateau is 1.333× the nominal label and 30% of the reference sits below 0.8× at every coverage. Every coverage column is mislabelled by +33%. The sign and mechanism stand; the x-axis does not.

## Test Plan

- [x] 720/720 cells complete; committed per-cell table reproduces from the committed invocation.
- [x] Saturation probe's k=13 row (0.03788) independently reproduces the 720-cell grid at the same cell (0.0377).
- [x] Markdown lint clean (MD036/MD040).
- [ ] **Not run:** anything on real reads, homopolymer-clustered indels, non-uniform real coverage, or repeat-rich genomes. The reference is random sequence — the friendliest possible case for a k-mer spectrum method. Each omission can only make the estimator look worse than measured here.

## Reviewer note

The README section "What this harness STRUCTURALLY CANNOT test" is the part most worth scrutiny. It distinguishes what this run did not cover from what its design cannot reach; only the second is a property of the instrument, and the saturation defect falls in it.

items.title: chore(docs): remove the internal benchmarks and manuals, and correct the offload figures
items.body:
## Description

Most of what is removed here already has a counterpart upstream in the backend repo and will
arrive through the backend sync. What lives in this repo today is a second, hand-maintained
copy, so the two drift apart. Dropping them leaves a single source.

| This repo (removed) | backend counterpart |
|---|---|
| `backend/tests/benchmark_llama_server_prefill.py` | `tests/e2e/benchmark_llama_server_prefill.py` |
| `backend/tests/benchmark_offload_vram.py` | `tests/e2e/benchmark_offload_vram.py` |
| `docs/benchmarks.md` (zh) · `docs/benchmarks.en.md` | `docs/benchmarks.md` (en) |
| `docs/inference_manual.html` (zh) · `.en.html` | `docs/inference_manual.zh-TW.html` · `inference_manual.html` |
| `docs/finetune_manual.html` (zh) · `.en.html` | `docs/finetune_manual.zh-TW.html` · `finetune_manual.html` |
| `docs/site-map.html` | `docs/site-map.html` |

Note the language-suffix convention is **inverted** between the two repos: here the bare
`.html` / `.md` is the Traditional Chinese file and `.en` marks English, while upstream the
bare name is English and `.zh-TW` marks Chinese. The names collide but the languages do not
line up, so the sync needs to account for it rather than assume a same-name overwrite.

Three things have no upstream counterpart and are simply dropped:

- The two raw result files, `benchmark_llama_server_prefill_results.json` and
  `benchmark_offload_vram_results.json`. Upstream deliberately keeps benchmark output out of
  git (`chore(tests): keep the llama-server benchmark results out of git`) and writes it to a
  gitignored `tests/results/` instead. This repo now matches that.
- The three example configs: `examples/fine-tune_configs/Llama3.3-70B-finetune.json`,
  `examples/fine-tune_configs/qwen3.5-122b-lora-finetune.json`, and
  `examples/inference_configs/GPT-OSS-120B-demo-inference.json`. These were written here and
  exist nowhere else, so they go away rather than moving. The `examples/` directory is emptied
  and disappears.

**References updated:**

- `README.md` / `README.zh-TW.md` — drop the links and directory entries pointing at
  benchmarks, the site map, both HTML manuals, and `examples/`.
- `wiki/{en,zh}/comparisons/trusta-ast-vs-market-solutions.md`,
  `concepts/offload-mechanism.md`, `summary/trusta-ast-core-differentiation.md` — replace
  "see `benchmark_*.py` / reproduce it with that script / raw data in `*_results.json`" with
  "measured in-house". Those paths were already stale once upstream moved `tests/` to
  `tests/e2e/`; naming no path means a future upstream reorganisation cannot rot these pages
  again.

## Corrected figure

The published VRAM reduction was wrong and is corrected here, in
`wiki/{en,zh}/concepts/offload-mechanism.md` and
`wiki/{en,zh}/summary/trusta-ast-core-differentiation.md`.

The old figure compared whole-device VRAM against model weights. The device peak includes
whatever other processes were already holding, and the benchmark recorded that baseline
without ever subtracting it, so the reduction was understated. The backend PR fixes the
benchmark; this applies the same correction to what is already published:

    model peak = 13.39 - 1.65 = 11.74 GB
    reduction  = 1 - 11.74 / 27.508 = 57.3%        (was published as 51.3%)

This is **recomputed from the raw fields the original run recorded, not a new run**. The
full-GPU requirement, the pre-load baseline and the device peak were all captured correctly;
only the final arithmetic was wrong. The pages now state both numbers — the ~11.7 GB
attributable to the model and the ~13.4 GB the device actually peaked at — so the two are no
longer conflated.

**The tok/s figure is deliberately left at ~0.5 and flagged as pending.** The original run
stored a count of SSE chunks in the `completion_tokens` field, so the real token count was
never recorded and cannot be recovered. Confirming it needs the benchmark re-run against a GPU
with the weights available.

## Related Issues

<!-- e.g. Closes #123, Relates to #456 -->

## Checklist

- [x] The PR title follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/)
- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits (see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md))
- [ ] `pytest` passes locally — not run; no collected test was touched (`backend/pytest.ini`
      sets no `python_files`, so `benchmark_*.py` was never collected)
- [x] Tests were added or updated where relevant — n/a, deletions and documentation only
- [x] Documentation was updated where relevant (English and 繁體中文 where applicable)
- [x] I have read the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

## Notes for Reviewers

- **Merge order matters.** `benchmark_offload_vram.py` only exists upstream once the
  corresponding backend PR lands — it is added there in the same change that fixes the
  hard-coded paths. Merge that one first, or this table describes a file that is not there yet.
- The corrected reduction is arithmetic on already-recorded measurements, so it needs no GPU to
  verify: the three inputs are in the deleted `benchmark_offload_vram_results.json`, visible in
  this PR's diff.
- Every deleted filename was grepped across the repo; nothing links to them any more. The only
  remaining mentions are provenance notes in `wiki/{en,zh}/log.md` and
  `wiki/{en,zh}/sources/finetune_manual.md` ("Ingested `inference_manual.html`"), which record
  where the wiki content came from rather than linking to the file, so they were left as they
  are.
- The HTML manuals' content was already absorbed into `wiki/{en,zh}/sources/`; the wiki itself
  is untouched.

items.title: docs(plans): PLAN-0103 — Step 6 record, six ACs closed, three corrections carried
items.body:
Brings PLAN-0103 into agreement with the code after Step 6 shipped in #1138. Six ACs closed in substance still read `[ ]` on disk, and Step 6 carried no execution record.

Authored by the in-harness `plan-drafter` from a Code dispatch (ADR-009 D1). Code verified the fact-pack on disk **before** dispatching and re-verified every drafter-originated citation after — which is what produced the two findings below.

## Ticked

AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, AC-4, AC-5, AC-7 — each with an evidence block citing artifacts by path/line rather than restating them.

## AC-6 deliberately NOT ticked

Verifying the fact-pack rather than relaying it found the "closed in substance" claim false for this one.

AC-6's own wording requires the per-system env-parse tests to exclude "the persona-key variable **if SD-4 introduces one**". SD-4 did introduce one — `UI_DEMO_PERSONA_KEYS` (ruling (b), s218), made a browser-served raw-key store by the s224 credential ruling. So that parenthetical is a live obligation, not a conditional.

- **Substance holds:** no committed file carries raw key values. Fleet's `published.env:88-90` states the variable's deliberate absence and why; `docker-compose.yml:69` is a bare host pass-through; `README.md:115-140` documents provisioning; `detect-secrets` green.
- **The guard does not exist:** no test anywhere asserts `UI_DEMO_PERSONA_KEYS` is absent from any committed file — the only two test files naming it *consume* the setting. And `test_ac4_no_secret_is_committed` reads only `oct-energy`'s env, because `_DEPLOY` is pinned there (`test_published_compose.py:59`); that module's own comment records the narrowing as temporary "pending the next step", which shipped in #1114/#1116.

Net: fleet and procurement are unguarded against exactly this AC's named secrets, and fleet is the profile that introduced the raw-key variable. Recorded as a partial record so it gets closed as **code**, never ticked as prose.

## Three corrections, classified per CLAUDE.md §6

**1. AC-7 — `was an error`.** The AC's own middle clause said `appr-fleet-manager-wirat` "approves within tier". The engine refuses him — `tier_role_mismatch … routed to 'appr-owner'` — because the DOA ladder routes the hero repair's amount to the owner tier.

It was false *when written*, not overtaken: `procedures.yaml` last changed 2026-07-29 and its tier block earlier still, both before the PLAN was drafted 2026-08-09 — and the YAML's own comment at `:282-286` already said the ฿48,000 breakdown "clears ฿30,000 and lands on the OWNER's desk". Nobody ran it. Same failure family as Lesson #0041.

The AC still closes, because what shipped is **strictly stronger** than what it asked for: two refusals from two *different* governance mechanisms (separation of duties; DOA tier routing) plus one grant. A module showing only a granted approval passes with SoD deleted; one showing only an SoD refusal passes with the ladder flattened.

**2. AC-1 — `superseded by new info`.** Its literal closure condition reads "Grep = 0 matches"; a raw grep now returns 1 — comment prose in `app.js:36` explaining what replaced the constant. The shipped oracle is comment-stripped and deliberately stronger. The corrected condition ("no live-code mention") is recorded with both surviving comment sites named, so a future session running the literal grep does not read a 1-match result as an unclosed AC.

**3. ADR-0037's status — `superseded by new info`.** The PLAN called it "Proposed" in four places; it has been **Accepted** since 2026-08-10 (s218). Refreshed at the Related-ADRs line, Step 4's gate map (gate satisfied, not pending), SD-1's ruling stamp, and the References entry. The dated 2026-08-10 rulings-round paragraph keeps its original wording as a historical snapshot, matching how earlier rounds' superseded statements were left intact.

## Step 6 recorded

Under its step, in Step 10's style: PR #1138, Cray's two typed s224 rulings (layout A; credential (a)) restated, the served-to-the-browser key posture cited to its committed rationale, the boot-refusal guards including the crossed pair, and `view-monitor.js`'s `isPublished()` count going 0 → 1 against the zero Step 3 recorded.

Three items from the session-224 closeout are **attributed rather than adopted** — the pre-test non-vacuity probes, the browser display-honesty probe, and the test-count delta were not re-verified by this edit. Laundering relayed claims into PLAN-level fact is the mechanism Lesson #0041 documents.

## Scope

No ruling, scope, step, or SD slot changed. `Status:` stays `Draft` — AC-6, AC-10 and AC-11 remain open. One file changed.

## Verification

Full offline gate on the committed tree `ae39f56`, captured before pushing so `git diff --stat HEAD` was empty and the gated tree is provably the pushed tree:

- `pytest tests/` — **4025 passed, 8 skipped** in 478.31s. Identical to the pre-edit baseline, which is the check that matters here: prose is under test in this repo and pre-commit does not run pytest.
- `mypy --strict services/` — no issues in 134 source files.
- `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` — clean on the committed tree, verified via `git archive HEAD` into a scratch dir. (A bare local `ruff check .` reports one S108 in `.claude/benchmark-results/`, an **untracked** scratch file absent from git and from CI.)

The Axis-B `goal-evaluator` judged the edit adversarially from disk: **J1–J4 PASS**, J5 pending on this merge.

## Note for a follow-up, not part of this PR

`.claude/launch.json` is untracked but **not** covered by `.gitignore`, and it names `UI_DEMO_PERSONA_KEYS` — verified via `git check-ignore` (rc=1). A `git add -A` would stage it. The keys it holds are synthetic and browser-served by ruling, so the exposure is not the risk; the risk is an unprotected credential-shaped file in a public repo. This is precisely the file class AC-6's missing guard would catch.

items.title: docs: rewrite both READMEs in simplified technical English
items.body:
Both READMEs were accurate but slow to read. Long sentences, em dashes, metaphors, and a lot of
project history that helps nobody who wants to run the benchmark.

Both are now in ASD-STE100 simplified technical English: short sentences, active voice, one idea
per sentence, and **no em dashes anywhere** (verified: zero in both files).

## Root README

Restructured to the requested outline:

1. What the work does
2. The two baseline projects, LMCache and the vLLM Production Stack
3. Our three patched files, the upstream pull request, and the tunable parameter
4. Repository structure
5. Our environment: OpenShift, GPU Operator, 2 x NVIDIA A10 24 GB
6. How to run the benchmark, with a link to the benchmark README
7. Our runs and results, the metrics collected, and the figure types

I kept one thing the outline did not list: a short block that verifies the results without
hardware. §6 requires installation instructions, and that block is also the reproducibility
story. It is 12 lines.

## Benchmark README, 617 lines to 358

**The history is gone.** The two eras of `beta`, the retired cell names, the pruned directories,
the pilot archaeology, and the ticket references that only record how the file reached its
current state.

**What stays** is what an operator needs: the three sweeps, the file list, a six step procedure
from an empty cluster to figures, the known cluster problems as a table of problem and
correction, the metrics, the 12 figures, the reason for each parameter (128 prefixes, Zipf 0.9,
rate 16, 64 output tokens, 45% GPU memory, 20 seeds), the approximate runtime, the in-cluster

items.title: Fix PyPI name collision, replace unverified claims with measured benchmarks
items.body:
## Why

Two problems that a reviewer trying the library would hit immediately.

**1. The PyPI name `semanticache` belongs to someone else** — [theabrahamaudu/SemantiCache](https://github.com/theabrahamaudu/SemantiCache), published March 2025. Every `pip install semanticache[local]` line in this repo pointed users at an unrelated library. Renamed to distribution `semanticache-py`, module `semanticache_py`.

**2. `benchmark.py` had never been run.** It called `SemanticCache(embedding="local", storage="memory")` — neither kwarg exists — and raised `TypeError` immediately. Every figure in BENCHMARKS.md was written without executing it.

## Measured vs. published

| Threshold | Published | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| 0.85 | ~72% savings, 1–2 FP | **46.7% cost cut**, 0 FP |
| 0.92 (default) | ~61% savings, 0 FP | **21.7% cost cut**, 0 FP |
| 0.95 | ~42% | **8.3%** |

The old table conflated paraphrase recall (denominator: 40 paraphrases) with calls avoided (denominator: 60 queries). Both are now reported separately. Raw output is committed to `benchmark_results.json`.

Also removed: a README section claiming "1,000 realistic chatbot queries / 61.2% hit rate / 0.3% false positive rate" — that run never happened. The "40–70%" headline isn't reachable at any tested threshold.

## Notable finding

Unrelated queries never exceed **0.328** similarity against anything cached, while real paraphrases median **0.856**. The wide empty band explains zero false positives at every threshold, and suggests the 0.92 default is stricter than necessary — `benchmark.py`'s own recommendation logic picks 0.85. Default left unchanged pending a larger false-positive sample.

## Other corrections

- Embedding overhead measured at 6.0ms p50 / 17.3ms p95 (was asserted "~20–50ms")
- Cache-hit example similarities were invented; the transformer paraphrases actually score 0.68–0.70, not ~0.93
- GPTCache comparison was wrong — it *does* support local embeddings (ONNX, SentenceTransformers) and runs on SQLite+FAISS without Redis
- Dropped the "production-ready" self-claim from an alpha library with no users
- `lightweight_demo.py` printed "2 misses, 1 hit" unconditionally while recording 0 hits; its toy embedder scores the advertised paraphrase 0.742, below its own threshold
- Citation year 2024 → 2026

## Verified

- 13/13 tests pass
- Wheel builds clean as `semanticache_py-0.1.0`
- Both runnable examples produce output matching their claims
- Thread-safety claim checked and kept (real locks in `storage.py`); README quickstart example checked and kept (0.9242, genuinely clears 0.92)

items.title: README: rewrite as the project's front door after the scanner phase
items.body:
## Why

The README on `main` describes a repo that contains only the blind/answer-key split, and ends with *"The scan → fix → verify harness itself is future work."* Since then the scanner has been built, run six times, benchmarked across three inference models, and had five investigations written up. The README was the only document that had not caught up.

This is step 1 of the repo-cleanup work: **README only.** No source, docs, or structural changes — those are separate branches.

## What

Rewritten to the agreed eight-section plan. 665 insertions, 31 deletions, one file.

| § | Section | What went in |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | One-liner + headline | Recall 71.1%, localization 88.7%, file-level 100%, $4.37 / 13m04s, against the ≥90% targets — **draft, see open item below** |
| 2 | The problem | 20% recall / 50% localization from the pure-pattern tool in the five-tool benchmark; the two tools of five that produced nothing died on a spend cap and a clock, not on reasoning — and the three design decisions that came out of that |
| 3 | Architecture | Five stages with inputs/outputs, a mermaid diagram colour-coding LLM vs. deterministic (only Stages 0 and 2 call a model), plus why one-lane-per-file replaced category lanes and why the trace loop exists |
| 4 | Project structure & engineering process | Two-repo mechanical split, `CLAUDE.md` as an enforced contract, docs tiered by lifetime, dispatch briefs as work specs, the runbook's *verify the tree not the intent* step, run archiving, append-only ledgers, the guard suite. The blind boundary sits **inside** this as one of the guarantees, not as the headline |
| 5 | Results & benchmarking | (a) runs 1–6 across recall / localization / file-level / precision proxy / hedging / tokens / cost / wall clock; (b) three models on identical prompts, lanes, corpus and scorer. Qualifications inline, not in footnotes |
| 6 | Technical challenges | Five, each as problem → investigation method → resolution → what it changed |
| 7 | Running it | Quickstart, model registry (adding a model = one JSON entry), concurrency derivation, Stage 2 arm selection |
| 8 | Known limits | n=97 on one app, the pretraining confound, unmet ≥90% targets with their structural caps, v2's missing validator and what that does to the precision proxy |

### On §6

The five written up are: the line-count desync invisible to every metric; concurrency vs. rate limits and lane loss; the 429 that carried `no credits remaining`; the location-weighted metric worth ~10 points of phantom variance; and run 4's F3 sweep, which reached 100% conformance on 3005/3005 lane-class pairs and moved `FILE_ONLY` by zero. Framing is diagnostic — each ends with what changed, and the windowing A/B is folded into the last one as a second instance of the same "confirmed mechanism ≠ confirmed cause" pattern.

### On the diagram

The plan marks the diagram as a separate work item. This PR carries a first-pass mermaid pipeline diagram — stages, artifacts between them, colour-coded for model-calling vs. deterministic vs. not-built — because the architecture section is unreadable without one. It renders natively on GitHub and needs no assets. **Treat it as a placeholder for the dedicated diagram work**, not as that work being done.

## Verification

- Every number traces to a committed artifact in `docs/run-history.md`, `docs/benchmarking-results.md`, `docs/analysis/`, or `results/archive/2026-07-five-tool-benchmark/`. Nothing was estimated or carried over from memory.
- Costs use the **corrected** `$0.20/$1.20` rates, with the 5× correction stated in the table's qualifications rather than buried.
- All ground-truth-denominated figures are on the **97 reachable** denominator, stated up front in §5.
- Claims checked against source rather than docs: `grep` confirms **zero** `if (provider === …)` outside `shared/`; `vuln-classes.json` has **14** classes covering **25** OWASP codes; the v2 playbook directory has **14** files, one per class. (`docs/stages/stage2-hunt-lanes.md` says "16 playbooks / 26 codes" and is stale — flagged for the docs pass, not touched here.)
- Guard-suite size is described as *"~80 assertion sites, more at runtime"* rather than a fixed count: `guard.test.ts` has 80 `check(` sites but the registry block iterates every model, and `node_modules` is absent in this environment so the true runtime count was not confirmed.

## Blind-boundary check

Aggregates only. No challenge identifier appears, nothing is paired with a file or a line, and no per-entry hit/miss detail is present. The five-tool archive is cited by its aggregate table, which is already redacted upstream. No credential, endpoint or model id is introduced — the registry example uses the same public shape as `docs/architecture/multi-model-architecture.md`.

## Open item — §1 needs your call

The headline is a **draft**, and the README says so inline (a blockquote that should come out before merge). It currently leads with the four-row table above. Alternatives, all defensible from the same artifacts:

1. **As drafted** — recall 71.1% / localization 88.7% / 100% file-level / cost + runtime, against targets.
2. **Lead with the attributable figures instead** — +11.3 of run 6's +27.8 recall points survive the budget-matched null. More conservative, harder to read cold, and the most honest single number in the repo.
3. **Lead with coverage rather than percentages** — *"40 of 66 distinct ground-truth locations, 100% file-level, $4.37"* — sidesteps the location-weighting caveat entirely.
4. **Lead with the cross-model result** — three model families through one byte-identical pipeline, spanning 5.7× in cost and 12 points in recall. Positions the repo as measurement infrastructure rather than as one scanner.

Tell me which and I'll rewrite §1 and drop the placeholder note. Everything downstream of §1 stands on its own either way.

items.title: refactor: make Agent Team incremental and contract-centric
items.body:
## Summary

Rebuilds Codex Agent Team around a first-principles compute-graph model instead of a fixed Luna/Terra/Sol lane sequence.

### Core architecture
- main session owns the compute graph and final acceptance
- no model is a mandatory stage; every Agent call must satisfy a distinct unresolved dependency
- Luna Max remains the default execution tier
- Terra becomes a read-only complex-investigation tier for unresolved technical deltas, not a generic reviewer or whole-task retry
- Sol becomes the selective judgment/review tier; `main -> Luna -> Sol -> main` is a normal short path
- adds Contractability Gate before writing delegation
- replaces Task Packet with Delegation Contract including Decision Rights and Acceptance Oracle
- adds Shared Evidence State, dependency-aware invalidation, and Delta Escalation
- useful parallelism requires different dependencies; duplicated inference is rejected by policy

### Routing and profiles
- removes Portable Mode
- decouples semantic roles from model names
- adds namespaced profiles: `codex_agent_team_reader`, `codex_agent_team_worker`, `codex_agent_team_investigator`, `codex_agent_team_advisor`
- managed installer migrates old model-named profiles only when previous ownership is proven

### Runtime Truth v2
- fixes the P0 where empty/partial observation objects could be treated as R1/R2-quality evidence
- adds independent typed `route_evidence`, `ancestry_evidence`, and `permission_evidence`
- complete role/model/effort is required before L1/R1/R2 can be emitted
- ancestry or permission conflicts no longer contaminate route status, while material cross-source conflicts still quarantine the result
- missing parent/permission evidence stays `not_observed`

### Behavioral eval v2
- switches to paired workload runs
- primary comparison: raw prompt -> Luna vs compiled contract -> Luna
- declared primary comparison modes are enforced per pair
- paired candidate-minus-baseline deltas are the primary scoring output
- global mode aggregates are descriptive only and explicitly unsuitable for cross-workload comparison
- adds main-session correction cost, scope/wrong-edit/regression metrics, review false positives, and evidence-reuse waste metrics
- adds explicit Luna + selective Sol comparison and Terra delta-escalation workloads

### Documentation
- rewrites Chinese and English READMEs around incremental orchestration and evidence reuse

items.title: Correct adaptive pooling and zero-op counting rules
items.body:
## What

Correct the counting rules that can be fixed completely on the supported PyTorch range:

- Adaptive average pooling now sums the integer windows PyTorch actually pools instead of using a fractional input/output ratio.
- Nearest and nearest-exact upsampling count zero arithmetic operations; interpolation costs stay in the hook that owns them.
- GroupNorm and RMSNorm reuse the existing normalization rule.
- The README benchmark rows are refreshed for the nearest-upsampling correction.
- Bump the package patch version from 2.1.1 to 2.1.2 so this final PR triggers the release after the preceding fixes merge.

The proposed MultiheadAttention rule was removed during review. It crashed on valid keyword-only calls because PyTorch 1.8 forward hooks cannot observe keyword arguments, and profile_origin() does not hook composite modules. Shipping partial coverage or a compatibility branch would regress valid models rather than solve the problem.

## Validation

- 20 existing tests pass.
- Ruff and formatting checks pass.
- Exhaustive AdaptiveAvgPool1d/2d/3d checks across small input/output shapes match the exact PyTorch window boundaries.
- GroupNorm, RMSNorm, nearest upsampling, keyword-only MultiheadAttention non-regression, and the 2.1.2 version were checked directly.

## Deleted

The incomplete MultiheadAttention rule and registration, calculate_adaptive_avg(), calculate_upsample(), and the one-consumer upsampling cost constant.

## 🛠️ PR Summary

<sub>Made with ❤️ by [Ultralytics Actions](https://www.ultralytics.com/actions)</sub>

### 🌟 Summary

THOP 2.1.2 improves operation counting for normalization, adaptive pooling, and upsampling layers, with refreshed YOLO benchmark values. 🚀

### 📊 Key Changes

- Added FLOP/MAC counting support for `nn.GroupNorm`.
- Added optional support for `nn.RMSNorm` in PyTorch 2.4 and newer.
- Improved adaptive average pooling calculations to account for actual pooling windows and avoid fractional operation counts.
- Updated upsampling operation estimates:
  - Supports `nearest-exact`.
  - Uses explicit per-element costs for linear, bilinear, bicubic, and trilinear modes.
  - Warns and safely defaults to zero operations for unsupported modes.
- Removed obsolete adaptive pooling and upsampling helper functions.
- Bumped the package version from `2.1.1` to `2.1.2`.
- Updated English and Chinese README benchmark tables with minor corrected values.

### 🎯 Purpose & Impact

- 📈 Produces more accurate and consistent computational-cost estimates for modern PyTorch models.
- 🧩 Improves profiling coverage for models using GroupNorm and RMSNorm, including newer architectures.
- 🛠️ Makes upsampling estimates clearer and more maintainable across supported interpolation modes.
- ✅ Prevents fractional operation totals from adaptive average pooling calculations.
- 📚 Keeps published YOLOv8, YOLO11, and YOLO26 benchmark results aligned with the updated profiling behavior.

items.title: bench: add headless benchmark suite + correct README performance claims
items.body:
## Summary

- Adds a standalone Go benchmark under `benchmark/` comparing plain (bash/grep only) vs gopls-mcp (semantic MCP tools) via headless Claude Code sessions
- 11 tasks across definition, reference, implementation, call-hierarchy, and dependency-graph categories; all score 100% for both groups
- Automated MustContain scoring eliminates manual answer review
- Corrects `README.md` performance claims that the data does not support

## Benchmark results

| Task | plain | gopls-mcp | gopls calls |
|------|------:|----------:|:-----------:|
| def-same-pkg | 15.8s | 28.1s | 2 |
| def-cross-pkg | 25.5s | 33.9s | 2 |
| def-cross-stdlib | 23.8s | **20.9s** | 1 |
| def-cross-third-party | 64.7s | **46.2s** | 1 |
| ref-same-pkg | 17.1s | 34.0s | 2 |
| ref-cross-pkg | 14.2s | 57.8s | 2 |
| ref-cross-third-party | 24.0s | 51.6s | 2 |
| impl-same-pkg | 31.0s | **21.4s** | 1 |
| impl-cross-pkg | 50.3s | **20.1s** | 1 |
| call-hierarchy | 47.8s | **28.2s** | 2 |
| dependency-graph | 64.6s | **30.6s** | 1 |

**gopls-mcp wins 6/11 tasks.** On semantic tasks (impl, call-hierarchy, dependency-graph) it uses 2–4× fewer tool calls and is 1.5–3× faster. On simple lookups (def-same, ref-same, ref-cross-*) plain bash/grep wins because MCP init overhead exceeds navigation cost.

## README correction

Closes #43. The old README claimed "lightning-fast", "instant response times", and "Zero noise" without data. The new text:
- States the actual value proposition: type-checker-level correctness on semantic tasks
- Gives honest call-count numbers from the benchmark
- Acknowledges that grep remains effective for simple lookups

## Key engineering notes

**Deferred tool protocol (root cause of impl-cross-pkg 340s → 20s):** gopls-mcp tools are deferred in Claude Code. Without explicit instruction, agents spawn sub-agents (which don't inherit loaded schemas) or fall back to Python subprocess. The preamble now says: call ToolSearch, then call the tool *directly in the same turn* — no sub-agents, no subprocesses.

**Contamination guard:** plain agents that find the gopls-mcp binary in PATH via marketplace.json will manually spawn it. `plainPreamble` blocks this.

## Running the benchmark

```bash
go run ./benchmark/cmd/run \
  --target /path/to/go/project \
  --gopls-mcp-bin $(which gopls-mcp) \
  --out /tmp/bench-results
```

## Test plan

- [x] All 11 tasks complete with 100% score (plain and gopls-mcp)
- [x] impl-cross-pkg gopls-mcp: 340s (pathological) → 20s (1 gopls call) after preamble fix
- [x] `benchmark/results/` excluded from git via .gitignore
- [x] `go build -buildvcs=false ./...` passes

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

items.title: fix(bench): esmemeval appraiser closed in ingest + X2 direct-VAD data correction
items.body:
## The bug

`AFTQueryAppraisedEsmemAdapter.ingest` built a temporary `EmotionalMemory` sharing `self._appraiser` and called `engine.close()` — which closes the appraisal engine's **httpx client**. Every subsequent `retrieve()`-time query appraisal hit a closed client and, with `fallback_on_error=True`, **silently fell back to the keyword appraiser** instead of the pre-registered `DIRECT_VAD_SCHEMA`. ~1,131 of ~1,133 query appraisals were affected (session/encode appraisals ran before the close → D1/D2 valid). MADial-Bench (Addendum X) is unaffected (persistent engine).

## The fix

- `ingest` no longer closes the engine (InMemoryStore is GC'd; the shared appraiser stays open); a new `close()` releases the appraiser once at end of run, mirroring the MADial adapter.

## Data correction (X2 re-run with genuine direct-VAD)

Verdict **unchanged** (Hx2 FAIL, inverted, powered); magnitude modestly smaller — direct-VAD query affect is slightly less harmful than keyword on this affect-orthogonal corpus:

| | published (bug) | corrected |
|---|---|---|
| AFT u_nDCG@4 | 0.120 | **0.133** |
| Δ | −0.164 | **−0.150** [−0.165, −0.136] |
| D1 AUC | 0.971 | 0.950 |
| D2 | 68.2% | 63.0% |

Nice consistency check: the corrected run's neutral-query fraction (45.5%) matches the original **post-hoc** (45.2%) — that post-hoc used a fresh healthy appraiser, so it was always right.

Propagated the corrected numbers to: closure (with a **Data-correction note**) + prereg Status, claim matrix (+ verbatim `09_current_evidence` mirror — test green), `08_limitations`, paper (abstract + X2 paragraph + regenerated arXiv bundle, 19pp), README, comparison, `benchmarks/README`, research index, ROADMAP, the two dated review docs, and a CHANGELOG Unreleased entry. **v0.15.0 carried the pre-correction numbers**; main now has the corrected direct-VAD values.

`make check` + claim-matrix mirror test + `check-arxiv-bundle` green.
