items.title: docs: comprehensive project documentation update & baseline evaluation suite
items.body:
## Summary

Documentation update that turned into a correctness pass on the measurement pipeline. The
headline change is that **the benchmark now reports what it measured**, rather than a mix of
measured and fabricated figures that shared filenames and formats.

Adds **Trivy** as a fourth scanner, removes fabricated result artefacts, fixes a plan-level
policy that inverted one control, fixes a case-isolation defect that inflated the corpus,
and repairs CI checks that could not fail.

`665 files changed`, 72 commits. Every table in the paper is generated from recorded scanner
output by `evaluation/analyze.py`; none is hand-written.

---

## Measured results

48 admissible cases (26 vulnerable / 22 compliant), 5 repeats, `control` matching strictness.

| Tool | TP | FP | TN | FN | Recall | 95% CI | Precision | Latency (ms) |
| :--- | -: | -: | -: | -: | -----: | :----- | --------: | -----------: |
| Checkov | 23 | 0 | 22 | 3 | 88.46% | [69.85, 97.55] | 100.00% | 2371.0 ± 85.8 |
| tfsec | 22 | 2 | 20 | 4 | 84.62% | [65.13, 95.64] | 91.67% | 419.5 ± 7.5 |
| Trivy | 21 | 1 | 21 | 5 | 80.77% | [60.65, 93.45] | 95.45% | 597.5 ± 25.3 |
| OPA (plan-level) | 20 | 0 | 22 | 6 | 76.92% | [56.35, 91.03] | 100.00% | 18.1 ± 4.7 |
| IaCSecBench L1 | 1 | 1 | 21 | 25 | 3.85% | [0.10, 19.64] | 50.00% | 0.2 ± 0.1 |

**The reference pipeline does not lead the comparison, and that is reported as measured.**
No pairwise difference among the four is significant after Holm–Bonferroni correction — a
consequence of corpus size, not evidence of equivalence.

---

## 1. Trivy added, and the finding it produced

Trivy is included because **tfsec is retired** — Aqua folded tfsec's engine and rule set into
Trivy — so a comparison reporting tfsec alone characterises a scanner practitioners are
advised off.

The two are **not independent**, and the PR is explicit about this rather than presenting
four columns as four opinions. Their identifiers are the same AVD numbers spelled differently
(`AVD-AWS-0086` vs `AWS-0086`). Trivy's control-map entries are therefore **derived
mechanically from tfsec's own recorded output**, which emits both spellings in every result —
*not* chosen by observing which rules Trivy fires on a case, which would fit the taxonomy to
the tool and manufacture detections. A regression test re-derives the crosswalk and fails on
drift in either direction.

**The measurement this enables:** tfsec and Trivy agree on 46 of 48 cases. Both
disagreements are the same control — IAM policy wildcards. tfsec reports
`aws-iam-no-policy-wildcards` on both members of the pair; Trivy emits `AWS-0057` on neither,
anywhere in the corpus.

The divergence is not a plain regression. tfsec's rule catches the violation **and** misfires
on the compliant case; Trivy's silence forfeits both. tfsec therefore records higher recall
and Trivy higher precision, from one rule behaving differently. Verified that Trivy's miss is
genuine and not a taxonomy artefact: the only unmapped finding it emits on that case is an S3
versioning rule, unrelated to IAM.

Corroborating the shared provenance quantitatively: of the identifiers each tool emits that
the taxonomy does not cover, **12 of tfsec's 13 have an exact Trivy counterpart on an
identical number of cases**. The thirteenth, a CloudFront TLS-policy rule, is absent from
Trivy as `AWS-0057` is. Two products separated by a major version and an engine change differ,
on this corpus, by two rules.

Trivy runs with `--skip-check-update`, because an uncached run would either charge a registry
fetch to scanner latency or, on fetch failure, record every case as clean —
indistinguishable from a genuinely clean corpus. `benchmark.yml` warms the cache and then
*proves* it warm by running the harness's exact command, failing on zero findings.

## 2. Fabricated artefacts removed

Three stages compute results by multiplying corpus counts by hardcoded per-tool rates. They
previously wrote to **the same paths a real run uses**, so a fabricated table and a measured
one were indistinguishable by filename.

- New shared opt-in gate (`evaluation/synthetic_guard.py`): `evaluation/score.py`,
  `pipeline/run_experiments.py` and `experiments/generate_charts.py` refuse to run unless
  `IACSECBENCH_ALLOW_SYNTHETIC=1` is set for that specific invocation.
- Deleted: `results/benchmark_results.json`, `results/metrics.csv`, `results/charts/*.txt`,
  `benchmark/reports/experiment_results.json`.
- `leaderboard/results.synthetic.csv` untracked and gitignored — it held 345-case, 90.72%
  figures contradicting the measured 48-case results, and shipped in the release archive.
- `score.py` redirected away from `leaderboard/results.csv`, which `analyze.py` writes from
  real runs, so the collision is now impossible rather than merely avoided.

`pipeline/sync_to_obsidian.py` had two hardcoded tables claiming 345 cases and 100% detection;
these now render from `results/evaluation.json`, or print a warning when no measurement exists.

## 3. Plan-level policy inverted one control

`cis_aws_benchmark.rego` tested for the *presence* of `kms_key_id`. Terraform serialises three
configuration states into a plan: an attribute set to a literal carries its value; one set from
a reference is **omitted** and recorded as not-yet-known; one **not set at all is present with
value `null`**. In Rego `null` is defined, so the presence test failed on the omitted case and
succeeded on the reference case — **inverting** the control.

The compliant case was reported violating and the violating case compliant, and the two errors
concealed each other: one FP and one FN, a signature indistinguishable from ordinary
imprecision.

The corrected rule distinguishes not-set from not-yet-known and reports only the former;
not-yet-known is genuinely indeterminate at plan time and is reported as neither. This is a
property of plan-level evaluation, not of this implementation — any engine reading plan
documents inherits the distinction, and any that collapses it inverts the same class of control.
Block-typed attributes are unaffected.

Effect: OPA FP 1→0, FN 7→6, recall 73.08% → 76.92%. Because the correction followed inspecting
results, it is disclosed as **one round of iteration the comparators did not receive**, and
`results/pre_opa_polarity_fix/` retains the pre-correction figures so the disclosure is checkable.

## 4. Case-isolation defect

A case is scanned as a **directory**. Four external CIS cases shared one, so every tool received
identical input and returned a byte-identical finding set, while scoring compared that one
result against four different controls. Four rows entered each confusion matrix where one
observation existed.

This misstates *precision*, not point estimates: interval width is driven by the number of
independent observations. After isolating them, **every confusion matrix was identical** — but
unmapped findings fell 313→268 (cross-contamination removed) and L1 `any`-level recall fell
from 100% to 92.31%, the 100% having been an artefact.

`evaluation/corpus.py` now **refuses to load** a corpus in which two cases share a directory.

## 5. Control map audited

28 → 26 controls. Removed 7 OPA identifiers no policy emits, corrected three Checkov mappings
(`CKV_K8S_23`/`CKV_K8S_40` → `CKV_K8S_6`; `CKV_K8S_13` (Memory *requests*) → `CKV_K8S_12`
(Memory *Limits*)), deleted two controls nothing could detect.

`STO_UNENCRYPTED_BUCKET` was retitled after blind relabelling disagreed: its text ("lacks
server-side encryption") is satisfied by SSE-S3, but the case labels an AES256 bucket violating,
correct only under a customer-managed-key requirement. **The control text was corrected, not the
label** — a CMK requirement is defensible and is what the corpus, the policy set, and the
CMK rules of Checkov, tfsec and Trivy all test. A test now pins the CIS citation to the
generator specification so the two cannot drift.

7 new tests enforce the invariants, including that unverified entries are **reported, not hidden**.

## 6. Ground-truth labelling

Labels are derived mechanically, so rater disagreement is impossible by construction and an
agreement coefficient over the generator's output would measure determinism. A **blind second
labelling pass** was run against the threat that does apply — specification error: comments
stripped, order keyed on a hash, reasons recorded before comparison.

47/48 agreed, κ = 0.958 before reconciliation. The single disagreement was a genuine
specification defect of exactly the predicted kind (§5). Stated limitations: the second rater is
automated, so this is **not** human inter-rater reliability, and it read the same public
documentation the specifications were written from, so agreement is biased upward. Five cases
were previously inspected; excluding them leaves 42/43.

`benchmark/labelling/` holds per-case labels, reasons and caveats.

## 7. CI/CD

**`IACSECBENCH_ALLOW_SYNTHETIC: '1'` removed from job scope in `ci.yml` and `infra-ci.yml`
(4 places).** *The previous version of this PR description listed adding it as a contribution.*
It switched the guard off for everything in the job — including the test asserting the guard
works. Tests that need it now set it per test, and `ci.yml` runs all three fabricating stages
with it absent and **fails if any succeeds**.

Both workflows also called `experiments/run_all.sh`, which now runs the real measurement — in
`ci.yml` that would have *failed*, since no scanner is installed there.

- **`ci.yml`** — fast structural corpus check plus the guard-regression step.
- **`infra-ci.yml`** — `opa check` + `opa fmt` over **both** policy sets (an earlier revision
  used Rego-v1-invalid constructs, so that layer silently never executed and scored a total
  miss on every case), Terraform-mode corpus admissibility, harness-wiring check.
- **`benchmark.yml`** (new) — the full measurement on dispatch + weekly cron. Installs all four
  scanners and **asserts each is present**, since an absent tool yields a silently missing
  column. Uploads `results/` as an artefact and **never commits**: committing would replace
  locally measured latency, the only publishable kind, with runner noise.
- **`update-data.yml`** — its `date` input was interpolated into a command string that
  `datagov-fetch` splices into a `run:` block: two hops from a dispatch field to a shell. Now
  bound to `env:`, rejected unless a real calendar date.
- **`release-please.yml`** — the "replication archive" omitted `experiments/` (the harness
  entry points), `pipeline/`, `leaderboard/` and the dependency manifests. A reader got the
  corpus but could not reproduce a number from it.
- **`doc8` removed** from `ci.yml` and pre-commit. It reads only `.rst`/`.txt`; every path named
  was Markdown, so the step passed **without opening a file** and the hook reported
  `(no files to check) Skipped` on every run. A green check that inspects nothing occupies the
  slot where a missing check would be noticed. Markdown is covered by prettier instead, with
  `.prettierignore` excluding generated files.

## 8. Lint, config and test-harness fixes

- `bandit -c pyproject.toml` **could never read that config in CI** — the composite action
  installed plain `bandit`; TOML parsing needs `bandit[toml]`.
- **`pytest` never ran the evaluation tests.** `testpaths` omitted `evaluation/tests`, and
  because `evaluation/tests/__init__.py` exists while `evaluation/__init__.py` does not,
  pytest's prepend mode put `evaluation/` on `sys.path` and `from evaluation.stats import …`
  raised. Added the testpath and `pythonpath = ["."]`; bare `pytest` now collects **133**, up
  from 78.
- `npm run format` rewrote 21 Markdown files that `format:check` never checked.
- flake8/bandit/pylint were failing repo-wide on the new `evaluation/` code. Real fixes where
  the finding was real; suppressions only where inapplicable, each with a recorded reason
  (`B404`/`B603` — a harness whose purpose is invoking scanners, already using argv lists and
  `shutil.which`; `B311` — a seeded generator for a *reproducible* bootstrap; `R0902` — all
  seven are `@dataclass` records).
- Removed a dead `n_total` parameter from `pairwise_comparisons`; each comparison correctly
  uses the cases the two tools actually share.
- 14 new tests for the Trivy parser. Its identifier has moved between `ID` and `AVDID` and in
  and out of an `AVD-` prefix across releases; since the control map is keyed on the bare form,
  a spelling change would stop matching every entry at once, and the parser yields unmatchable
  identifiers rather than raising — so that failure would present as zero detections.

## 9. Documentation corrections

Beyond adding Trivy to nine files, three claims were false:

- `docs/framework/README.md` said the unit tests verify **"100% engine accuracy"**. Unit tests
  cannot measure accuracy, and that engine's measured recall is **3.85%**.
- `README.md` carried a hardcoded **`IaC Coverage 100%`** badge. Measured: **22 of 26** controls
  exercised, 8 mappings unverified. Removed along with three other static shields that stayed
  green regardless of state.
- `application/README.md` claimed **100% API test coverage**. Measured: **92%**.

Two READMEs documented files that do not exist (`check_compliance.py`, `generate_docs.sh`,
`schemas.py`, `services.py`) while omitting everything that does. `scripts/README.md` now also
records that none of those utilities is wired into CI and that `compliance_checker.py` is a stub.

`evaluation/README.md` claimed evaluation against Sentinel and Terratest; neither has ever been
executed here.

---

## Verification

- `pytest` → **133 passed**
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` → clean
- `pre-commit run --all-files` → all hooks pass (no skipped no-op hooks remain)
- `opa check` + `opa fmt --list` over both policy sets → clean
- `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` → clean
- `make paper` → builds, **0 unresolved `TODO(author)` markers**; `make check` → no missing or
  uncited references
- All 7 workflows and 4 composite actions parse

---

## Known limitations, stated rather than resolved

- **`results/run_manifest.json` records commit `dde59f84`, which is 11 commits behind this
  branch's HEAD and predates the Trivy harness.** The measurement ran against a working tree
  that was not yet committed, and the manifest has no field recording that. Anyone checking out
  `dde59f84` gets a harness with no Trivy support. The manifest should record tree cleanliness;
  until it does, treat its commit field as approximate.
- **N = 48 is underpowered** for the comparison it makes. Intervals span ~28 points and no
  pairwise difference survives correction.
- **8 of 26 control-map entries remain unverified** — tfsec 1.28 exposes no check-listing
  command, so these need the upstream Trivy/tfsec catalogue.
- **4 controls are unexercised** (3 Kubernetes, API-gateway authorization) — a corpus gap.
- **Only two independent third-party rule sets** are represented across three scanners, since
  Trivy inherits tfsec's.
- **Independent human relabelling remains outstanding**; the automated pass is not a substitute.
- The corpus was authored by the same investigator who implemented the evaluated policy set.
  Controlled-corpus results should be read as an **upper bound** on field performance.
- The pipeline validates the corpus **twice** per run (~7–8 min of duplicated
  `terraform validate`); scans are fully serial. Not addressed here.

items.title: Re-verify the three hardened repos against their live state
items.body:
Every figure below was read from the repository or its CI run on 2026-07-27. Nothing was carried over from the previous version of this file.

## Corrected — these were wrong on the live profile

| Claim | Was | Is | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Salary predictor test count | 222 | **509** | `main` @ `cf38148`, CI run |
| Salary predictor coverage | "92% actual" | **91.33%** against the 88 floor | same CI run |
| Job decision engine suite | "under 3 seconds" | **about 3 seconds** | measured `350 passed in 3.27s` |

The 222 predated three merged hardening rounds. 3.27s is not "under 3" — small, but it is a number a reader can check in one command.

## Verified and left alone

- NYC honest test R² **0.835**, leaked v1 **0.997** — `reports/training_metrics.json`
- **4,526** listings; external benchmark **18,321** scored sales — `benchmarks/results.json` (`n_scored`)
- NYC coverage gate **78** (`--cov-fail-under=78` in CI), actual **88.85%**, **220 passed**
- **29** mutations, **all 29 caught** — re-ran `scripts/verify_gates.py` today
- `schema-firewall` exports exactly **three** checks, and PyPI serves **0.2.1**
- JAMA / Nature Communications / Kaggle Santander references are real, in `README.md` and `_checks.py`

## Added — work that existed but the profile never mentioned

The salary predictor's section described a 2024-era version of the repo. It now names what is actually in it: published metrics pinned to the artefact that produced them, hyper-parameters with a committed producer and a search recorded as a tie rather than a win, an integrity gate that refuses to start on a *missing* manifest as well as a mismatched digest, one key across the prediction/drift/telemetry routes with auth resolving before the rate limiter, and a conformal margin whose serving path is pinned by tests rather than assumed.

The NYC mutation harness now says what it is for, and gives the number that makes it credible: it started at **6 of 15** caught. That is the evidence that a passing suite proves nothing on its own.

`schema-firewall` names its three checks and what 0.2.1 fixed — 0.2.0 had narrowed tail sampling to the twenty highest-variance columns, re-opening a fail-open that 0.1.3 had closed; a cross-row edit on a low-variance column was missed on eighteen of twenty seeds on a twenty-six column frame.

## One thing for you to decide — I did not touch it

The private-name sweep (external list, positive control 50/50 firing) reports **one hit on the live profile: line 23**, in the RAG platform paragraph that names the private flagship. It is **pre-existing on `main`** and **outside this diff** — my hunks are at lines 14, 36, 41, 45 and 54.

I have not removed it, because it reads as a deliberate positioning choice in your own prose, and that is yours to make. But it is a genuine conflict between the ban-list and this page, so it should be a decision rather than an oversight: keep it as intentional disclosure, or drop the name and say "a private flagship built on the same design."

## Correction I made to myself

My first draft of the `schema-firewall` row said 0.2.1 closed a fail-open where a transform mutating its input in place was reported clean. That is a different finding. The changelog says tail sampling. Corrected before commit.

English-first documentation with the Portuguese version preserved, plus three factual corrections.

## Structure

- `README.md` is now English; the previous Portuguese README is preserved verbatim-ish as `README.pt-BR.md`. Both cross-link.
- `docs/` split into `docs/en/` and `docs/pt-BR/` — **29 files each, full parity** — indexed by `docs/README.md`. Portuguese originals moved with `git mv`.

## Corrections

1. **Broken on GitHub, worked locally.** The README linked `[CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md)` but the tracked file is lowercase `claude.md`. Fine on Windows, 404 on GitHub's case-sensitive backend. Fixed.
2. **`docs/infrastructure/ci-cd.md` was factually wrong.** It stated no GitHub Actions workflow was configured, while `.github/workflows/qa.yml` (Ruff + pytest with `--cov-fail-under=80`) and the E2E workflow both exist and run. Corrected in both language versions.

Root carries `claude.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.agents/AGENTS.md` and 15 vendored third-party skill packages. For a repo meant to read as a portfolio piece, that is a lot of AI-tooling clutter above the fold. Left alone — moving it is a repo-structure decision, not documentation.

items.title: Add pluggable offline ASR and Japanese intent foundation
items.body:
## What changed

- added a pluggable offline ASR interface
- preserved Vosk behind the new interface
- added an optional `faster-whisper` CPU/int8 backend
- changed faster-whisper confidence handling to derive an utterance score from segment log probabilities rather than language-detection probability
- added Japanese Unicode/spacing/punctuation normalization
- added replaceable `core`, `kali`, and `azazel` vocabulary packs for ASR representation correction
- added deterministic intent routing so execution no longer depends on tokenizer whitespace
- added confidence policy: `execute / clarify / reject`
- unknown or low-confidence input fails closed
- legacy command/SOP fallback now requires explicit yes/no confirmation before execution
- fixed the original Japanese boolean-condition bug by replacing ambiguous string checks with explicit intents
- added `DRY_RUN` mode so voice tuning can exercise recognition, intent, and confirmation without executing operational actions
- added a Raspberry Pi 5 benchmark corpus and backend-neutral evaluator for transcript accuracy, intent accuracy, false-execution rate, and latency
- added lightweight GitHub Actions tests for NLU, policy, vocabulary, and evaluator compilation
- updated README and migration documentation

## Why

The original Japanese path coupled Vosk output directly to tokenization and string-oriented command matching. This made Babbly sensitive to spacing, segmentation, and representation variation. It also allowed unknown-intent text to fall through to legacy command/SOP matching. The new architecture separates recognition, normalization, intent, policy, and execution authority.

## Compatibility

`ASR_BACKEND` defaults to `vosk`, so existing installations retain the current recognizer until explicitly switched. `faster-whisper` is optional and can point to a pre-provisioned local model directory for disconnected operation.

## Validation

Focused pytest coverage now checks Japanese normalization, domain vocabulary correction, deterministic intent resolution, unknown-input fail-closed behavior, and confidence-policy decisions. A CI workflow is included. Raspberry Pi hardware/audio performance still requires real-device validation.

## Safe field tuning

Set `DRY_RUN: true` while evaluating recognition. Babbly will suppress executable network scans, command mode, commands, and SOP operations while still exercising wake phrase recognition, NLU, confidence policy, and confirmation dialogue.

## Benchmark path

`benchmarks/ja_command_corpus.json` plus `tools/evaluate_asr_results.py` provide a reproducible comparison path for Vosk vs faster-whisper. The design prioritizes task-level intent accuracy and false-execution rate, not transcription cosmetics alone.

## Follow-up

PR #8 is stacked on this branch and adds the generic Situation Model and read-only Azazel adapter foundation.

items.title: fix: stop rescanning the CA directory on every TLS handshake
items.body:
Touches only `src/`. The benchmark harness these numbers come from is in **#35**, which should land first.

## What

`ngx_http_ffi_client_ssl_ctx()` called `SSL_CTX_set_default_verify_paths()` unconditionally. That registers the hashed CA directory as `X509_FILETYPE_DEFAULT`, and with `DEFAULT` OpenSSL enumerates the **whole directory on every handshake** rather than opening the single `<hash>.N` file the lookup actually needs.

Found by profiling `tlsshort` (fresh connection per request over TLS), the one shape in the matrix where this client lost to `lua-resty-http`.

## Evidence

`perf diff` between the two clients, sampling the pinned target worker — every top delta entry is kernel directory-reading, all of it on our side:

```
Baseline  Delta Abs  Symbol
           +2.04%  [k] filldir64
           +2.01%  [k] ext4_htree_store_dirent
           +1.82%  [k] str2hashbuf_signed
           +1.76%  [k] half_md4_transform
           +1.05%  [k] htree_dirblock_to_tree
```

|  | C FFI | lua-resty-http |
|---|---:|---:|
| CPU in directory-lookup code | 11.83% | 0.42% |
| CPU in the kernel overall | 36.7% | 17.9% |

Confirmed at the syscall level: **2132 `openat` + 4264 `getdents64` for ~2168 requests**, one full sweep of a 245-entry directory per handshake. The same trace against `lua-resty-http` caught zero.

Reproduced independently of this module, with `openssl s_client` against the benchmark upstream:

```
default_verify_paths     getdents64=4
explicit -CAfile bundle  getdents64=0
explicit -CApath dir     getdents64=0
```

Explicit `CApath` still verifies correctly (return code 0) when the issuer is present, so it is the filetype that costs — not hash-dir lookup, and not lookup failure.

## The fix

1. Install the trust store by hand as `X509_FILETYPE_PEM`, honouring `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR` the way OpenSSL does. **A verifying caller no longer pays the sweep either.**
2. Don't install it at all unless the caller asked to verify. OpenSSL checks the chain during every handshake regardless of verify mode, but the handshake handler only reads the result when `ssl_verify` is set — for everyone else the store was pure waste.
3. Key the context cache on the verify flag as well as the CA path, since a verify-off context carries no store and would fail every chain a verify-on request handed it.

## Result

Median of 5 saturated repeats, target worker pinned to one core, upstream and load generator on separate cores:

| shape | before | after | vs lua-resty-http |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `tlsshort` | 932 | **1257** req/s | **1.10x** (was 0.81x) |
| `tls` | 18655 | 18276 req/s | 1.53x |
| `tlsverify` *(new)* | — | 17543 req/s | 1.48x |
| `tlsverifyshort` *(new)* | — | 1229 req/s | 1.08x |

Zero `openat`/`getdents64` per handshake afterwards, verify **on and off**.

## Tests

All 447 pass, including `t/004-tls.t` TEST 4, which asserts verification still *rejects* an untrusted self-signed cert — so the store is genuinely loaded, not silently disabled.

The matrix had never exercised `ssl_verify = true` (all four call sites in `bench.lua` hardcoded `false`). New `tlsverify` and `tlsverifyshort` cases close that gap, so the verifying path in change 1 ships measured rather than assumed. Both clients trust the same self-signed upstream cert — the FFI client via `ssl_trusted_certificate`, `lua-resty-http` via `lua_ssl_trusted_certificate`, since it has no per-request trust store.

## Known gaps

- **The READMEs still carry pre-fix numbers**, including a `ffi.stateful` p99.9 claim of 20.94 ms that a later 3-repeat run disproved (actual: 2.730 ms vs `resty.stateful`'s 3.320 ms). It was flagged at the time as single-sample and not yet evidence. Corrected data for the whole matrix is in `benchmark/results-full.md`; re-baselining the READMEs is deliberately left to a follow-up.
- **The FFI short-TLS cases intermittently miss the fixed latency-phase rate** by ~2% despite ~40% CPU headroom, which coordinated-omission correction reports as a ~7x latency blowup. `lua-resty-http` hits the target every time. Throughput is unaffected and stable across all 5 repeats. Unexplained; no latency claim is made for those shapes here.

## Note on scope

The first commit is the benchmark harness this finding came out of — both columns of every comparison are now generated from one shape table, so fairness is structural rather than reviewed. It was already uncommitted in the tree and the new TLS cases depend on it. The fix itself is the second commit and touches only `src/`.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved TLS client context caching to correctly distinguish certificate verification settings.
  * Enhanced certificate verification by loading configured and platform trust stores explicitly.
  * TLS initialization now reports an error when no default trusted certificate source is available.
  * Disabled certificate verification no longer loads unnecessary trust stores.
  * Improved reliability by preventing TLS configurations with different verification behavior from sharing cached contexts.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

items.title: docs: claims honesty audit — refresh stale test counts and add a verified-claims policy
items.body:
Advances #423.

## What changed and why

A claims-honesty audit of the documents #423 names. Most of the specific defects
the issue lists have already been fixed by later work, so the diff is limited to
the two things that are still wrong or missing today.

**1. `docs/Testing_and_Gym.md` — stale regression baseline.**
The paragraph claimed "as verified on 2026-07-10 ... 2,874 passing unit tests in
95 files". Measured at `main` (`332c48d`) today: **3,010 passing unit tests in
100 files**. Replaced with the measured figure, the command that produced it, an
explicit note that the old number was stale, and a reminder that these counts are
volatile engineering snapshots that stay out of user-facing copy (per the
existing `CONTRIBUTING.md` rule on exact counts).

**2. `CONTRIBUTING.md` — verified-claims policy.**
Added the one-paragraph policy #423 asks for, at the head of the existing
"Claims and evidence" section: no user-facing protection claim without a
committed measurement artifact or a CI-verified fixture behind it, and a
`docs/Project_Roadmap.md` gate checkbox only when that task's own **Done when**
text is literally true today (a partially met gate stays unchecked with a dated
note rather than being checked with a caveat).

## What the audit found already correct — deliberately left alone

Each of these was checked in this worktree, not assumed:

- **Bloom / threat-feed claim.** `README.md` no longer claims known-bad-domain
  protection "compiled from public threat feeds (URLhaus, OpenPhish)", and neither
  does `docs/cws-listing/STORE_LISTING.md`. #321 landed via PR #509; the default
  profile in `config/release-profiles.json` is `interaction-only` with
  `reputation: false` and `releaseEligible: true`, `research-reputation` is
  `releaseEligible: false`, and `scripts/package.mjs` calls
  `inspectBuiltReleaseProfile(..., { requireReleaseEligible: true })`. The README's
  wording matches that. Remaining URLhaus/OpenPhish mentions are in research,
  corpus-tooling and historical-analysis docs describing build-time/corpus feeds,
  not user-facing protection claims.
- **Roadmap gate boxes.** All three boxes #423 names are **already unchecked**
  with justifying notes, so there was nothing to un-check:
  - P1-05 re-run — `docs/Project_Roadmap.md` L563, unchecked, and already
    corrected to "Tranco top-**200**" with the 0.72%/never-re-measured caveat.
  - P2-10 competitive arm — L902, unchecked, notes `benchmark.mjs` has no Safe
    Browsing arm, baseline `lastRun` is `null`, `tests/benchmark-results/` holds
    only `.gitkeep` (#418).
  - P3-06 CWS listing — L1164, unchecked; the P3-06 detail section already flags
    the "only browser extension that detects…" headline as an unevidenced
    superlative that must not ship.
  I therefore made **no change to `docs/Project_Roadmap.md`**, which also keeps
  this PR off PR #514's lines in that file.
- **CWS store copy.** `docs/STORE_LISTING.md` is only a pointer. In
  `docs/cws-listing/STORE_LISTING.md` I verified the substantive claims against
  code: "3 consecutive allow decisions" (`SMART_DEFAULT_THRESHOLD = 3` in
  `smart_defaults.ts`), known-redirector detection (`redirect_chain.ts`),
  punycode/IDN and mixed-script signals (`domain.ts`), local prompt-outcome
  records with scores/reason codes/timestamps (`PromptOutcomeEntry` in
  `storage.ts`), and "fully open source" (repo visibility is PUBLIC). No
  superlative or competitive claim appears in the listing copy. No edit needed.
- **README capability claims.** DoubleClickjacking across MAIN / isolated /
  service-worker layers is real (`main_guard.ts`, `capture_isolated.ts`,
  `sw/sw.ts`). "No runtime network lookup in the opt-in reputation research
  build" holds: the only `fetch` in `reputation_runtime.enabled.ts` targets
  `chrome.runtime.getURL("reputation_data.bin")`. Gym claims check out —
  `level1`…`level12` fixtures exist and RW fixtures run `rw01`…`rw25`.
- **`docs/Project_Overview.md`.** Found no over-claim. It is *narrower* than what
  ships (its capability list omits ClickFix, DoubleClickjacking, redirect-chain
  and pushState detection), which is an under-description, not a honesty defect;
  expanding it would be adding claims, the opposite of this issue. Left for a
  separate slice. Its one stale line (L73, dead visual-sim path) is already
  rewritten by PR #514.

Because those items are already true, this PR **advances** #423 rather than
closing it: the remaining work under that issue is a judgement call about whether
`Project_Overview.md` should be broadened, which is not a claims correction.

## Overlap with PR #514

PR #514 (`fix/ri02-excise-visual-sim`) edits `README.md`,
`docs/Project_Roadmap.md`, `docs/Project_Overview.md`, `docs/Product_Strategy.md`
and other `docs/` files. I read `gh pr diff 514` before editing and **this PR
touches none of those files** — only `docs/Testing_and_Gym.md` and
`CONTRIBUTING.md`, neither of which appears in #514's file list. There is no
file-level, let alone line-level, overlap, so the two merge independently in
either order.

## Verification

Run in the worktree at branch head `41be977`, full output redirected to a file
and the exit code captured explicitly (not inferred from a pipe or wrapper):

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx vitest run --reporter=dot` | **exit 0** — `Test Files 100 passed (100)`, `Tests 3010 passed (3010)`, 24.99s |
| `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` | **exit 0**, no output |
| `npx eslint extension/src/ tests/` | **exit 0**, no output |

The vitest figure above is the measurement this PR writes into the doc; it was
taken on the tree at `332c48d` before the doc edits, and re-running tsc/eslint
after the edits also returned exit 0. Supporting facts (file counts, profile
config, source symbols) were read directly from the files cited above.

## NOT verified

- No `npm run build`, no Playwright lane (`test:e2e`, `:rollback`, `:stress`,
  `:corpus`), no `check:perf-budget`, no `check:release-profile`,
  no `package:ext`, no `measure:fp`.
- No real Chrome session; no manual UI check.
- The **14 Playwright spec files** figure is a file count (`tests/e2e/*.spec.ts`),
  not a passing-test count — the doc states it that way.
- I did not re-derive the merged-PR provenance behind every *checked* roadmap box
  (e.g. "PR #64 merged"); I spot-checked the ones with a cheap local proof
  (nightly stress cron in `.github/workflows/stress.yml`, `scripts/release.mjs`,
  property tests, PSL data) and all held.
- Hosted CI on this PR has not run yet at the time of writing.

## Residual risk

Low, and documentation-only — no runtime code, manifest, build script or test was
touched, so shipped browser behaviour is unchanged. The residual risks are
(a) the test counts are a dated snapshot and will drift again — the paragraph now
says so explicitly and the new policy keeps such counts out of user-facing copy;
and (b) this audit asserts the *absence* of over-claims in README/STORE_LISTING/
Project_Overview based on targeted verification of each substantive claim rather
than an exhaustive line-by-line proof, so a reviewer may still find a claim I did
not enumerate.

Gate-3: not required

items.title: Slim the README to setup and a capability overview
items.body:
The README had grown to **1,336 lines**. Everything past the quickstart was
reference material — a 690-line capability guide, the full CLI reference, the
module call graph, troubleshooting, the security model — so the two things a
newcomer actually needs (install it, see what it does) were buried under
sections nobody reads top to bottom.

**README is now 209 lines.** No content was deleted; the reference sections
moved into `docs/` and are linked from an index.

## What the README keeps

What it is · the evidence · install · quickstart · mental model · a
one-line-per-feature table · a command table · dashboard · CI · a
documentation index · scope.

## What moved (verbatim)

| New file | Was |
|---|---|
| `docs/capabilities.md` | "Capability guide" (690 lines) |
| `docs/cli.md` | "Command reference" |
| `docs/codebase.md` | "Codebase guide" |
| `docs/development.md` | "Development and testing" + "Generate the evaluation results" |
| `docs/troubleshooting.md` | "Troubleshooting" |
| `docs/security.md` | "Security model" + "Supported clients" |

Wording is unchanged; only heading levels were promoted (`###` → `##`) now
that each is its own document. `docs/README.md` is restructured by task —
using it, shipping it, working on it, boundaries — instead of one flat list.

The old "Current limitations" list turned out to be fully duplicated by
`docs/limitations.md` already, so it was dropped rather than copied a second
time.

## Three corrections made while moving

Each of these was a claim the repository does not support:

**The headline number is measured, not inherited.** The planning doc's "0.62s"
was carried into the README unverified. Measured over four runs: a warm replay
of the checked-in cassette is ~0.6s against 32.0s recorded, but the first run
is ~2.9s cold. Stated as warm so it reproduces.

**The byte-identical claim now separates what CI proves from what it doesn't.**
CI asserts the workspace and stdout hashes — but it rebuilds the image, so the
image ID differs and `replay.yml` passes `--allow-image-mismatch`. Strict image
identity is a local `REPLAYABLE_STRICT_IMAGE=1` opt-in. The previous text
implied CI checked both, which is exactly the overstatement the build plan
warned about ("green in CI must not quietly become a weaker claim than it
reads").

**"Current limitations" was stale.** It said M5/M6 acceptance evidence was
still outstanding. The golden cassette is checked in and its acceptance suite
passes. What is genuinely missing is `results/` — the 100-run determinism proof
and the cost benchmark are generated from a real recording rather than
committed. `docs/limitations.md` now says that instead.

## One footgun fixed

The no-API-key path now tells you to copy the fixture first:

```sh
cp -R tests/fixtures/cassettes/research-agent /tmp/demo-cassette
chmod -R u+w /tmp/demo-cassette
uv run replayable replay --cassette /tmp/demo-cassette --strict
```

Replay writes its report, logs, and transcripts *into* the cassette directory,
and `tests/fixtures/cassettes/` is tracked — so the obvious version of that
command dirties the repo. Ran the block above verbatim: exits 0, prints
`DETERMINISTIC ✓`, leaves the fixture clean.

## Checks

- `tests/test_docs.py` link checker green — it caught one link (`docs/cli.md`
  → `docs/dashboard/README.md`) that broke when the file moved down a level.
- 303 unit tests, 10 skipped.
- `ruff check .` clean.
- README internal anchors verified against its own headings.

## Review note

Worth a skim of the README top-to-bottom for tone, and a spot-check that the
capability table's one-liners match what `docs/capabilities.md` says in full.
The moved files are pure content transplants — `git diff` will show them as
new, but they are line-for-line the old README sections.

## PR Type

- [x] Spec only

## What

Updates the normative GH935 product and technical contracts for completing the
Claude Code ↔ Codex cross-host continuity benchmark.

- preserves the current truth: 24 skeleton tasks, no live runs, no report, and
  no public conclusion;
- defines the executable `cross-host-v2` task matrix, one-source/many-condition
  sealing, same-path project identity, source-native import pairing, typed
  partial evidence, and deterministic hash-bound reporting;
- makes the current single-user production limitation explicit instead of
  reporting an untestable wrong-user metric as zero;
- closes the native-neutral import lineage, maintained-export cycle state,
  SQLCipher sidecar/key lifecycle, pre-action causal evidence, and exact
  multiplicity-adjusted bootstrap/verdict contracts;
- pre-registers either an action-before-use signal or an exact same-state
  counterfactual for every causal stop-loss rule; Stop-created usage/citation
  rows are post-action corroboration only, and missing/conflicting proof makes
  the comparative verdict `INSUFFICIENT` unless an identity-valid, otherwise
  complete direction already proves a conservative stop-loss breach;
- fixes the directional `memory_hurt` denominator at all 36 registered pairs,
  so missing or invalid evidence never shrinks the denominator;
- defines a sealed-snapshot `remem import claude-memories` dry-run/apply
  boundary with per-record lineage, plus immutable hash-bound source-attempt
  records for failures before a Source Seal;
- restores numeric `wrong_user_injection > 0` as a zero-tolerance security
  failure once the production user-scope prerequisite exists;
- requires each registered foreign-project canary to return the typed
