items.title: feat(speculative): opt-in acceptance-optimal rejection sampling, and a premise correction

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: New features, capabilities, or significant additions

items.body:
## Summary

Adds modified rejection sampling as an **opt-in** acceptance rule for the classic speculative path (`MLXCEL_SPECULATIVE_STOCHASTIC_ACCEPT=1`, default off), together with the proof, the regression guards, the closed-form diagnostic, and a correction to the issue's premise that changes what this issue should be understood to be asking for.

## The premise correction, and why it changes the ask

Issue #902 states that the verify loop "accepts a draft token iff it equals the target model's argmax", and that this biases the output at `temperature > 0`. **For the path the issue's line numbers point at, that is not true.**

`SpeculativeGenerator` selects the target token with `sample_token_optimized(pos_logits, target_sampling, history)`, a fresh draw from the target *sampler*, which is `argmax` only at `temperature == 0`. It emits that draw on **both** branches: the drafted token on acceptance (equal to the draw by the accept test) and the draw itself on rejection. Every emitted token is therefore a fresh conditional draw from the target, and the stream was already exactly a target-only sample. Call this rule *sampler-match*. It was never biased; what it loses is acceptance rate, `sum_x p(x) q(x)`.

This is measured, not argued: `the_default_sampler_match_rule_also_matches_the_target_distribution` passes the same chi-square that rejects argmax-against-argmax at ~1825.

The biased rule the issue describes is real, but it lives in `Gemma4MtpTargetAdapter::verify_forward` (`argmax_per_position`, `src/models/gemma4_mtp_target.rs:655`) and the DFlash round loop (`argmax_logits_to_array`, `drafter/dflash/round_loop.rs:728`), both regardless of `sampler.temperature`. Neither is changed here.

## The acceptance ceiling: why "strictly improves vs argmax" is unachievable

For a `q`-distributed proposal and a `p`-distributed emission, the largest probability the two can coincide is `sum_x min(p(x), q(x))` — the maximal-coupling bound, equivalently `1 - TV(p, q)`. **Every distribution-preserving rule is capped there.**

| Rule | Lossless | Acceptance probability |
|------|----------|------------------------|
| Sampler-match (the default, pre-#902) | yes | `sum_x p(x) q(x)` |
| Modified rejection sampling (this PR, opt-in) | yes | `sum_x min(p(x), q(x))` — the ceiling |
| Argmax-against-argmax (MTP, DFlash) | **no** | `q(argmax p)` — not bounded by the ceiling |

Since `min(a, b) >= a * b` on `[0, 1]`, rejection sampling always accepts at least as often as sampler-match. But `q(argmax p)` is under no such constraint: with `p(a) = 0.3` and `q(a) = 0.95` the argmax rule accepts at 0.95 where the ceiling for any correct rule is about 0.30.

So the reviewer's reading is correct and I agree with it: **no implementation can make a distribution-preserving rule strictly improve mean accepted length against argmax acceptance.** That is not a defect to fix, it is the price of unbiasedness, and it means the issue's required outcome is unachievable as literally written. Read against sampler-match — the rule this generator actually ran — the improvement is real and provable, and that is what the tests assert.

## Recommendation: opt-in, not default

Modified rejection sampling is **off by default** in this PR. `MLXCEL_SPECULATIVE_STOCHASTIC_ACCEPT=1` enables it; `SpeculativeGenerator::with_stochastic_acceptance(bool)` overrides programmatically.

The reasoning: on the only path this rule reaches, the rule it replaces was already distribution-preserving, so it buys acceptance rate and nothing else. The available gain is exactly `sum_x min(p, q) / sum_x p(x) q(x)`, and that ratio collapses toward 1 whenever the drafter is confident, because `q(t*) ~ 1` makes `min(p, q)` and `p * q` coincide. Measured at ~1.02 on a Llama-3.1-8B / Llama-3.2-1B pair at temperature 0.7. Two extra full-vocabulary passes and an extra host sync per verified position do not pay for two percent of theoretical acceptance.

This follows `MLXCEL_FUSED_QK_NORM` (#326) and the #905 fusions in this same epic: the machinery, the proof and the tests land and are available, and the default does not move until a measurement justifies it. The place this rule earns its default is a verify path whose current rule is genuinely biased — MTP and DFlash — where it would buy correctness rather than only acceptance rate, and where trading acceptance for unbiasedness is a real decision.

With the env default off, every distributional test would have silently stopped exercising this module, which is exactly how #899 nearly shipped a dead path. The programmatic override exists so the tests force the rule explicitly, and `stochastic_runs_report_the_stochastic_rule_and_a_longer_accepted_run` fails if a run reports anything but `rule=stochastic`.

## A separate bug this work uncovered: #994

The draft KV cache rewind trims `min(rejected + 1, n)` where the correct trim is `rejected - 1`. At `accepted == 0` the draft cache does not advance at all, so the drafter proposes from a frozen prefix while the target advances, in a self-reinforcing loop. It predates #902, affects every acceptance rule identically, and is the most likely explanation for measured acceptance of 0.12-0.46 on an 8B/1B pair against the 0.6-0.8 reported upstream. It also makes any speculative A/B on this path noisy: two 200-token runs produced `closed_form_sum_min` of 0.221 and 0.396 on the same model pair.

Filed as #994 with the derivation. `draft_cache_falls_behind_the_main_cache_every_round_pre_existing_defect` pins the current wrong behavior so a fix produces a failing test rather than silence. Not fixed here: it changes token streams at every temperature and needs its own parity story.

## What changed

`src/lib/mlxcel-core/cpp/mlx_cxx_bridge.cpp` — the filter chain of `fused_sample_impl` (temperature scale, top-k, top-p, min-p) is extracted into `fused_sample_filter_logits`, and a new `fused_sample_probs` runs that same chain and returns `softmax(...)` in float32 instead of drawing. The effective distribution is therefore derived from the sampler's own code rather than reimplemented next to it, so it cannot drift. A greedy configuration (`temperature == 0` or `top_k == 1`) returns the one-hot argmax indicator, which is the degenerate `q` a greedily-proposing drafter needs. Float32 is deliberate: the caller reads single entries back to the host and compares them against a uniform draw, and an f16 probability underflows below ~6e-8, turning a legitimately small acceptance ratio into an unconditional accept.

`src/lib/mlxcel-core/src/sampling.rs` — the pre-sampler steps (last-position slice, token bias, repetition / DRY / frequency-presence penalties, XTC) are split out of `sample_token_optimized_core` into `preprocess_logits_for_sampling`, with no behavior change. Two new public functions build on it: `effective_token_distribution` returns `p` or `q` for a given logits/config/history triple and consumes no randomness, and `sample_token_with_distribution` returns a token together with the distribution it was drawn from from a single pre-step, which is what guarantees `q` is the actual proposal distribution rather than a later reconstruction.

`src/lib/mlxcel-core/src/speculative/stochastic_accept.rs` (new) — `acceptance_rule`, `accept_draft_token`, `residual_resample`, `verify_draft_token`, the kill switch and the one-shot info logging. The module header carries the losslessness proof and the reason it holds for any proposal `q`. The accept test is `p(t) > 0 && u * q(t) <= p(t)`; the first conjunct is load-bearing, not cosmetic, because a `q(t)` that has underflowed float32 to zero would otherwise make the product test read `0 <= 0` and accept a token the target's own filter excluded. The residual draw goes through `ffi::fused_sample(log(relu(p - q)), 1.0, 0, 1.0, 0.0)`, so `softmax(log r) == r / sum(r)` is the normalized residual by construction and the draw reuses the #900 Gumbel-max kernel where the backend supports it.

`src/lib/mlxcel-core/src/speculative/mod.rs` — the verify loop dispatches on the rule. On the stochastic arm the draft loop captures `q` per position (left unevaluated, so a chain rejected early never materializes the tail) and the verify loop builds `p` at each position from the history including the tokens accepted so far in the round. Both arms produce the same `(accept, replacement)` pair, so all the downstream bookkeeping, EOS handling and cache rewind is shared and unchanged. New `SpeculativeAcceptanceStats` counts rounds, proposals and acceptances.

Docs: `docs/speculative-acceptance.md` (new), `MLXCEL_SPECULATIVE_STOCHASTIC_ACCEPT` in `docs/environment-variables.md`, links from `README.md`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/architecture.md`.

## The distributional argument, and how the test verifies it

**Null hypothesis.** The token stream emitted by `SpeculativeGenerator::generate` at `temperature > 0` is distributed identically to sampling the target model alone at the same temperature.

**Why the test can check it directly.** The test target model's logits do not depend on its input, so target-only sampling emits i.i.d. draws from one known categorical `p = softmax(target_logits / 0.7)`. Under H0 every token the speculative generator emits, whatever mixture of accepted drafts, residual resamples and bonus tokens produced it, is also an i.i.d. draw from that same `p`, so a Pearson goodness-of-fit test against `p` tests H0 directly rather than by proxy.

**Statistic, samples, threshold.** Pearson chi-square over a 6-entry vocabulary, `dof = 5`. The committed default draws **12000 emitted tokens** (`SAMPLE_TOKENS`, overridable with `MLXCEL_SPEC_DIST_SAMPLES`); the `num_draft = 1` companion test draws half that. Rejected above **25.7448**, the upper-tail quantile at `alpha = 1e-4`, so a correct implementation fails one run in ten thousand.

**Demonstrated power, not assumed power.** `chi_square_rejects_known_wrong_acceptance_rules` replays the same statistic against two deliberately wrong rules and requires rejection. Measured on this branch at n = 4000 verify positions: correct rule **4.88**, "resample from `p` instead of the residual" **136.48**, argmax-against-argmax **1825.13**, threshold **25.7448**. The middle arm is the specific mistake a naive implementation makes, and it is detected with a five-fold margin at a quarter of the end-to-end sample count.

**Where chi-square is blind, zero-tolerance assertions cover.** A goodness-of-fit test cannot see a single wrong token, so: `filtered_target_support_is_never_violated` runs a `top_k = 2` target against an unfiltered drafter over 1500 emitted tokens and fails on the **first** token outside the target's two-token support (exactly what a missing `p(t) > 0` conjunct produces); `tokens_outside_the_target_support_are_never_accepted` and `underflowed_proposal_mass_does_not_bypass_the_target_support` assert the same property on the primitive over 400 and 200 trials with no tolerance; `residual_draw_follows_the_normalized_relu_difference` fails if the residual ever emits a token with `p <= q`; and the temperature-0 test fails on one differing token.

## Temperature 0

`acceptance_rule` returns `Argmax` whenever the target sampler is greedy (`temperature == 0.0` or `top_k == 1`, matching the C++ sampler's own short-circuit, pinned by `sampler_is_greedy_matches_fused_sampler_short_circuit`). On that arm no distribution tensor is built, no randomness is drawn, and the pre-existing comparison runs verbatim. `temperature_zero_stream_is_byte_identical_to_greedy_target_only` walks a deterministic 6-cycle target against two drafters (one agreeing on one token in six, one never agreeing) at `num_draft` 1, 2 and 4, and asserts the emitted vector equals the target's own greedy continuation exactly.

## Proving from a log which rule ran

Both lines are at **info**. The first time a process runs each distinct rule it logs `speculative acceptance rule active rule="stochastic (modified rejection sampling)" distribution_preserving=true`; the latch is per rule kind, not one global flag, so a process that serves a greedy request and later a `temperature > 0` one logs both lines. The other three labels are `argmax (greedy target sampler)`, `argmax (stochastic acceptance disabled by env)` and `argmax (drafter reported no proposal distribution)`. The first occurrence of each per-token outcome is logged the same way (accept, residual resample, and the degenerate residual fallback). Every `generate` call then logs `speculative decode finished rule=Stochastic rounds=.. proposed_draft_tokens=.. accepted_draft_tokens=.. acceptance_rate=.. mean_accepted_len=.. generated_tokens=..`, which is both the A/B measurement and the proof of which arm produced it. `stochastic_runs_report_the_stochastic_rule_and_a_longer_accepted_run` fails if a `temperature > 0` run reports anything other than `Stochastic`.

## Kill switch

`MLXCEL_SPECULATIVE_STOCHASTIC_ACCEPT=0` (also `false`, `no`, `off`, case- and whitespace-insensitive) restores the previous rule at every temperature, read once per process.

## RNG

The accept test draws one `U[0,1)` per verified position and the residual draws one categorical per rejection, both through MLX's default key sequence, so `--seed` still reproduces a run exactly. But the stream is consumed differently than before, so **at an equal seed the emitted tokens differ from a pre-change run** even though the distribution is identical (the same relationship `MLXCEL_SAMPLING_GUMBEL` has). Set the kill switch to reproduce a stream recorded before this landed. Documented in `docs/speculative-acceptance.md` and the env-var table.

## Observability: how to prove which rule ran

The `mlxcel` CLI installs no `tracing` subscriber, so info-level instrumentation is discarded on the only binary that runs `SpeculativeGenerator`. Every speculative run therefore prints an unconditional **stdout** summary:

```
[Speculative acceptance] rule=stochastic rounds=153 proposed=612 positions_tested=195 accepted=46 per_position_acceptance=0.2359 acceptance_rate=0.0752 mean_accepted_len=0.3007 (stochastic (modified rejection sampling))
```

`rule=` is a stable, whitespace-free, greppable id: `greedy-argmax`, `sampler-match`, `stochastic`, `sampler-match-no-proposal-distribution`. Its shape is pinned by `cli_summary_line_carries_the_rule_id_and_mean_accepted_len`. Setting `RUST_LOG` additionally installs a subscriber for the offline CLI commands (stderr, so piped stdout stays clean); default output is unchanged when it is unset, and `Serve` is skipped because the server installs its own.

## Two metric corrections found by making it visible

**`acceptance_rate` is the wrong metric for an A/B.** It is `accepted / proposed`, but a chain stops at its first rejection and never tests the block positions behind it, so `proposed` is not the denominator theory predicts against. On a real Llama 8B/1B pair this made a correct implementation read as a 2x regression (0.059 stochastic vs 0.119 kill-switch). `positions_tested` is now counted identically on both rules and `per_position_acceptance` is reported beside it. On the same runs that reads 0.2359 vs its own closed form 0.2213: correct.

**The drafter-kind line was misleading.** With no explicit `--draft-kind`, the CLI printed the kind auto-detected from the drafter's `config.json` (usually `dflash`) and then ignored it and ran the classic `SpeculativeGenerator` anyway, so a benchmark run was indistinguishable from a DFlash round-loop run. The path actually taken is now printed:

```
Resolved drafter kind: dflash (block_size = 16, default)
Drafter kind was auto-detected only; running the classic SpeculativeGenerator path (pass --draft-kind explicitly to select a kind-specific round loop).
```

Passing `--draft-kind` explicitly does not give you a DFlash round loop here; it returns an error saying the offline path does not construct one.

## Verifying the gain before trusting a throughput number

`MLXCEL_SPECULATIVE_ACCEPT_DIAG=1` adds `closed_form_sum_min` (`sum_x min(p, q)`, what modified rejection sampling accepts) and `closed_form_sum_prod` (`sum_x p(x) q(x)`, what the old rule accepts), averaged over the positions the run actually tested, and makes the argmax arm capture `q` so both halves of an A/B report the same quantity. Because `min(a, b) >= a * b` on `[0, 1]`, `sum_min >= sum_prod` holds for every pair of distributions, so the two numbers convert an acceptance anomaly into an arithmetic statement: the measured per-position rate must sit at `sum_min`, and `sum_min` can never fall below `sum_prod`. Off by default (two full-vocabulary reductions per tested position).

Measured on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-4bit with a Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct drafter, 200 tokens, `--num-draft-tokens 4`, one trajectory per row:

| Temperature | `closed_form_sum_min` | `closed_form_sum_prod` | Ratio | measured `per_position_acceptance` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.7 | 0.2808 | 0.2740 | 1.02x | 0.2902 |
| 1.0 | 0.1738 | 0.1613 | 1.08x | 0.1735 |
| 1.5 | 0.6809 | 0.0494 | 13.8x | 0.6966 |

The measured value sits on `sum_min` at every temperature: that is the correctness result, and it is the strongest evidence in this PR that the accept test is right on real models rather than only on synthetic ones. The **ratio** column is the throughput headroom, and on this pair at 0.7 there is essentially none, because `sum_x min(p, q)` collapses onto `sum_x p(x) q(x)` whenever the drafter is near-deterministic (`q(t*) ~ 1` makes `min(p(t*), q(t*)) = p(t*)` and `p(t*) q(t*) ~ p(t*)`). The gain appears when `q` is diffuse. Between-trajectory variance is also large: two 200-token runs at 0.7 differed by nearly 2x in `sum_min`, so a single short run there measures noise, not the change. Read `sum_min / sum_prod` first; it bounds what any throughput measurement can show. The 1.5 row is a real measurement of the mechanism but comes from a degenerate high-temperature trajectory where both models agree on repetitive text, so it is not a production number.

## How to run the throughput benchmark

Throughput timings were not run here, by instruction. The classic `SpeculativeGenerator` is reachable only from the offline CLI (`src/server/speculative_dispatch.rs:41` records that the server does not use it), so the A/B is `mlxcel generate --draft-model`, with the kill switch selecting the arm:

`MLXCEL_SPECULATIVE_ACCEPT_DIAG=1 ./target/release/mlxcel generate -m models/<target> --draft-model models/<draft> --num-draft-tokens 4 --temp 0.7 --seed 1234 -n 256 -p "<prompt>"` for the default (sampler-match) arm, and the same command with `MLXCEL_SPECULATIVE_STOCHASTIC_ACCEPT=1` for the opt-in arm. Confirm `rule=argmax-kill-switch` vs `rule=stochastic`, then compare `per_position_acceptance` and `mean_accepted_len`. At `--temp 0.0` both arms must produce identical output and identical `rule=greedy-argmax`.

**Do not measure this change with `speculative_bench`.** Every pairing it benches is MTP or DFlash, which this PR does not touch, so a before/after would compare the unchanged fallback against itself and produce a clean-looking null. `docs/speculative-acceptance.md` says this explicitly so the next person does not repeat it.

## What this PR does not do

Task 1 of the issue (expose draft probabilities on `Drafter`, `speculative/mtp/`, `drafter/dflash`, `drafter/gemma4_assistant`) and the MTP/DFlash half of task 3 are **not implemented**. `Drafter::draft_block` returns `Vec<i32>` and `MtpTarget::verify_forward` returns `VerifyForwardOutput { target_tokens: Vec<i32>, .. }`; the target logits are a local inside `Gemma4MtpTargetAdapter::verify_forward` that is dropped at the end of the function, and `MtpBatchedVerifyForwardOutput` has no logprobs field at all. Wiring stochastic acceptance there means widening both traits and every implementor, on the perf-critical deferred-greedy path, with no Gemma 4 or DFlash checkpoint available in this environment to validate against. Adding that surface without a consumer that can be exercised is how #899 shipped a path that never activated, so it is deliberately left out and recorded in `docs/speculative-acceptance.md`'s per-path table instead. The `ArgmaxNoProposalDistribution` rule variant exists so those paths have a correct, logged answer when they are wired.

The `mtp_policy` half of task 3 needs no change: `MtpBurstProfile::from_summary` consumes `MtpAcceptanceSummary`, which `MtpRoundDiagnostics::record_round` fills from the MTP walk's own accepted counts. That plumbing is untouched and keeps working; had the MTP path been converted, its higher acceptance profile would flow through the same counters with no code change.

The issue's `docs/benchmark_results/chain-speculative-acceptance-<hw>-<date>.md` is not written, because writing a results file without having run the benchmark would be fabrication.

**CUDA is unvalidated.** No CUDA hardware and no `nvcc` in this environment. `fused_sample_probs` uses only backend-agnostic MLX ops and inherits `fused_sample`'s existing `single_dtype_scalars` (non-Metal) branch through the shared filter chain, but nothing on the CUDA path was compiled or run.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --release -p mlxcel-core --lib --features metal,accelerate speculative::` — 95 passed, 0 failed.
- [x] `cargo test --release --test speculative_parity --features metal,accelerate` — passed.
- [x] `cargo check --release --lib --tests --features metal,accelerate` — clean.
- [x] `cargo test --release -p mlxcel-core --lib --features metal,accelerate` — 1285 passed, 1 failed (pre-existing #964; baseline was 1250+1).
- [x] `cargo clippy --release -p mlxcel-core --lib --tests --features metal,accelerate -- -D warnings` — clean.
- [x] `cargo clippy --release --bin mlxcel --features metal,accelerate -- -D warnings` — clean.
- [x] End-to-end CLI check on a real Llama 8B/1B pair: all three arms print distinct `rule=` ids (`stochastic`, `sampler-match`, `argmax-greedy`) and the diagnostic confirms measured per-position acceptance sits at `sum_min` at temperatures 0.7, 1.0 and 1.5.
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- [x] `python3 scripts/ci/check_cross_repo_refs.py` — exit 0.
- [ ] Throughput A/B at temperatures 0.0 / 0.7 / 1.0 — deferred to the maintainer per instruction; commands above.

Closes #902

items.title: Add voice engine quality benchmark and 2026-08 results
items.body:
Compares **Azure Voice Live** and **gpt-realtime-2** on the two things a small-business phone agent is actually judged on: did it understand the caller, and did it handle the call. 165 live calls plus 1200 conditioned ASR clips plus a 400-clip noise-suppression teardown, $22.29 spent.

Full write-up: `docs/research/voice-engine-quality-2026-08.md`. Datasets: `docs/research/voice-eval-datasets.md`.

## Recommendation

**Keep `kataleptic-realtime-hd` (Voice Live + gpt-4.1-mini) as the default, and never enable Azure's noise suppression.** Offer gpt-realtime-2 as an opt-in "more capable, slower" tier.

| | Voice Live + gpt-4.1-mini | gpt-realtime-2 |
|---|---|---|
| TTFA p50 / p95 | **1393 / 1654 ms** | 2079–2408 / 3468–3812 ms |
| Slots heard | **0.967** | 0.856–0.933 |
| Slots echoed back | 0.719 | **0.812–0.819** |
| Judge groundedness | 0.667 | **0.939** |
| pass^3 | 0.091 | **0.182–0.273** |
| Cost | **$0.03/min** | $0.07/min |

The two capabilities separate cleanly: Voice Live **hears** better (0.967 vs 0.856; it never lost a phone number) and answers ~690 ms sooner at p50 and two seconds sooner at p95 for 43% of the cost. gpt-realtime-2 **reasons** better — groundedness 0.939 vs 0.667, the largest single gap in the study. One mishears a name; the other invents an opening time.

`vl-native-brain` (Voice Live serving gpt-realtime-2) scores like gpt-realtime-2 on groundedness *and* has the worst p50 of any arm. **The difference is the brain, not the serving stack.**

## Two things worth acting on

- **`input_audio_noise_reduction` makes recognition worse under exactly the noise it exists to remove.** German degrades 6.05 → 7.47 WER at 10 dB cafe noise and 9.84 → 16.84 at 5 dB, with **zero** dropped utterances — so this is recognition damage, not plumbing. On English it *additionally* drops ~24% of utterances outright, even on clean audio. Reproduced at n=50 with the alternative explanations ruled out (locale, truncation, pairing drift, sample rate). `near_field` and `far_field` are byte-identical to off, so only the deep model does anything — and what it does is harmful. OpenFon doesn't set this knob, so this is a "don't turn it on later" finding.
- **`end_call` is unreliable on every arm** (23–27 of 33 runs). The `isFarewell` heuristic and the 15 s DO safety net are load-bearing — don't remove them.

## On recognition, the engines are close

Within one WER point in **12 of 16** language×condition cells. whisper-1 wins more cells (10/16) but by small margins (max 1.17 pt); azure-speech wins 6 but wins them big — including **20.5% vs 34.5% at 0 dB cafe noise in German**. On clean and moderately degraded audio there is no meaningful difference and the choice should not be made on WER.

## Review round 2 — fixture hygiene and scoring tests

- **Fixture phone numbers replaced** with ranges reserved for fiction (BNetzA `0152 288173xx` / `030 23125xxx`, `555-01xx`). Branch was rebuilt and force-pushed so the old Vodafone-prefix number is in no commit. README states plainly that all scenario audio, names and numbers are synthetic; a test fails the build if a fixture number leaves the reserved ranges.
- **Scoring tests added** and wired into CI as a `bench-scoring` job. They caught a time matcher that scored "2 PM" as a miss against `14:00`, and German scripts whose ASCII transliteration (`fuenfzehn`) Azure TTS read aloud as "fuer-enf-zehn" — a fixture defect masquerading as an engine failure. Both fixed by re-running 150 calls.

## Review round 3 — six scoring bugs

All scoring-side, so all corrected by **re-deriving from the existing raw logs — no calls re-run**.

| # | bug | effect on reported numbers |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | clock times compared as text (`normalize("14:00")` = "vierzehn null") | **grounded_ok 147/165 → 159/165**; strict success up on every arm |
| 2 | forbidden claims matched across turn boundaries | the study's **only `forbidden_hit` was a false positive** → 0 |
| 3 | `bargein_correct` read the caller transcript, not the agent | **24/30, not 30/30** — my "3/3 everywhere" claim was wrong |
| 4 | missing judge verdict counted as a pass | now aborts; `--allow-missing-judge` scores as failure |
| 5 | `run_all.sh` omitted `vl-gpt41mini-semvad` | default produced 132 calls vs the report's 165 |
| 6 | `end_call` double-counted on shared `call_id` | **`tool_ok` unchanged** (set comparison) — 23–25/33 stands; judge input cleaned and re-run |

**The corrected numbers widen the quality gap rather than closing it**, so the recommendation now splits by business type:

| | Voice Live + gpt-4.1-mini | gpt-realtime-2 |
|---|---|---|
| Strict success | 0.394 | **0.424–0.606** |
| pass^3 | 0.182 | **0.273–0.545** |
| Judge groundedness | 0.697 | **1.000** |
| TTFA p50 / p95 | **1393 / 1654 ms** | 2079–2408 / 3468–3812 ms |
| Cost | **$0.03/min** | $0.07/min |

gpt-realtime-2 made **zero unsupported claims in 66 runs** against 24 for the Voice Live arms — six of which are the agent promising a specific appointment slot *is available* when the prompt says "Do not promise a confirmed slot." **Keep Voice Live as the default for information-only businesses; route booking businesses to gpt-realtime-2.** `realtime_model` is already per-business, so it's a settings default.

39 tests, all six bugs pinned. Spend $23.19. Typecheck and tests green.

## Review round 4 — four more, and the class behind them

| # | bug | effect |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ttfa_p95_ms` was a percentile of **per-call medians** | **moves in both directions** — VL p95 1654 → **1748**, native 3812 → **3048** |
| 2 | `pass^k` ran `all()` over rows present | two trials satisfied pass^3; missing scenarios left the denominator |
| 3 | empty judge file read as "no judge supplied" | runs passed with zero verdicts |
| 4 | JSON `true` passed as a judge score | `bool` is an `int`; `float(True)` → 0.0 turned a **positive** verdict into a failure |

Per-turn TTFA was recoverable from the existing logs, so #1 is fixed properly rather than renamed. Percentiles are now over 96–106 individual turns per arm.

### The class — four more instances found by audit

You were right that this was a default, not a series of bugs. Auditing every `if x:` guard on a collection, every aggregate over "the rows present", and every vacuous conjunction turned up four beyond the ones reported:

- a run that **errored on the wire** could still satisfy the conjunction
- so could a call the **agent never joined** (zero agent turns)
- an unparseable `forbidden_hit` defaulted to **0** — "no forbidden claim"
- an unparseable `slots_all_heard` defaulted to **1** — "all slots captured"

**Ten places across three rounds, every one pushing the same way.** `summarize.py` now fails closed throughout: validates arm × scenario × k completeness, treats an empty `--judge` as an error, aborts on unparseable conjunction inputs, scores errored and agent-absent runs as failures, and prints `not measured` rather than a blank cell that reads as zero.

**None were firing on the final dataset** — all 165 runs are complete, judged and error-free — so every reported number is unchanged **except the latency percentiles**. The guards exist so the next run can't quietly report a partial one as a good one.

50 tests. `TestAbsentDataNeverPasses` invokes `summarize.py` as a subprocess per case, because what's pinned is that the *run refuses*, not that a helper returns False.

The README's synthetic-data section landed in round 2 (`bench/quality/README.md`, "No real call data is committed") — it names the reserved ranges and the test that enforces them.

## Review round 5 — the sweep's own misses, plus a percentile bug

**The sweep missed two instances of its own class**, because it matched the reported shapes instead of deriving the rule. The rule — *any place where the number of observations can differ from the number expected, and nothing compares the two* — catches both:

- `success_mean` averaged **only the rows present**, so under `--allow-incomplete` two successes out of an expected three reported **1.0**, which is precisely what that flag promises not to do. `pass_k` beside it handled the same gap correctly.
- `run_all.sh` neither stopped nor recorded a runner exiting non-zero, and the trailing `echo` made it exit 0, so a half-finished matrix scored as a whole one.

Re-running the pass against that statement, every aggregate now knows its denominator:

| aggregate | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| `success_mean`, `tool_ok`, `grounded_ok` | mean over rows present | rate over **expected** runs |
| `slot_heard`, `judge_*` | mean over rows present | carries n, flagged when short |
| `ttfa_*` | — | no a-priori denominator (a turn only yields a latency if the agent replied); run-level completeness carries it |
| `score_asr.py` | **no completeness check at all** | validates every (arm, lang, condition) cell, emits `complete` |
| `run_all.sh` | exit 0 regardless | collects failures, exits non-zero, says INCOMPLETE |

**Two more:**

- **`round()` is not nearest-rank.** Banker's rounding selects rank 20 of 20 and 96 of 100 where nearest-rank selects 19 and 95. Now `ceil(q*n) - 1`. The arms have 96–106 turns where `q*n` is non-integral, so **no published latency figure moves** — but at n=100 it would have. (`bench/realtime` isn't on `main` yet so I couldn't diff PR #2's implementation directly; adopted the `ceil` form you described.)
- **A late commit could bind a clip to the previous transcript.** On timeout `run_asr.py` recorded the clip without an item id and kept the socket, so a late `input_audio_buffer.committed` was consumed as the *next* clip's and every subsequent clip inherited its predecessor's hypothesis — silent WER corruption, no error on any affected row. It now aborts the batch so the existing retry reconnects.

**No reported number changes this round.** All 165 Track B runs and all 48 Track A cells are complete, judged and error-free, so the corrected guards agree with the published values exactly. 58 tests.

## Review round 6 (final) — two more of the class, and a written inventory

**Instance nine.** `run_scenarios.py` turned any exception into an error row and **exited zero**, so the shell taught last round to propagate child failures faithfully reported success from a runner that had swallowed its errors. Now exits non-zero listing failed scenarios.

**Instance ten.** `summarize.py` checked completeness by **counting rows**, so three copies of trial 1 satisfied `--trials 3` while trials 2 and 3 were missing, and `pass_k` reported success over duplicates. The runners append to JSONL, so any partial re-run reached this. Both the check and `pass_k` now key on the **set of trial ids**.

Since three sweeps each missed instances of the class they were sweeping for, the checks are now written down: **`bench/quality/COMPLETENESS.md`** — all twelve places the harness decides "this is complete", what each compares, how each can be fooled, and the three that cannot be verified at all. The rule in its final form: *every check compares what it got against what it expected, by identity rather than by count.*

### Cancellation — and barge-in withdrawn

An interrupted generation is `response.done` with `response.status == "cancelled"`; **zero** top-level `response.cancelled` events appear in any log, so the old check never fired. Re-derived from committed logs:

| arm | responses cancelled by the interruption |
|---|---|
| `native-gpt-realtime-2` | **6/6** |
| `vl-native-brain` | 1/6 |
| `vl-gpt41mini`, `-dns`, `-semvad` | **0/6** — nothing left to cancel |

That's the latency difference seen from the other side, and it's a direct observation.

**`bargein_stop_p50_ms` is withdrawn from the report rather than corrected a fourth time.** It measured when audio stopped arriving on the wire, not when the agent stopped speaking; that's not recoverable from this design. Cancellation counts and correction-adoption (24/30) survive because both are directly observable. The report marks barge-in as the weakest part of the study.

Also fixed: a closing turn burned **25 s of billed silence** when the response was only an `end_call` tool call.

**All headline numbers unchanged.** 67 tests.

### One self-inflicted incident

The `run_all.sh` test I added last round **truncated the committed results file** — `run_all.sh` does `cd "$HERE"` regardless of cwd, and `TRACK=b` begins by emptying `results/scenarios.jsonl`. It ran before I committed, so the commit captured the empty file. Restored from `4bfc79b` (165 runs, verified), and the output root is now overridable so no test can reach a finished run. The suite now asserts the results hash is unchanged.

### Fixture numbers, for the human reader

PR-Agent flags these because it cannot tell synthetic from real. They are: German **Bundesnetzagentur drama ranges** (`0152 288173xx` mobile, `030 23125xxx` Berlin landline) and the **`555-01xx`** convention for English. None can reach a subscriber. `bench/quality/README.md` § "No real call data is committed" states that every scenario, name, number and audio file is synthetic and TTS-generated, and `TestFixtureHygiene` fails the build if a fixture number leaves those ranges.

## Review round 7 (final) — barge-in withdrawn, three fixed

**Barge-in is no longer reported.** Applying your standard: four independent defects across four rounds in one metric.

1. stop latency timed when audio stopped arriving *on the wire*, not when the agent stopped speaking
2. adoption read the **caller's** transcript, not the agent's reply
3. cancellation watched for an event neither service emits
4. in-flight state recorded **after** the quiescence wait — and when the previous response was silent or tool-only, the barge-in turn's audio was **skipped entirely**, invalidating the rest of that scenario with no error raised

The two scenarios still run (transcripts are useful qualitatively); nothing is scored from them. The surviving qualitative finding — interruption is the client's job, and on Voice Live there is often no generation left to cancel — doesn't depend on any withdrawn number.

**Three fixes:**

- **`score_asr.py` validated by row count.** A duplicated clip id beside a missing one totals correctly, marks the cell complete, and double-weights the duplicate in the WER. Now compares clip **id sets**: no duplicates, expected size, identical across arms for the same (language, condition). **No published WER moves** — checked, and there are no duplicates: all 48 cells are exactly 25 clips with matching id sets.
- **`IndexError` on a condition-only run.** dWER and SNR50 are both relative to a clean baseline; without one it now emits no robustness rows and says why, instead of throwing after the detail CSV was written.
- **The inventory's one unfixed gap**: a scenario that connects, produces no agent turns and exits cleanly is now an error the runner reports.

## How much to trust these numbers

Now stated in the report itself, as plainly as you put it:

- **Eleven instances of one bug class** across six review rounds, where missing or unverified data read as a pass. Three sweeps each missed instances of the class they were sweeping for — hence `COMPLETENESS.md`.
- **One metric withdrawn** (barge-in, four defects).
- **The recommendation never moved.** Corrections changed magnitudes — the p95 gap narrowed substantially, strict success rose on every arm once time-valued facts became matchable — never the direction.

The report separates the figures that **survived unchanged** (WER table, slot capture, judge groundedness) from those that **moved under correction and could again** (latency percentiles, strict task success) from the one that **did not survive** (barge-in).

70 tests. Typecheck and tests green. Ready to merge.

## Review round 8 (final) — CI unblocked, four fixed

**[P1] CI was broken.** Reproduced on a clean env with only `jiwer` + `num2words`: collection died, `Ran 1 test, FAILED`. Took the refactor rather than adding the dependency — pure event helpers moved to `events.py`, and a test now asserts no scoring module reaches for `websockets` or the runner. **78 tests pass under the exact CI dependency set.**

**[P1] An outage was being published as a measurement.** An exhausted ASR batch wrote a full cell of error rows and exited zero, so the shell reported completion and the scorer saw a complete set of clip ids — a transport failure rendered as **100% WER**. Instance twelve, and the worst-consequence one: the others let a gap pass as success; this converts infrastructure failure into a number a reader would take for an engine that couldn't transcribe. Runner exits non-zero; `score_asr.py` refuses any cell whose rows are all errors.

**[P2] `final_language` — wrong in both directions, and it moved numbers.** Scored from the caller's transcript (testing what the *caller* said) with an echoed companion that joined all agent turns (earlier German drowning out a correct English reply). Scored from the agent's **final turn**:

| | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| code-switch followed | native 2/3 | **15/15, every arm** |
| `native-gpt-realtime-2` strict success | 0.606 | **0.636** |
| `native-gpt-realtime-2` slots heard | 0.856 | **0.911** |
| `vl-gpt41mini-dns` slots echoed | 0.651 | **0.706** |
| `vl-native-brain` slots echoed | 0.812 | **0.868** |

The earlier "native failed the switch once" was an artefact. `pass_k` unchanged everywhere; ordering unchanged.

**[P2] `--out` without an extension** silently overwrote the aggregate — `str.replace` returns the original when the pattern is absent. Both scorers derive companion paths properly and reject extensionless names.

`COMPLETENESS.md` now records that this class has been found **twelve times across seven rounds** — framed as the failure mode this code attracts, so the next person extending it expects to introduce it rather than assuming it's been designed out.

Ready to merge.

## Review round 9 (final) — barge-in excluded from scoring

**Fixed: the withdrawn metric's scenarios were still being scored.** You're right that leaving them running left them feeding `success`, `pass^k` and the slot aggregates — and when the preceding response produces no audio the runner never speaks the interrupting turn, so a row can exist for a call in which the scripted correction was never delivered.

Now marked `"scored": false` in the fixture and dropped from every aggregate *before* the completeness checks. They still run; their transcripts are still committed. **9 scored scenarios, 135 of 165 runs.**

**Checked rather than assumed — the recommendation does not move.** Every Track B figure shifts, and one within-family pair swaps (`vl-gpt41mini-dns` ↔ `vl-native-brain`), which was never a decision point:

| arm | success | pass^3 | slots heard | grounded |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `native-gpt-realtime-2` | **0.593** | **0.556** | 0.893 | **1.000** |
| `vl-native-brain` | 0.407 | 0.222 | 0.920 | **1.000** |
| `vl-gpt41mini-dns` | 0.370 | 0.222 | **0.960** | 0.815 |
| `vl-gpt41mini` | 0.333 | 0.222 | **0.960** | 0.704 |
| `vl-gpt41mini-semvad` | 0.259 | 0.111 | 0.920 | 0.704 |

Both gpt-realtime-2 arms still lead both gpt-4.1-mini arms on strict success; groundedness is still 1.000 vs 0.704; Voice Live is still ~700 ms faster at p50 for 43% of the cost. The split recommendation stands unchanged.

## Documented, not fixed

Per your line — *silent contamination gets fixed, visible failure and debug-flag-only gets written down* — these are in `COMPLETENESS.md` with the shapes named:

- `--allow-incomplete` counts rows not identities: 4 rows against 3 trials → rate 1.333, `missing_runs` −1. The default path validates by identity, and that's what the published numbers rest on.
- `--allow-incomplete` omits entirely-missing ASR cells rather than reporting `complete=0`.
- A mid-stream `ws.send()` failure can leave the mic task without setting the event a turn awaits — hangs the run rather than corrupting it. Never fired.

80 tests, verified under the CI dependency set. Ready to merge.

## Review round 10 (final) — report now matches the CSV

**1. The VAD-control conclusion was wrong in both directions.** Recomputed on the final scored dataset, holding brain and stack constant:

| server → semantic VAD (gpt-4.1-mini, Voice Live) | change |
|---|---|
| strict success | 0.333 → 0.259 (**−0.074**) |
| pass^3 | 0.222 → 0.111 (**−0.111**) |
| TTFA p50 / p95 | 1315 → 1320 / 1719 → 1852 ms (**+5 / +133**) |
| judge groundedness | 0.704 → 0.704 (no change) |

The old "−69 ms, no effect on success" predated both the barge-in exclusion and the switch to turn-level percentiles — stale twice over. **Semantic VAD is marginally slower and scores slightly worse here.** At 27 runs/arm that's 2 runs and 1 scenario, so the magnitude is noise — but the direction is against it.

**The attribution survives via a cleaner cell than the control.** Holding stack *and* VAD constant — Voice Live, semantic VAD, brain varied — is the one fully-controlled comparison in the design: success **+0.148**, groundedness **+0.296**, TTFA p50 **+1049 ms**. The brain effect is twice the VAD effect on success, and it runs *opposite* to the confound (`vl-native-brain` is itself on the VAD that costs success, so its advantage is understated). The native-vs-Voice-Live comparison still crosses a VAD boundary and is now labelled directional.

**2. Groundedness denominator.** 24 was the all-run count. On the 135 scored rows it is **21**, all from gpt-4.1-mini arms, against **zero** for gpt-realtime-2 across 54 scored runs. The six over-promising cases are unchanged.

Swept the document for other pre-exclusion denominators and found three more: a stale worst-case p50 (2408 → 2369), `end_call` quoted as 23–25 of 33 rather than **17–19 of 27**, and a judge groundedness figure (0.697 → 0.704). A scripted check now verifies every Track B table cell against `summary.csv` and greps for stale tokens; it reports zero.

**3. `probe_session.py`** stopped at the first transcript-shaped event, which is truthy when empty — so on the noise-suppression arm it could report "no transcript" while the real one was queued. Keeps the longest text and drains for the duplicate; verified against `vl-gpt41mini-dns`.

80 tests, verified under the CI dependency set. Ready to merge.

### Rebased onto main

PR #4 and #6 landed while this was in review and rewrote the `deploy` job in `ci.yml`. Rebased onto `f627a08`; the conflict was resolved keeping **both** — main's expanded Cloudflare credential documentation and this branch's `bench-scoring` job. Validated the resulting YAML parses and still declares all three jobs (`check`, `bench-scoring`, `deploy`).

Re-verified after the rebase: 80 scoring tests under the CI dependency set, 138 repo tests, typecheck clean, report values still match `summary.csv`.

## Review round 11 — instance thirteen

**Fixed: the scenario universe was inferred from the results.** `summarize.py` built its scenario set from the rows it was given, so a scenario omitted across *every* arm disappeared from `expected_runs` and the `pass_k` denominator together — completeness passed and every aggregate was computed over a smaller matrix. You're right that this is the one gap the trial-identity checks can't see: they verify trials *within* a scenario, and this loses the scenario.

The set now comes from `fixtures/scenarios.json`. A fixture scenario with no rows aborts (or under `--allow-incomplete` scores as a failure for every arm while staying in the denominator); a results file containing a scenario the fixture doesn't declare is rejected. Three tests cover it, including the `--allow-incomplete` path where a missing scenario must give `pass_k` 0.5 rather than 1.0.

**Documented, not fixed** — both in `COMPLETENESS.md` with their shapes named:

- `response.done` with `status == "failed"` and no separate error event reads as a normal finish, so a partially failed call could enter scoring if another turn produced text.
- The final drain in `run_asr.py` catches `Exception`, so a websocket closure or decode error there is indistinguishable from the timeout that normally ends it, yielding an empty error-free hypothesis scored as a recognition miss rather than retried. The `CommitDesync` guard covers the same failure during the main loop; this is the tail.

Neither occurred in this run — all 165 runs error-free, all 48 ASR cells complete — and neither changes a reported number.

**No reported number changes.** 83 scoring tests under the CI dependency set, 138 repo tests, typecheck clean.

## Review round 12 — two matchers fixed, two fidelity limits stated

**Two P1 limitations now open the Confounds section**, ahead of everything else, because they change what the numbers *mean*:

- **The recogniser was told the caller's language.** Both tracks pass the scenario language to Azure Speech / whisper-1; `src/call-session.ts` leaves it unset in production. Every slot and success figure benefits from an oracle prior the product doesn't have — most of all German names, digit strings, and the 15/15 code-switching result. Both arms got it, so the comparison holds; the **levels are optimistic**.
- **Scripted turns continue after `end_call`.** Production begins hanging up. **Could it flip the ordering? No, on this dataset** — measured exposure is **two turns, both on `vl-gpt41mini`**, because the scripted `end_call` almost always lands on the closing turn. The gap it would need to close is seven runs, and it runs *against* the arm that would lose credit, so removing it would widen the gap. Stated with that number rather than as an open worry.

**Two matchers fixed**, and they cut opposite ways, so here's the net rather than an assumption:

| | effect |
|---|---|
| time matcher (inflating) | expected `14:00` matched `2:30`, `2 AM`, bare `2` → now parsed as (hour, minute) and compared |
| negation (deflating) | "not open on Saturday" matched forbidden `open on Saturday` → negation-window guard |

**Net:** seven false grounding credits removed, **all on gpt-4.1-mini arms** (`grounded_ok` 1.000→0.963, 0.963→0.852, 1.000→0.889) plus one echoed slot. gpt-realtime-2 arms untouched. **No success or pass^3 figure moved.** The negation guard changed nothing here — the study's only `forbidden_hit` had already been removed as a cross-turn artefact — so it's a guard for future runs.

One subtlety worth noting: the first fix needed a second one. `normalize("2:30")` is "two thirty", so a word scan over normalised text re-admitted the very times the digit pass had rejected. Spoken hours are now scanned only after digits are stripped.

90 tests. Ready to merge.

## Review round 13 — cancelled responses were attributed to the next turn

**The negative-TTFA count, and the real affected set.** Eight turns went negative — but that understates it: **every run containing a cancellation** has shifted attribution, whether or not the arithmetic crossed zero.

| | count |
|---|---|
| turns with negative TTFA | 8 (min **−5461.8 ms**) |
| runs containing ≥1 cancellation | **14 of 165** (7 in the scored set) |
| affected scenarios | `message-de-01` (6), `codeswitch-01` (1) |
| affected arms | `native-gpt-realtime-2` (4), `vl-native-brain` (3) |
| Voice Live gpt-4.1-mini arms | **0** — no cancellations at all |

`message-de-01`'s second caller turn has an internal pause, which is what trips the VAD.

**Fixed in the runner**: a cancelled response is discarded — its audio timings and the agent text it contributed — and the turn keeps waiting for the replacement.

**The committed runs can't be repaired.** Reconstructing the metric needs the moment the harness finished streaming the caller clip, which the log doesn't record. Those runs carry `ttfa_trustworthy=0` and are excluded from the percentiles:

| arm | p50 | p95 |
|---|---|---|
| `native-gpt-realtime-2` | 2022 → **2077** | 3262 → **3325** |
| `vl-native-brain` | 2369 → **2408** | 3474 → **3722** |
| Voice Live gpt-4.1-mini arms | unchanged | unchanged |

The mis-attribution had been **flattering the slower family**, so correcting it widens the latency gap. **Transcripts were never affected** — they append in arrival order, not per turn — so slots, grounding, success and pass^3 are unchanged.

**Contraction negation fixed.** You were right that the previous fix only handled phrasing nobody uses: the normaliser turns `aren't` into `aren t`, not `arent`. Split stems now listed, and the time path substitutes apostrophes in place so its offsets stay valid. Covers `aren't`, `don't`, `can't`, `couldn't`, `won't`, and the typographic apostrophe.

**Time matching documented as approximate.** No fourth regex. The report states both inflating failure modes — numeric strings parsing as clock mentions, and spoken composite times recording only the hour — names the affected metric (**strict success on the three booking scenarios**), notes that a single run is 0.037 at n=27, and points the reader at the WER table, slot capture and groundedness instead. Both modes hit every arm identically, so the comparison isn't skewed.

94 tests. Ready to merge.

## What's in here

- `bench/quality/` — harness, fixtures, scoring, raw event logs (audio redacted), CSV results.
- Track A streams conditioned FLEURS clips and scores each engine's own caller transcript. This measures **the STT front-end each stack ships** (whisper-1 vs azure-speech), not a free-standing ASR model, and is labelled that way throughout.
- Track B runs 11 Riverside Dental scenarios as live multi-turn calls against the **real** `buildSystemPrompt` output — `gen_prompt.ts` calls the product code, so the 21-day calendar block is genuine.
- Scoring is split by whether the question has an objectively right answer: slots, tool calls and language adherence are programmatic; the LLM judge sees only groundedness, resolution and tone, blind, with a seeded per-scenario shuffle. **Two seeds agree on groundedness 159/165 (96.4%)** — the judge is validated, not assumed.

## Confounds, stated

- Voice Live **rejects** `server_vad` on the gpt-realtime-2 brain, so that arm runs Azure semantic VAD while native runs server VAD. I added `vl-gpt41mini-semvad` as a control: on the same brain, VAD choice moves TTFA p50 by 69 ms and success not at all, so it is not driving the brain comparison — but the native-vs-Voice-Live comparison still crosses a VAD boundary.
- Caller audio is Azure neural TTS: more fluent than real callers, so Track B is optimistic in absolute terms but comparable between arms. Track A uses real human speech.
- **Barge-in cannot be measured server-side.** These engines deliver a whole response's audio faster than real time (`response.done` ~600 ms into a 4 s reply), so in 29 of 30 attempts there was nothing left to interrupt. Barge-in is entirely the client's job. All five arms did adopt the corrected value, 3/3.
- A collector bug was found and fixed mid-run; `vl-gpt41mini` was re-run as a control and produced **100/100 byte-identical** transcripts, confirming the fix is behaviour-preserving and the remaining empties are the service's.

Raw logs are committed so every number can be re-scored without spending again. Audio corpora are gitignored; `bench/quality/prepare/` regenerates them.

`npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass.

items.title: v3.5.0 release polish: close every gap the post-merge verification pass surfaced (pre-tag)
items.body:
## Pull Request Description

### Summary

Post-merge trust-but-verify over #380, run **before the `v3.5.0` tag is cut** so the tag lands on a tree whose every claim is true. Two adversarial verification waves (finder agents → per-finding refutation agents → completeness critic) audited the merged release state; **45 findings survived verification, zero were taken on faith, and all 45 are fixed here**. No cryptographic behavior changes anywhere — the diff is documentation truth, release/SBOM machinery, measurement-harness hygiene in `tools/`, one broken demo import, and gate hardening. **Merge this, then tag the new merge commit `v3.5.0`** (same two commands as before; the runbook inside `release.yml` now names them correctly).

### Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) — docker monitor demo crash-loop; dudect Ascon timed-region selection; dangling doc pointers
- [x] Documentation update (changes to documentation only) — README/wiki/SECURITY/CHANGELOG/compliance-report truth fixes
- [x] Test enhancement (adds or improves tests) — citation-test broadening detection made real; new Ed25519-row pin; SBOM completeness gate
- [x] Code refactoring (improves code quality without changing functionality) — checker extensions, generator provenance discipline

### Related Issues

Close-out of #380 (v3.5.0 release finalization). Blocks the `v3.5.0` tag: several fixes (release-notes claim, SBOM asset, `release.yml` runbook) are only effective if merged before the tag exists.

## Motivation and Context

### Why is this change required?

An exhaustive post-merge verification pass (version stamps, CHANGELOG diff-integrity, baselines, SBOM, `release.yml` dry-trace, docs claims, adversarial diff review, integrity signing, plus a completeness critic over surfaces nobody had checked) found that the release, while CI-green, still shipped false or stale claims — several of them freezable-forever if the tag had been cut first.

### What problem does it solve?

Four HIGHs, all confirmed against the tree:

1. **The SBOM was incomplete and the release would have frozen it.** 11 components vs 16 shipped public primitives — `ama_ascon` (3.4.0), `ama_frost`, `ama_agent_binding`, and this release's own `ama_lms`/`ama_nistp` were absent. `--check` passed because it validates versions/purls of listed components, never completeness. Now: 16 components, and the generator **fails closed** on any unclassified top-level `src/c/*.c` (negative-tested).
2. **Release notes claimed a "Python SBOM" asset the tag-triggered run cannot attach** — under immutable releases the false claim could never be corrected with the asset. The body now claims exactly what is attached.
3. **`wiki/Security-Model.md` said `3.4.x | ✓ Active` with no 3.5.x row** — a false security-support claim on a page that declares SECURITY.md authoritative.
4. **The shipped docker-compose `ama-monitor` service could not start** (`from tools.monitoring…` — a package that does not exist in the image; `restart: unless-stopped` crash-loop). One-line import fix, verified in an `/app`-equivalent layout.

Plus, notably: the ARM baseline's new 3.5.0 change-log entry was an x86 copy-paste asserting a recalibration that never touched that file (rewritten honestly; floors untouched; historical entries left verbatim); three dudect Ascon lanes still selected their class inside the timed region despite the comment claiming otherwise (hoisted; disassembly-verified branch-free); and a cluster of README/wiki/compliance claims that failed their own printed reproduction commands.

## Cryptographic Impact

### Security Impact Assessment

- [x] No cryptographic security impact

No signing, verification, KDF, AEAD, or key-management code changes. `src/c` changes: one comment in `ama_argon2.c`; `include/` changes: one docstring. The dudect change alters how the *harness measures* (class-selected pointer hoisted above the timer in the three Ascon lanes), never what is measured — verified by disassembly (every timed region branch-free, `cmov` before timer-open) plus self-test and a clean 20k-iteration run (all strict lanes PASS, Ascon |t| ≤ 1.25).

### Standards Compliance

- [x] No standards affected. `docs/compliance/CSRC_ALIGN_REPORT.md` gained a re-validation addendum per INVARIANT-16: mappings re-verified against this tree, six corrections recorded, post-audit primitives tabulated with their conformance gates **re-executed** (full vendored Wycheproof corpus: 4,263 vectors, 0 failures; Ascon/LMS/NIST-P/parameter-set suites: 244 tests, 0 failures). It adds no ACVP claims.

## Implementation Details

### Changes Made

**Truth-critical (must precede the tag):** SBOM inventory + fail-closed completeness gate in `tools/generate_sbom.py`; `release.yml` notes/runbook/range comment; wiki security-support matrix mirrored to SECURITY.md (+ Document History through 3.5.0, Last Updated rolled); docker demo import; `benchmarks/arm-baseline.json` + `baseline.json` provenance (`baseline_source_release` 2.1.2 → 3.4.0/3.1.0, ARM notes de-copy-pasted, corrections logged as new entries — **no floor value changed**, justification gate untriggered by its own contract); dudect Ascon lanes + real nine-lane header inventory.

**Claim accuracy:** README (Ed25519 row cites INVARIANT-26 only; INVARIANT-37 anchor fixed; counts re-derived at commit time — 3,057 functions / 126 files, 57 C suites of 60 TUs; "25 modules + `__init__` + `__main__`"; AES-GCM headroom stated honestly per BENCHMARK_HISTORY; benchmark-artifact provenance section). `tests/test_readme_invariant_citations.py`: broadening detection implemented with negative anchors that provably fire, plus an Ed25519-row pin. `docs/METRICS_REPORT.md` fully re-measured via its own commands. Wiki: Python 3.10–3.14, current algorithm surface, OpenSSL PQC cells corrected against this repo's own OpenSSL 4.0.1 benchmarks (plus a swapped RFC 3161 cell), AES opt-out two-flag `INSECURE` gate stated, floor table regenerated from `baseline.json` with floor-only rows for post-run gate entries (`update_docs.py` no longer silently drops them). Five dangling `[Unreleased] § BREAKING` pointers → `[3.0.0]` (runtime `SecurityWarning` text included); INVARIANT-22 "signing principal" → "encrypting principal"; CHANGELOG 3.0.0 summary date matches its heading.

**Deliberately NOT done:** `dashboard.html`/`competitive.html` are **not** restamped — their "3.4.0 / 2026-07-29" stamps are the true provenance of their measurement runs, and an offline re-render would label data with a build that was never benchmarked (this pass briefly did exactly that to `competitive.html` and reverted it on realizing the implication; `generate_competitive.py` now derives the version at render time and documents the regenerate-only-with-a-run rule). `benchmark-results.json` (2026-04-27) is likewise left as the honest record, its divergence from `benchmark-report.md` (2026-07-29) now stated in README with the pending canonical-host dual-output run named as the re-convergence path.

**Toolchain/process:** `requirements-lock.txt` closure completed via clean-venv freeze — 8 additions (`packaging`, `librt`, `ast_serialize`, `Cython`, `build`, `pyproject_hooks`, `setuptools`, `wheel`), zero drift on existing pins, header states the closure contract. `check_version_consistency.py` now covers `docs/Doxyfile` `PROJECT_NUMBER` (was "2.0" across three major generations) and `@vX.Y.Z` pins in `docs/**/*.rst` (the Sphinx landing page shipped `@v3.4.0` into 3.5.0) — both negative-tested. Small stamps: index.rst pin, bandit pre-commit rev 1.9.4, `Dockerfile.alpine` labels, phantom `secure-memory` extra removed, CMake SIMD blame precision. CHANGELOG `[3.5.0]` carries the full narrative plus the `### Release` mechanics block. Integrity digest/signature regenerated over the final sources (INVARIANT-17).

### Technical Approach

Two-wave verification: eight surface auditors → per-finding adversarial refuters (every claim re-derived from the tree; one finding refuted and dropped) → completeness critic → a second refutation wave over the remaining 32 claims. Fixes applied at the smallest correct scope; where a finding's naive fix would have created new dishonesty (restamping generated measurement artifacts), the provenance was documented instead and the generator hardened. Historical records (baseline change logs, CHANGELOG history, the CSRC report body) were never edited — corrections are recorded as new entries/addenda.

### Breaking Changes

**Breaking Changes:**
- [x] None

## Testing

### Test Coverage

- [x] Unit tests added/updated (citation-test negative anchors + Ed25519-row pin; SBOM completeness gate negative-tested)
- [x] Test coverage maintained or improved
- [x] All tests pass locally

### Testing Performed

**Environment:**
- Python version(s): 3.11
- Operating System: Linux x86-64
- PQC backend: [x] Native C library (rebuilt at 3.5.0 on this tree)

**Test Cases:**
1. Full `pytest tests/` on the final tree: **4139 passed, 0 failed** (4 environment-only skips: SoftHSM2, bandit, network TSA/corpus).
2. All repo gate checkers green, including the extended `check_version_consistency.py` ("All declarations agree on version '3.5.0'"), `generate_sbom.py --check`, documented-counts/extras/claim-honesty, headers, secrets, workflow commands, action pins, line endings, gate coverage, suppression hygiene, fdopen safety, corpus originality, fuzz-target registration; repo-wide `black --check` / `ruff check` clean.
3. dudect: `--self-test` green; 20k-iteration run all strict lanes PASS; disassembly audit of all three converted Ascon timed regions (branch-free, single call site, hoisted `cmov`).
4. Full vendored Wycheproof corpus: 4,263 vectors, 0 failures, every non-run vector in a named policy bucket. Conformance suites for post-audit primitives: 244 passed.
5. New gates proven able to fail: SBOM completeness (probe TU → exit 1), Doxyfile/rst checker rules (stale values → FAIL), then restored to green.
6. `verify_module_integrity()` → signed integrity verified; import-time POST `OPERATIONAL`.
7. Docker demo verified running through its monitoring phases in an isolated `/app`-equivalent layout.

### Known Test Vectors

- [x] Tested against official NIST/IETF test vectors (Wycheproof full corpus re-run; RFC 8554 / RFC 6979 / SP 800-232 / FIPS 203/204 suites re-executed for the CSRC addendum)

## Code Quality

### Code Quality Checks

- [x] All functions have comprehensive docstrings
- [x] No security warnings from linters
- [x] Inline code comments added for complex logic (SBOM partition contract; dudect idiom rationale; generator regenerate-only-with-a-run rule)

### Documentation Updates

- [x] README.md updated
- [x] CHANGELOG.md updated (`[3.5.0]` narrative + `### Release` block)
- [x] Inline docstrings (crypto_api, pqc_backends, INVARIANTS.md, public header)

## Backwards Compatibility

### Compatibility Assessment

- [x] Fully backwards compatible

items.title: Make spatial domain decomposition the canonical MPI benchmark
items.body:
## What changed

- removes the old case-scheduling MPI implementations under `c/mpi`, `cpp/mpi`, and `python/mpi`
- removes their dedicated Slurm jobs, raw case-MPI tables, and obsolete mixed comparison packages
- defines MPI consistently as spatial decomposition of one CFD grid
- keeps the canonical domain implementations under `src/` for OpenMP, MPI, and hybrid execution
- repairs stale pre-`src/` paths in benchmark and scaling scripts
- fixes the C distributed rebuild problem by forcing `mpicc` in the spatial-MPI and hybrid Makefiles
- adds root targets for repository checks, clean domain rebuilds, reference smokes, OpenMP smokes, spatial-MPI smokes, hybrid smokes, and selected-result generation
- rewrites the root README around the two numerical tracks and only the most relevant archived domain results
- adds a reproducible `results/selected/` package generated from the existing raw CSV archive
- retains detailed secondary/raw domain results under `results/final/` for traceability instead of displaying all of them in the root README
- preserves pressure-correction validation evidence as a separate reference track
- keeps CUDA explicitly experimental because the current archived validation does not pass

## Selected README evidence

The README now highlights one matched repeated domain workload:

- `N=128`
- `Re=400`
- central convection
- RBSOR
- 2500 outer steps
- 250 Poisson iterations per step
- three repetitions per resource configuration

It reports only the retained C/C++ OpenMP and Python spatial-MPI/hybrid points that are supported by the archive. It does not invent C/C++ MPI performance results from failed historical jobs.

## Rebuild fix

The previous distributed C Makefiles used `CC ?= mpicc`, which could be overridden by GNU Make's built-in `CC=cc`. The canonical C spatial-MPI and hybrid Makefiles now use the MPI wrapper explicitly.

## Validation

GitHub Actions now passes all of the following:

- repository consistency and removal checks
- clean rebuild of every compiled domain implementation
- pressure-correction reference smoke tests and output verification
- C/C++ domain OpenMP smoke tests and output verification
- C/C++/Python spatial-MPI smoke tests and output verification
- C/C++/Python hybrid smoke tests and output verification
- reproducible regeneration of `results/selected/`

## Numerical impact

No numerical equations, discretization kernels, convergence criteria, or retained full benchmark rows were changed. No full benchmark or Stromboli performance matrix was rerun.

The selected archived domain results remain fixed-step performance evidence, not convergence-controlled time-to-solution evidence.

## Follow-up after merge

1. rerun the full C and C++ spatial-MPI and hybrid performance matrices
2. add one common convergence-controlled protocol
3. validate the streamfunction-vorticity domain track against accepted cavity reference quantities
4. repair and revalidate CUDA before reporting CPU/GPU speedup
5. then return to the paper branch and freeze the final benchmark protocol

items.title: refactor(benchmark): rename downstream_success_rate to required_file_completeness_rate
items.body:
## Stack

Stack-Id: `r2-truth-in-claims`
Base: `docs/r2-cross-tool-baseline-semantics`
Position: 3/3

1. `fix/r2-savings-targeted-read-baseline` -> #572
2. `docs/r2-cross-tool-baseline-semantics` -> #573
3. `refactor/r2-required-file-completeness-rate` -> this PR

Depends on: #573

Milestone R2 (truth-in-claims correction), `.docs/DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md` §6 Section A. Stack leaf.

## What changes

`ScorecardRow.downstream_success_rate` never measured downstream task success. `_completion_outcomes` reads `task_completion_result`, which `completion_result_from_missing` sets to `PASS` iff no required file is missing — so the field is a function of required-file recall, and archex never puts a model in the loop to decide whether a task was solved. The name asserted an outcome the benchmark cannot observe.

- The field is renamed `required_file_completeness_rate` (applied via LSP rename, so every reference moved together) and carries a docstring stating the recall derivation, that no model is in the loop, and the single exception: the opt-in `benchmark bundle-eval` lane, where an operator-supplied external evaluator command may report `bundle_only_success`. archex neither provides nor calls that evaluator.
- The scorecard markdown column header reads `Required-File Completeness`.
- `docs/external-quality-frontier.md` renders that column and described it as downstream success; it is relabelled. Its values are unchanged and the doc says so.
- A regression test asserts the rendered header, which previously had no test behind it.
- `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` records the whole R2 stack — the savings re-baselining, the self-repo withdrawal, the cross-tool annotation, and this rename.

Values and aggregation are unchanged. No artifact is deleted and no version is bumped.

## Verification

```text
$ grep -rn "downstream_success_rate\|445×\|673×\|99\.78\|99\.64" src tests docs README.md
(no output)

$ grep -r downstream_success_rate src/ tests/ docs/
(no output)

$ uv run ruff check .            -> All checks passed!
$ uv run ruff format --check .   -> 499 files already formatted
$ uv run pyright                 -> 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations
$ uv run pytest tests/ -k "scorecard or metrics or cross_tool" -q
148 passed, 4333 deselected

$ uv run pytest -q
4472 passed, 9 deselected in 309.44s
Required test coverage of 85% reached. Total coverage: 91.56%
```

**Rename-breaks-an-evidence-reader risk (the milestone's declared mitigation).** No checked-in artifact under `benchmarks/` contains the `downstream_success_rate` key, so nothing deserializes into the renamed field. `archex benchmark validate --kind evidence --input <dir>` takes an evidence *directory*, and every checked-in one is revision-pinned to the commit that recorded it, so it fails a source-revision check on any later commit — pre-existing and unrelated to this change. The reader path was therefore exercised directly instead:

```text
$ uv run python -c "... load_evidence_reports(benchmarks/results/m9_documentation_status/raw) ..."
reports: 24
header ok: True
stale label gone: True
rows: [('comprehension', 0.5416666666666666)]
```

24 persisted reports load, build a scorecard, and render through the new column name.

## Risks

The renamed field is part of the `M3ScorecardArtifact` JSON schema. A previously saved scorecard artifact holding the old key will not round-trip into `ScorecardRow`; no such artifact is checked in. Rollback is a revert of the stack; no data is destroyed.

---

## Review round 1 — corrections applied

- **The docstring made two false provenance claims.** "archex neither provides nor calls that evaluator" — `run_bundle_only_evaluator` invokes it via `subprocess.run`. And `bundle_only_success` is not in the evaluator's required output schema: when the evaluator omits it, archex derives the value itself by exact string comparison of the evaluator's `answer` against the task's `expected_answer` (`_with_expected_answer_success`). Both corrected, and the docstring now states the consequence the new name hides — where a bundle-only outcome exists it takes precedence, so a task with perfect required-file recall can contribute `0.0`.
- **The caveat was source-only.** `use_attribute_docstrings` is not enabled anywhere in the repo, so the attribute docstring reached neither the JSON schema nor the rendered markdown; the published surface was a bare column header. `format_m3_scorecard_markdown` now emits the definition beneath every scorecard, with a test pinning it.
- **`gate.py` kept the repudiated label on the enforcement surface.** `_completion_outcome_score` duplicated `_completion_outcomes` byte-for-byte and still called it a downstream outcome. Both now call `archex.benchmark.models.completion_outcome_score`; `check_fixed_agent_non_regression` is relabelled, and its `fixed_agent_success_regression` metric string is kept as a stable machine-readable contract.
- **`docs/RETRIEVAL_DEFAULT_DECISIONS.md` published the same claim about the same run.** The acceptance grep matches only the snake_case identifier, so the prose form passed the gate while the claim stayed live in a decision document. Relabelled; values unchanged.
- **`artifact_version` was not bumped.** A version-1 `M3ScorecardArtifact` no longer loads (loudly — pydantic reports the renamed field as missing), yet both shapes stamped version 1. Now `2`, with the reason on the model and the break recorded in the CHANGELOG.

The plan's acceptance grep is empty; widening it to the prose forms (`-iE 'downstream[-_ ]?success'`) leaves exactly one hit — `tests/benchmark/test_scorecard.py:301`, the negative assertion that enforces the label's absence.

Re-verified: every one of the four rename commits passes `tests/benchmark/test_scorecard.py tests/benchmark/test_gate.py` on its own; full gate `uv run pytest -q` 4473 passed, coverage 91.55%; ruff and pyright clean; CI green on all three PRs.

items.title: Rewrite README/CLAUDE.md around the current tool, and make the documented entry points work
items.body:
Stacked on #5 — review that first, or read this diff on its own (GitHub shows it
against `pr/data-contract`). Base retargets to `adding-ocaml-support`
automatically when #5 merges.

The README had drifted badly enough to be misleading rather than merely stale, so
this rewrites it, moves the machine-facing detail into `CLAUDE.md`, and fixes the
handful of things it turned out the docs were describing incorrectly *because the
code was wrong*.

## README

Restructured to follow what someone actually does: what it is → a quick start
that works → what a run produces → configs → runtimes → modifiers → tag
selection → commands → **adding a benchmark** → **adding an experiment** →
analysing results → env vars.

Documented for the first time: the config layering model (`includes:` /
`overrides:` and its merge rules), `comparisons:`, `schema_version` and native
contract emission, `buildbms` / `minheap` / `adapt`, the run-directory layout and
filename grammar, the notebooks, and the two "how do I add one of these" walkthroughs.

## Corrections (all verified against the code, not assumed)

- **`make_targets` does not exist.** The README documented it as a runtime option
  with default `["world.opt"]`. Nothing reads it.
- **Toolchain caching was described wrongly.** `/tmp/running-ng-ocaml-toolchains/`
  is OxCaml-only; stock OCaml and MMTk cache as the opam switch
  `running-ng-<name>`, which is what you delete to force a rebuild.
- **Sidecars are per tool.** `olly_*.json` / `perf_*.json`, not one combined
  `<base>.json`. The old format is still *read* for back-compat but nothing writes it.
- **Benchmark counts.** micro: 13 suites / 200 enabled (was "138"). macro: 20
  active suites / 31 enabled (was "20 tools, 31 programs", and note the 56 count
  seen elsewhere belongs to the Knob-A rungs on `knob-a-rungs`, not this branch).
- **MMTk default repo** is `udesou/ocaml-mmtk`; the shipped configs override to
  `fplaunchpad`. README and CLAUDE.md previously disagreed about this.
- **`benches/macrobenchmarks/` no longer exists** — real-world tools moved to
  `~/macro-benches`.
- Dropped references to `experiments/mmtk_minheap.yml` and `mmtk_minheap_result.yml`,
  which live only on the unmerged `mmtk-minheap` branch.

## Code fixes, so the documented entry points actually run

Writing an honest quick start meant fixing what it pointed at:

- **`examples/ocaml_gc_sweep_example.yml` is the `CONFIG_FILE` default and failed
  to load.** `validate()` rejects runtimes declared but never referenced by a
  `configs:` entry, and it declared two. `bash run_ocaml_bench_gc_sweep.sh` with
  no `CONFIG_FILE` aborted before running anything.
- **`build_ocaml_binaries_gc_sweep.sh` defaulted to a path that moved** —
  `config/ocaml_gc_sweep_example.yml` instead of `config/examples/…`. Upstream
  already fixed the same stale path in `install_deps_linux.sh` (cdf0743); the
  build script was missed.

## CLAUDE.md

Now carries the operational detail: the build-script contract table, output-naming
grammar, binary-cache and `.build-failed` sentinel semantics, config-merge failure
modes, `minheap` output symbols, the three MMTk mechanisms with *why* each is
needed, and a **known-broken/inconsistent files** table (with what this PR fixes
removed from it).

One thing I deliberately did **not** change: `validate()`'s "declared but unused"
rule is stricter than the configs it inherited — it also rejects upstream's own
`runbms_example.yml`, and it rules out the commented-menu style those files were
written in. `resolve_class` already drops unreferenced runtimes, so it is hygiene
rather than correctness. That trade-off is written down in `CLAUDE.md` for a
separate decision, rather than changing validation behaviour inside a docs PR.

Plus one `### Fixed` line under `## [Unreleased]` summarizing the corrections (kept to a single bullet — other PRs also touch this section).
