items.title: chore: professionalize repository structure and documentation

labels.name: area: infrastructure
labels.description: CI, packaging, releases, and repository automation

items.body:
Closes #70.

**No behavior changed.** This is a documentation and structure pass. No runtime contract, capability, diagnostic, schema, public API, or test expectation was modified. The five touched `src/` files are pure additions inside module docstrings — the diff there is 71 insertions, 5 deletions, all inside `"""..."""`.

## 1. Documentation information architecture

`docs/` had grown organically with no index and two similarly named handoff files at its root.

- **Added `docs/README.md`** — an index that says what each document *owns*, with an "if you are new" routing table, plus a conventions section explaining what ADRs, ledgers, research docs, and handoffs each guarantee.
- **Moved the handoff documents into `docs/handoff/`**, renamed to say what they are: `HANDOFF.md` → `project-state.md`, `HANDOFF_CODEX.md` → `codex-onboarding.md`. Added `docs/handoff/README.md` with a table distinguishing them ("where does the project stand / what must never be broken?" vs. "I am the continuing agent — what do I do first?"). All five inbound links updated; verified by `git grep` and the new link checker.
- Fixed the stale codebase map in `project-state.md` (it claimed `docs/adr/` held ADR-0001…0026; it holds 0001…0065) and a broken ordered-list numbering in `codex-onboarding.md`.
- **`docs/research/README.md`**: three surveys were missing from the index (`freerouting-harness-owned-kicad-transaction.md`, `kicad-orthogonal-courtyard-topology.md`, `ne5532-audio-routing-fixture.md`). Added, in the index's existing "what it covers / what it refuses to claim" sentence form. Added a "how to read this directory" preamble stating that each document is a **dated snapshot of external evidence, not a maintained summary**, and that each carries its own date line.

## 2. README

Was 455 lines, ordered: status wall → why → 85 lines of capabilities → labs → research → 200 lines of CLI reference. A first-time visitor hit "how do I try it" at line 183.

Now ordered **what it is → why it exists → quick start → what it can do → what it does not claim → architecture → labs → research → docs**.

- The full CLI/MCP walkthrough moved to a new **`docs/usage.md`**, complete and linked. Nothing was dropped; every command, flag, and caveat carried over.
- **The honesty discipline is strengthened, not weakened.** The explicit non-claims were previously scattered inline across the capability bullets, where they were easy to skim past. They are now gathered into a single `## What CopperMCP does not claim` section, grouped by area (routing / placement / apply / schematics / evidence / scope), and linked from the status callout at the top. Every non-claim in the old README survives, including the leading one — that nothing has been routed by CopperMCP on a board that needed it.
- All relative links verified.

## 3. ADR hygiene

- **`docs/adr/README.md` was missing 16 of 64 records** — 0036–0047 and 0060–0063 were never indexed. It is now a table with every number, title, and **status**, which it previously did not carry at all.
- **ADR-0035 and ADR-0036 had no `Status` line at all.** Added `Status: Accepted`, confirmed against their `Accepted` decision-ledger rows (D-051, D-052). This is the one amendment ADRs explicitly permit after acceptance.
- **Numbering: one gap, no duplicates.** There is no ADR-0027. Rather than silently leave it, the index now carries a tombstone row explaining that the number is deliberately unused so an external reference to ADR-0027 resolves to nothing rather than to an unrelated decision.
- Added an "adding an ADR" section naming the next free number (0066) and the allocate-at-merge rule, and a thematic reading order, since the ADRs are chronological rather than grouped by arc.
- **No ADR was found to be superseded-in-fact but unmarked.** ADR-0035 ("keep the layered seam internal *until* board fidelity exists") is the closest call — ADR-0042 later made it public — but D-051 records that as a conditional whose conditions were met by a follow-on ADR, not a reversal. Declaring a supersession is a maintainer decision, so it is reported rather than made here; the index documents the convention instead.

## 4. Ledger ID hygiene

Audited all five ledgers. **Findings:**

| Ledger | Range | Gaps | Duplicates |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decision `D-` | 001–137 | `D-039` | none |
| Risk `R-` | 001–110 | none | none |
| Security `SEC-` | 001–113 | `SEC-021` | none |
| Benchmark `B-` | 001–076 | `B-006` | 9 IDs appear twice — all deliberate replay sub-entries |
| Release | versions | n/a | n/a |

`D-039`, `SEC-021`, `B-006` appear **nowhere in the repository** — genuinely never-allocated holes, not entries moved elsewhere.

**Root cause of the collision hazard in #70:** `scripts/check_ledgers.py` does not look at IDs at all. It checks that each ledger exists, contains its heading, and that benchmark artifacts match their self-digests. Gaps, duplicates, ordering, and format are entirely unchecked, so two branches both taking `D-137` would merge silently.

Added **`docs/ledgers/README.md` § Allocating IDs**: a prefix/next-free table, and five rules — allocate in the PR that lands the entry rather than in advance, never reuse a number (gaps are permanent, and why), corrections get a new ID, a benchmark replay reuses its parent's ID as a `####` sub-entry, three-digit zero padding. It states plainly that nothing enforces this automatically.

The benchmark ledger also carried **three mutually incompatible replay-naming conventions**; rule 4 settles on one. Existing entries are left untouched — they are append-only history.

## 5. Stale files

**Nothing was deleted.** A full sweep found no zero-byte files, no truncated docs, no scratch/backup/editor artifacts, and no orphaned fixtures. Every candidate that looked dead turned out to be load-bearing: the 17 "unreferenced" benchmark scripts each produce a committed, ledgered evidence artifact; the provenance JSONs are licence-compliance records; `hardware/coppertone-buffer/NOTICE.md` is required by CERN-OHL-S-2.0.

Two genuine index omissions were fixed rather than deleted (the three research docs above; `docs/github-setup.md` had zero inbound links and is now linked from `docs/README.md`).

Three findings reported but deliberately **not** acted on, since each needs a maintainer decision rather than a docs edit:

1. `schemas/drc-summary.schema.json` has **zero references repo-wide** — no loader, no test, no doc, untouched since PR #7. Its sibling schemas are cited from `docs/architecture/board-ir.md`. It publishes a public `$id` URL, so deleting it has external-contract implications; it should probably be cited or wired into a test instead.
2. `benchmarks/results/placement/2026-08-05-post-placement-observation-historical-b045.json` is **byte-identical** to `2026-08-05-post-placement-observation.json`, yet both are cited as separate ledger entries (B-045, B-052). Likely a bookkeeping error; both are immutable evidence, so untouched.
3. `docs/ledgers/risk-register.md` changes table schema mid-file — rows `R-046`…`R-110` have a 7th `Date` column with no new header or delimiter row, so under GFM they do not render as a table at all. `security-ledger.md` handles the same situation correctly. Fixing it means editing append-only rows, so it is reported instead.

## 6. Contributing and governance

Both were accurate but incomplete relative to how the project actually runs.

- **CONTRIBUTING.md**: added the per-target quality-gate table; the mypy version-skew warning; ledger and ADR ID allocation; branch protection's conversation-resolution requirement and the automated reviewer; a new **"Changes that write to a user's file"** section covering the mandatory adversarial review, the absolute safety property, and the rule that concurrency must be proven with genuine under-lock contention rather than a wall-clock timeout; and two domain invariants that were only in `AGENTS.md` (every claim bound to a test or declared a non-claim; the board's own text is untrusted data).
- Verified the existing dependency-light claim before keeping it: `python -m unittest discover -s tests` still passes, 406 tests.
- **GOVERNANCE.md**: added an append-only record section stating which properties the ledgers do and do not claim, a review section, and made explicit that release authorization is a `Ready` ledger row — no handoff or PR comment authorizes a release.

## 7. Documentation link check

Added **`scripts/check_doc_links.py`**, wired into `make lint` and CI. It verifies every relative Markdown link in tracked docs resolves to a real path, skipping fenced code blocks, and refuses root-relative and repo-escaping links. It deliberately does **not** fetch network URLs or validate heading anchors, and its docstring says so.

It found two real breaks on the pre-change tree, both in the benchmark ledger:
- B-036's dataset link omitted the `benchmarks/` path segment.
- B-057 linked to `docs/HANDOFF-CODEX.md`, a user-owned untracked file that has never existed in this repository.

Both **link targets** were corrected with displayed text unchanged, and the correction is recorded as append-only entry **B-076**. No run ID, digest, fixture name, metric, source commit, or interpretation changed.

`Documentation link check passed (140 Markdown files).`

## 8. Code readability

An AST audit of all 87 modules under `src/copper_mcp/` found the code hygiene already excellent: **100% module-docstring coverage**, **zero** `__all__` entries referencing undefined names, and `__all__` ordering 100% consistent under the codebase's constants-first convention. Nothing needed fixing.

The one inconsistency was stylistic: 48 of 53 multi-line docstrings state what the module *refuses*, but several boundary-critical modules had bare one-liners. Expanded five — `security.py`, `tools.py`, `models.py`, `routing/contracts.py`, `apply/contracts.py` — to state ownership and refusal, matching the dominant convention. Every claim in the new text was verified against the code.

**Deliberately left alone:** `mcp_contracts.py`'s `__all__` lists 31 tool types while the module defines ~130 public contract fragments, and three tests already import names outside it (`RouteDrcSummaryContract`, `InTotoDrcStatementContract`, `PlacementPreviewToolResponse`). Some limit constants are also absent from `apply/contracts.py`, `placement/contracts.py`, and `routing/congestion.py`. Editing `__all__` changes star-import behavior — that is a contract change, out of scope here, and reported for a follow-up.

## Gate

Full gate, run against this branch:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `ruff format` / `ruff check` | clean, 362 files |
| `mypy src` (strict) | Success: no issues found in 87 source files |
| **`pytest`** | **1496 passed, 1 skipped, 376 subtests** |
| `pytest` on `main` (baseline) | **1496 passed, 1 skipped, 376 subtests** |
| `check_version` | passed (0.5.0) |
| `check_ledgers` | passed |
| `check_doc_links` | passed (140 files) |
| `check_audio_benchmarks` | passed |
| `check_circuit_intents` | passed |
| `check_secrets` | passed |

Test counts are **identical to main's baseline**, as required for a docs-only change.

items.title: bench: machin vs Rust & Zig on build, size and evidence — and two stale claims corrected
items.body:
Answers "do we beat Rust and Zig at anything?" with numbers you can re-run — and
corrects two claims that were already shipping and were wrong.

## Two stale claims removed

**1. The integer-loop win did not exist.** `bench/native-speed` timed
language-by-language: all N machin samples, then all N Rust, then all N Zig. On a
laptop that down-clocks during a multi-second kernel, that penalizes whoever runs
last — always Zig. Interleaving the rounds and rotating the starting language
changed the headline:

```
intsum 10^9      before (blocked)     after (interleaved)
machin              2832 ms                3079.7 ms
rust                3764 ms                3223.8 ms
zig                 3556 ms                3189.7 ms
                 "machin +20-25%"        machin +3% = a TIE
```

That "~20-25%" was in the README **and inside `machin guide`**, which is what
every coding agent reads to learn the language. Corrected in both.

**2. The sieve loss had the wrong explanation.** The README blamed machin's
"slice indexing/layout" vs a Rust `Vec`. Phase timing disproves it:

| phase | machin | Rust |
|---|--:|--:|
| build the 10M array by `append` | 70–83 ms | 27–29 ms |
| **the sieve loop itself** | **110 ms** | **111 ms** |
| the count loop | 5–7 ms | 3 ms |

Indexing ties exactly. The whole gap is `append`: an arena frees nothing mid-life,
so `mfl_realloc` can only allocate fresh and memcpy, ~21 times, never releasing the
old buffers — where `Vec::push` extends in place via `mremap`.

I wrote the obvious fix (hand the arena's newest block straight to `realloc`) and
then **rejected it**: MFL slices share backing storage — `b := a` aliases, and so
does passing a slice to a function — so in-place growth turns every live alias into
a use-after-free. Filed as #578 with three directions that could be sound.

## Two new benchmarks

**`bench/compile-speed`** — build time and binary size. Results cut both ways:

- **Rust wins build time outright**: ~57 ms vs machin's ~95–116 ms. Invoked as bare
  `rustc`, not `cargo`, so the comparison can't be inflated in machin's favour.
- **machin wins size**: 14 kB vs 335 kB stripped, both dynamically linked — ~24×.
  Fully static, **Zig wins instead** (491 kB vs 940 kB).
- Zig's build-time column is reported but draws **no conclusion**: on this 0.16
  beta every `-OReleaseFast` build touching `std.debug.print` costs ~13 s and isn't
  reused between identical runs, while the same program in Debug costs 0.5 s and
  one that prints nothing costs 0.22 s.

**`bench/evidence`** — which toolchain tells you about the bug, and when. This is
the real differentiator, and it isn't speed:

| | deadlock | out-of-range index |
|---|---|---|
| **machin** | `DL001` at compile time; exit 2 at runtime with the wait-cycle | `FALS001` with a concrete failing input, before running |
| Rust | accepted silently → **hangs forever** | silent at build |
| Zig | accepted silently → **hangs forever** | silent at build |

Rust prevents *data races*; it has never claimed to prevent *deadlocks*, and that
`recv()` is idiomatic `unsafe`-free Rust.

That benchmark carries its own correction too. The first version compared machin
`--safe` against Zig `ReleaseFast` — machin's checked mode against Zig's unchecked
one — and made machin look safe by default. **It isn't.** machin's default build
printed a silent wrong `0` where Rust trapped (exit 101), the same class of
silent-wrong as Zig reading `281479271677952` out of adjacent memory. The table now
shows both modes for both languages and says plainly that Rust wins that row.

## Docs

`docs/BENCHMARKS.md` indexes all seven benchmarks with the losses as prominent as
the wins, linked from the README. Methodology section documents the ordering fix,
the 3% tie band, stripped-and-linkage size reporting, and one more harness bug
worth knowing about: exit codes were captured as `cmd | sed; echo $?`, which reads
`sed`'s status and silently recorded **failed Zig builds as successes**.

Full suite green — `ok machin 158.722s`.

items.title: Fix token budget accounting: measure full rendered output, not just code
items.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a critical token budget accounting bug where `--max-tokens` was systematically overshot by 25-41% on real repositories. The selector was budgeting on bare `symbol.code` length while the compiler rendered each symbol with `FILE:`/`FUNCTION:` headers and CALLERS/CALLEES relationship blocks, creating a measurement mismatch.

## Authorship disclosure

The changes in this PR were implemented by an AI coding agent (Claude, via Claude Code), working from an external audit's findings and task list, under the direction and review of the repository owner. Reviewers should apply the scrutiny appropriate to machine-generated changes. All claims in the diff are backed by tests or committed benchmark results rather than the agent's say-so; the before/after numbers were produced by executing the audit's repro commands, and `FIXES_SUMMARY.md` documents what was verified and what remains open.

## Key Changes

**Core fix (compiler & selector):**
- Extract per-symbol rendering into a shared `render_symbol_block()` function in `compiler.py` so both selector and compiler measure the same thing
- Add `relationship_cap()` helper to centralize the relationship-block cap logic (tighter under tight budgets)
- Add `build_reverse_graph()` helper to avoid duplication between compiler and selector
- Update `select_context()` to budget candidates at their full rendered size (with pessimistic `[NOT IN CONTEXT]` tags) when a call graph is provided
- Implement a post-render trim pass in `compile_context()` that enforces the budget against the final full output (meta + code sections + suggestions)
- Thread the call graph through `pipeline.py` to the selector

**Service hardening (security):**
- Add URL validation to `/clone` endpoint: reject hostnames resolving to private/loopback/link-local addresses before any git process runs
- Add post-clone size cap (default 500MB, configurable via `DIFFCONTEXT_MAX_CLONE_MB`)
- Add per-IP rate limiting on `/clone` (default 5 per 10 minutes, configurable)
- Document residual risks and deployment considerations in `diffcontext-service/README.md`

**Benchmark improvements:**
- Add `EmbeddingBaseline` class for dense-retrieval comparison (sentence-transformers when available, with explicit TF-IDF-cosine fallback for offline environments)
- Update `eval_v2_hardened.py` to include embedding baseline in the six-method comparison
- Record encoder type in results so dense and lexical runs cannot be conflated

**Documentation & testing:**
- Add `tests/test_token_budget.py`: regression tests verifying `--max-tokens` bounds the full output or is disclosed as a floor
- Add `tests/test_service_clone.py`: hardening tests for URL validation, size cap, and rate limiting
- Add `FIXES_SUMMARY.md`: audit remediation summary with before/after evidence
- Add `docs/ROADMAP_STATEFUL_HARNESS.md`: architecture for stateful, auditable context selection
- Add `docs/IMPLEMENTER_PROMPT.md`: scoped task for `diffcontext verify` command
- Add `docs/WRITING_TESTS_FOR_JUNIORS.md`: testing patterns for verification
- Update `README.md` to lead with precision figures alongside recall claims
- Update `CHANGELOG.md` with detailed fix description

## Notable Implementation Details

- The selector's pessimistic sizing (empty `selected_set` so every relationship entry carries the longer `[NOT IN CONTEXT]` tag) ensures candidates are never underestimated
- The post-render trim pass iterates to a fixed point when substituting the final token count into the output (stabilizes after 1-2 rounds)
- The documented exception: meta header and changed symbols are never dropped; when that floor alone exceeds budget, the output is the floor and the overshoot is visible in the meta's own token lines
- Service hardening includes DNS rebinding caveat: the check runs before clone but cannot pin the resolved IP for the actual connection (git doesn't expose this)
- Embedding baseline explicitly labels the TF-IDF fallback so offline benchmark runs don't get misrepresented as dense-retrieval results

## Post-merge correction

A reviewer caught numeric drift between `CHANGELOG.md` (black sweep 8000 → 7,269) and `FIXES_SUMMARY.md` (8000 → 7,329). Both were real measurements taken at different points in the pass: the changelog sweep predated the structural-ceiling disclosure line, which costs ~60 meta tokens at every budget. Commit `f9639b7` (follow-up PR from the same branch) corrects the changelog to the final numbers, pins the black SHA both documents measure against, and explains the delta instead of papering over it.

items.title: fix(#3947): stop sync-conformance fighting prettier, and name the real cause
items.body:
Fixes #3947.

Two defects in `scripts/sync-conformance-numbers.mjs`, plus the markdown-formatting class they exposed.

## 1. `--check` named a cause it had not established

It printed `DRIFT  CLAUDE.md`. Under a script called sync-conformance-**numbers** that reads as "your conformance number is stale". It was not — the difference was two blank lines. Measured cost of that wording: ~50 min of one agent, a wasted cycle for a second, and a third CI round-trip.

`--check` now computes an LCS line diff of the anchor block and classifies the failure:

```
[sync-conformance] DIFFERS  CLAUDE.md

[sync-conformance] CLAUDE.md: generated block differs — WHITESPACE/FORMATTING ONLY.
  The generated line is byte-identical, so nothing about the conformance figures
  has changed. (Usual cause: a markdown formatter reflowed the block. See #3947.)
[sync-conformance]     <!-- AUTO:conformance-start -->
[sync-conformance]   + (blank line)
[sync-conformance]     **test262 conformance**: 30,530 / 43,099 (70.8 %)
[sync-conformance]   + (blank line)
[sync-conformance]     <!-- AUTO:conformance-end -->
```

versus, with a genuinely stale figure:

```
[sync-conformance] CLAUDE.md: the generated line CHANGED — the committed value
  does not match benchmarks/results/test262-current.json.
[sync-conformance]   committed: **test262 conformance**: 29,999 / 43,099 (69.6 %)
[sync-conformance]   generated: **test262 conformance**: 30,530 / 43,099 (70.8 %)
```

Blank lines render as `(blank line)` on purpose — the whole failure was blank-line-only, which is invisible in a diff that prints an empty string.

## 2. prettier and the sync script mutually undid each other

`replaceAnchorBlock` emitted `<anchor>\n<body>\n<anchor>`; prettier's markdown formatter wants a blank line either side. It now emits that shape, which is **byte-identical** to prettier 3.8's output — the sync-written `CLAUDE.md` and the prettier-written one are the same git blob (`7ee35143c1b5a2`). Verified on all four targets including `README.md`'s two adjacent anchor pairs, the one shape that could have disagreed.

## 3. All markdown is `.prettierignore`d

`format:check` is `prettier --check 'src/**/*.ts' 'tests/**/*.ts' 'scripts/**/*.ts'` — zero markdown. So prettier has no authority over any `.md` file, and `prettier --write <doc>` rewrites the **whole** file rather than the part you edited. Measured on a clean tree:

| file | delta | nature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CLAUDE.md` (on main) | 2 +/0 − | the two blank lines — mutual undo |
| `CLAUDE.md` (post-merge) | 1 +/1 − | **list-continuation de-indent — damage** |
| `docs/ci-policy.md` | 5 +/6 − | 4 cosmetic `*em*`→`_em_`, **1 code-span corruption** |
| `README.md` | 17 +/12 − | tables realigned, `*em*`→`_em_` in prose |
| `ROADMAP.md` | 18 +/16 − | same |

`README.md` and `ROADMAP.md` were not previously recorded — same class. The `docs/ci-policy.md` corruption reproduced exactly: a backtick span adjacent to `**bold**` makes prettier mis-parse the emphasis run and delete the spaces between words.

**`CLAUDE.md` is included in the ignore, reversing a call made mid-branch.** It was originally excluded so the sync-vs-prettier agreement would be tested on the merits rather than passing because prettier could not see the file. That reason died on the merge: post-merge, `prettier --write CLAUDE.md` de-indents a list-item continuation, dropping the fenced code block after it out of the list item:

```diff
 - **Verify, don't trust the date.** Enforcement is a repo **ruleset**, not
   classic branch protection (the classic endpoint answers `404 Branch not
-  protected`):
+protected`):
```

Leaving that armed inside the PR whose subject is "stop prettier silently damaging ungated markdown" was not defensible. The `CLAUDE.md` row moving from 2 +/0 − to 1 +/1 − within one merge is the argument for a category rule over a remembered list.

The agreement stays **non-vacuously tested**, by a stronger detector: `tests/issue-3947.test.ts` asserts it via prettier's **programmatic** `format()` on a temp fixture, which does not consult `.prettierignore`. It isolates the anchor block from unrelated prose drift (exactly what began confounding the manual command), cannot be silenced by an ignore rule, and runs in CI on every PR.

## Correction: the prescribed remedy was never broken

The issue states `pnpm run sync:conformance` "rewrites the *number*, not the whitespace, so it reports a drift it cannot repair." **That is false, and was false before this PR.** Measured on `origin/main`:

```
$ npx prettier --write CLAUDE.md   # re-adds the two blank lines
$ node scripts/sync-conformance-numbers.mjs
[sync-conformance] wrote  CLAUDE.md
$ node scripts/sync-conformance-numbers.mjs --check ; echo $?
0
```

`processFile` rewrites the **entire** anchor block, so it normalised whitespace and value together all along. The lost time was the wording plus the undo *loop* — run the remedy, reflexively run `prettier --write` again, and the block comes straight back, which reads indistinguishably from "the remedy did nothing." Fix 2 kills the loop; fix 1 makes the remaining failure self-explanatory. Nothing in the repo auto-formats markdown (`.husky/post-merge` and `lint-staged` both filter to `.ts/.js/.mjs`), so those prettier runs were hand-run.

## Verification

- `prettier --write CLAUDE.md` → `md5sum` identical before/after; `sync:conformance:check` exit **0**. Taken while `CLAUDE.md` was still prettier-visible, so it is on the merits.
- `prettier --write docs/ci-policy.md` → `git diff --numstat` **empty**.
- **Positive control**: number hand-edited to `29,999` → `--check` exits **1** and the message names both values.
- Remedy repairs **both** modes: broken → `--check` 1 → `sync:conformance` → `--check` **0**, for the stale-number and the whitespace-only case.
- **Mutation check**: reverting `\n\n` to `\n` in `replaceAnchorBlock` fails **4 of the 7** tests. The suite is a detector, not a rubber stamp.
- Gates run locally past the fail-fast point: `format:check`, `lint`, `tsc --noEmit`, `check:issue-ids:against-main`, `generate:feature-badges:check`, `check:done-status-integrity`, `check:issue-spec-coverage`, `check:test-vacuity-shapes` — all green.
- `main` merged cleanly, including the 67-line move in `docs/ci-policy.md`.

## Known one-time cost

`promote-baseline` writes the new block shape on `main` once this lands, so a PR open across the merge hits a one-line conflict per anchor block. Resolve by taking either side and re-running `pnpm run sync:conformance`.

items.title: fix: correct 01_inference_profiling results after re-running every benchmark
items.body:
## Summary

Verified every number in this repo by actually running the underlying scripts (per request), not just reading the docs. Full pass covered all of 01-04; two of the four `01_inference_profiling` benchmarks didn't hold up:

- **`benchmark_cpu_vs_gpu.py`**: six fresh runs ranged **1.05s–7.39s** (mean ~3.07s) on the same hardware and code — a 7x spread. The documented 2.17s sits within that range near the median, so it wasn't wrong, but presenting it alone implied a precision this benchmark doesn't have on this CPU. `RESULTS_cpu_vs_gpu.md` now reports the full spread.
- **`benchmark_batching_effects.py`**: the script itself was rewritten at some point (4 rotating prompts, tokens/sec metric, 2 runs/batch) but `RESULTS_batch_size.md` still documented an older version's methodology and output format entirely — not just stale numbers, a stale script description. Rewrote to match current behavior.
- **`benchmark_kv_cache_analysis.py`** (the big one): documented **48.1x speedup** does not reproduce — four fresh runs measured **0.6x–1.2x**, i.e., no consistent cache benefit at all, one run even showing next-token latency *slower*. Root cause: `measure_next_token_latency()` calls independent `generate(max_new_tokens=1)` invocations in a loop; HF's KV cache is scoped to a single `generate()` call, so nothing is actually persisted across the measured iterations. This is a real methodology gap, not noise — the script likely never isolated the effect it claims to measure. Rewrote to lead with this, kept the original numbers in a clearly-labeled Historical Record section for audit purposes, and listed what a correct version would need.

Propagated the corrections everywhere these specific numbers were cited: `01_inference_profiling/README.md`, the top-level README's `01` section + Roadmap, and three `05_system_diagrams` files that had baked the same figures into diagrams built in an earlier PR (`inference_pipeline.md`'s timing annotations were removed rather than left showing a number that doesn't reproduce; the general KV-cache mechanism itself is kept since it's real, well-documented knowledge independent of whether this repo's benchmark demonstrates it).

**Confirmed accurate, no changes needed:** `benchmark_quantization_comparison.py` (within normal variance), all of `02_light_finetuning` (exact match on both perplexity numbers), all of `03_agentic_performance` (already fixed in #19), both `04_research_reproductions` notebooks (exact match, seeded).
